surveys.surface: Contextual control registry + recipe composition — the data architecture behind SystemSketch's floating appearance toolbar (the "pill"), its Block-title formatting menu, and the Contextual Menu Lab that drives the same objects

files.role: model — THE donor. Type vocabulary (kind/layout/trigger/glyph family), the 10 option vocabularies, CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY, 5 shipped recipes, bindContextualControl, composeContextualControls, and 4 pure selection predicates
test — pins registry key order, 'one thickness vocabulary', 'one Line shape vocabulary', recipe-only composition, empty-group dropping, and the Automatic-badge predicate regression
model — whole-menu (item-level) composition. ZERO imports of any kind; the most portable file in the survey
test — pins each surface's item order
model — THE one shared/mixed fold (sharedValueAcross, combineSharedStyles). One type-only tldraw import; otherwise pure
test — agreement, disagreement, abstention, empty-folds-to-undefined, custom equality tolerance, fold-of-folds
renderer — 20 lines: maps a surface id to an ordered list of caller-supplied ReactNode slots. Already host-agnostic React
model — the lever board's pure model. ZERO engine imports; its ONLY import is the registry itself (lines 34-47)
test — proves the lab composes with the product's own machinery, and that no preset may drift from the recipe it names
renderer/glue — the lever UI. Mounts a real <Tldraw> and re-parents popovers; the single most engine-coupled file in the survey
css — lab board styling only (not the menu's own)
renderer (adjacent, the consumer of every object above) — the one renderer for every registered control across every surface
renderer (adjacent) — GLYPH_FAMILIES lookup table; where the registry's `glyph` field is actually dispatched
glue (adjacent) — builds the CANDIDATES the recipe filters; owns modeControl stacking and restructureForV1Cluster
glue (adjacent) — the product binding site: picks a recipe, binds every candidate to the live editor
glue (adjacent) — second product consumer; binds BLOCK_TITLE_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE to a title, NOT to a selection

anatomy.description: The whole composed menu: a flex row of groups, one `<span class="systemsketch-appearance__separator">` drawn at every groupIndex > 0. Carries `data-contextual-recipe={composition.id}` so a test can assert WHICH recipe rendered.

One `<div class="systemsketch-contextual-controls__group" data-contextual-group={group.id}>` per surviving recipe group. Groups with zero surviving controls are never emitted, so a separator can never hang over an empty gap.

The clickable face of one control. Four shapes, chosen by the registry's `trigger` field, never by a per-kind conditional: `toggle` (a bare pressed button, the Bold B), `action` (icon button, fires onSelect immediately, no popover), `value`/`icon`/`text` (a popover trigger showing the current value's glyph, its text, or an icon) + a chevron. Wears an 'A' badge when isAutomaticContextualSelection is true.

The popover body. Reads `data-layout={control.layout}` (swatches | row | chips | list | library) and `data-mode={control.modePlacement}`. Above-stacked modes render as a vertical chain of sections outermost-last; a `beside` mode renders as one sibling group with a divider.
One option cell. Its preview comes from AppearanceGlyph, which dispatches on the registry's `glyph` family. A `list` layout gets a check mark and a text label; a `row` layout is icons only.
FigJam's 22nd swatch — only rendered for a control whose definition sets `custom: true` (today: `color` and `strokeColor`).

The live px entry row at the bottom of a Font size list. Rendered ONLY when the binding supplied a `customSize: ContextualCustomSize` — a surface bound to an explicit target (Block title) gets presets-only instead of a dead cell.
The value preview. `GLYPH_FAMILIES[control.glyph]` is a Record lookup — a table, not an if-chain.

The whole-menu composer, one level ABOVE controls: maps a ContextualSurfaceId to an ordered list of caller-supplied item slots (block-actions, appearance, opacity, arrange, wrap, layout, …). 20 lines, no engine.

The lever board: one row per registered kind with checkbox (include), four selects (layout, trigger, stack, value), a 'new group' checkbox and up/down reorder arrows. Right pane shows the REAL composed menu, the composed group ids, the control order, a dangling-control warning, the recipe literal as source text, and a rolling log of the last 8 writes.

surveys.dataModel:
FIVE exported types carry the whole architecture, all in /home/bam/systemsketch/src/contextualMenus/contextualControlRegistry.ts.

(1) `ContextualControlKind` (:8-24) — a CLOSED union of 16 strings: geo, color, fill, lineStyle, strokeColor, strokeWidth, codeLanguage, size, font, align, verticalAlign, lineShape, arrowheadStart, arrowheadEnd, bold, addText. `AppearanceControlId = Exclude<ContextualControlKind, 'bold' | 'addText'>` (:26) is the implicit split between style controls and commands. Three orthogonal presentation axes are separate unions: `ContextualControlLayout = 'swatches'|'row'|'chips'|'list'|'library'` (:27), `ContextualControlTrigger = 'value'|'icon'|'text'|'toggle'|'action'` (:28), `ContextualGlyphFamily` (:41-53, 12 members).

(2) `ContextualControlDefinition` (:60-71) — THE VOCABULARY ENTRY. `{ kind, label, options: readonly {value,label}[], layout, trigger, glyph?, columns?, custom?, meta? }`. Pure data. No value, no callback, no target. `CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY: Readonly<Record<ContextualControlKind, ContextualControlDefinition>>` (:260-309) is the single table; its doc comment states the law: "One vocabulary for every contextual control. Surfaces bind values and commands; they do not re-declare labels, options, previews, or layouts." (:256-259)

(3) `ContextualControl extends ContextualControlDefinition` (:96-116) — THE BOUND CONTROL. Adds `id: string` (stable DOM/test hook, distinct from `kind`), `value: SharedStyle<string> | null`, `onSelect(value?, {continuous?})`, plus five optional bindings: `automaticOption`, `customColorOpacity`, `customSize?: ContextualCustomSize`, `rungPx?(value): number|null`, and the stacking pair `modeControl?: ContextualControl` / `modePlacement?: 'above'|'beside'`. Note `modeControl` is itself a ContextualControl — the stack is a linked list, not a flat field.

(4) `ContextualCustomSize` (:84-94) — a four-method port for a size list's continuous channel: `sharedPx(): number|'mixed'|null`, `onPresetRungs(): boolean`, `applyPx(px): void`, `minPx`, `maxPx`. Its absence is meaningful: no binding ⇒ presets-only, no Custom row.

(5) `ContextualControlRecipe` (:128-134) = `{ id, groups: readonly { id, items: readonly ContextualControlKind[] }[] }` — a pure list of KINDS, no values, no bindings, no JSX. Its output `ContextualControlComposition` (:123-126) = `{ id, groups: readonly ContextualControlGroup[] }`, `ContextualControlGroup` (:118-121) = `{ id, controls: readonly ContextualControl[] }`.

Shipped recipe literals: SHAPE_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE (:311-326), CONNECTOR_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE (:332-344), BLOCK_TITLE_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE (:346-354), V1_COMPACT_RECIPE (:375-385), V3_SEGMENTED_RECIPE (:403-409).

SECOND, coarser registry — /home/bam/systemsketch/src/contextualMenus/contextualSurfaceRegistry.ts: `ContextualSurfaceId` (:1-7, 6 members) → `readonly ContextualSurfaceItemId[]` (:9-21, 12 members) via `CONTEXTUAL_SURFACE_REGISTRY` (:33-50). Same idea one level up: which ITEMS (appearance pill, opacity, arrange, wrap, layout, …) a whole menu carries, in what order.

Value model — /home/bam/systemsketch/src/contextualMenus/sharedValues.ts: everything reads through tldraw's `SharedStyle<T>`, which is a five-line discriminated union (`{type:'mixed'} | {type:'shared', value:T}`, /home/bam/systemsketch/node_modules/@tldraw/editor/dist-cjs/index.d.ts:7220-7225). `sharedValueAcross` (:19-35) folds raw readings; `combineSharedStyles` (:38-46) folds already-folded verdicts.

Lab model — /home/bam/systemsketch/src/prototypes/menuLab/menuLabModel.ts: `LabControlState` (:65-75) = `{ kind, included, layout, trigger, stack: 'none'|'above'|'beside', value: 'first'|'second'|'mixed', breakBefore }`, `LabState` (:77-80) = `{ popoverMode, controls }`. `LabPreset` (:107-112) and `LabPresetDrift` (:207-212).

engineCoupling.what: `import { FIGJAM_COLOR_NAMES, FIGJAM_PALETTE_COLUMNS } from '../appearance/figjamPalette'` — a RUNTIME value import used to compute the color and strokeColor option lists (:264, :278) and their `columns` (:266, :279). figjamPalette.ts imports `DEFAULT_THEME` from 'tldraw' as a value (:23) and does `declare module '@tldraw/tlschema'` (:25-37), so importing the registry pulls the whole tldraw theme module into the bundle. The palette is also SystemSketch product taste (21 FigJam colours), not a generic menu concern.

`import { isCustomColor } from '../appearance/customColors'`, called at :456 inside `selectedContextualOption` and hardcoded to two kinds (`control.kind === 'color' || control.kind === 'strokeColor'`). The predicate itself is a pure regex (`customColors.ts:31-33`, `/^custom-([0-9a-f]{6})$/` at :26), but customColors.ts imports `DefaultColorStyle, registerColorsFromThemes, type Editor` from 'tldraw' (:20) and FIGJAM_THEME (:22).

`import { ASYNC_LINE_VALUE, type StrokeMetaField } from '../appearance/strokeMeta'`. ASYNC_LINE_VALUE is the string 'async' (strokeMeta.ts:50), used once in DASH_OPTIONS (:165); StrokeMetaField is `'color'|'pattern'|'width'` (strokeMeta.ts:103), surfacing as the definition's `meta?` field (:69-70). strokeMeta.ts imports tldraw VALUES (DefaultColorStyle, DefaultDashStyle — strokeMeta.ts:33-42) and `../store/looseShapeUpdates` (:44). The `meta` tag is also a tldraw-shape-metadata concept leaking into a presentation vocabulary: it exists only so the BINDING site can branch on how to write the value (AppearanceControls.tsx:203-210).

`import { CODE_LANGUAGES, CODE_LANGUAGE_LABELS } from '../code/codeModel'`, used to compute CODE_LANGUAGE_OPTIONS (:231). The data itself is a plain array + Record (codeModel.ts:6-30) but codeModel.ts:1 imports `DefaultSizeStyle, StyleProp, T, type TLShape` from 'tldraw'.
`import type { SharedStyle } from 'tldraw'` — TYPE-ONLY, erased at build. The type is a five-line discriminated union (@tldraw/editor/dist-cjs/index.d.ts:7220-7225). Copy it and the coupling is gone.
Same type-only `SharedStyle` import. The entire rest of the file (sharedValueAcross :19-35, combineSharedStyles :38-46) is a pure generic fold with no runtime dependency at all.
NO coupling to report — the file has zero import statements. Only its VOCABULARY is SystemSketch-specific (ids like 'branch-selection', 'behavior-tree-selection', 'propagation-focus').

NO engine coupling — its only import is the registry itself. Every exported function (labRecipe, labCandidates, labDangling, labComposition, labRecipeSource, setLabControl, moveLabControl, labPresetDrift) is pure. 388 lines that port as-is once the registry does.

`getAssetUrlsByImport` from '@tldraw/assets/imports.vite'; `ContainerProvider, Tldraw, useContainer, useEditor` from 'tldraw'; `import 'tldraw/tldraw.css'`. The lab route mounts a whole canvas engine.

Mounts a real `<Tldraw hideUi components={{Background:null}} onMount={editor => editor.updateInstanceState({isReadonly:true})}>` purely to supply the renderer an editor and tldraw's popover primitive. Its own comment (:59-63) says this is deliberate: 'the renderer reads swatch colours off the live theme and opens tldraw's own popover primitive. A lab that mocked either would stop reproducing product bugs, which is the only reason to have one.'

DOM traversal + z-index workaround: `node?.closest<HTMLElement>('.tlui-dialog__positioner')` (:103) re-parents popovers via ContainerProvider because 'tldraw stacks its popover layer at z-index 400 and its dialog layer at 500 (measured), so a contextual popover opened from inside Settings renders *behind* the dialog that hosts it'. Pure host/z-order concern — exactly what the trunk's law says must never travel.
`editor.getInstanceState().isReadonly` printed as a hint line. A readout only; delete or pass in as a string prop.

The renderer that consumes every object surveyed here imports `@radix-ui/react-popover` AND `TldrawUiPopover, TldrawUiPopoverContent, TldrawUiPopoverTrigger, useContainer, useEditor, useValue, type Editor` from 'tldraw'. `popoverMode: 'selection'|'editing'` (:43) literally selects between the two popover implementations (ContextualPopover :514-547 uses tldraw's; EditingPopover :546-573 uses Radix portaled into `useContainer()`).

Seven `useEditor()` / `useValue()` reactive reads. Every live value the panel shows (custom px, rung px, on-preset-rungs, registered hex) is read through tldraw's signal system rather than through props. The DATA layer is clean — the registry's own WHY (:73-83) forbids the renderer reaching for the selection — but the renderer still holds an Editor to pass DOWN to glyphs and to the customSize binding's reads.
`onPointerDown={editor.markEventAsHandled}` on the Radix popover content — host interaction plumbing so a live canvas text editor stays open while the menu is used.

`GlyphFamilyRenderer.render(value: string|undefined, editor: Editor)` — the glyph contract takes an Editor. Only the `swatch` family actually needs it (ColorSwatch reads the live theme for a colour name's hex); every other family ignores it.

The product binding site. `bindAppearanceControl(editor, control)` closes over the editor for onSelect (applyLineShape / applyLinePattern / applyStrokeMeta / applyStrokeWidth / applyStyle, :202-211) and for customSize/rungPx (:183-200). This is NOT a defect — it is the seam working as designed: all of it already lives on the far side of `bindContextualControl`, which is why the data layer stayed clean.

`usePillPresentation()` (a global/persisted store that remembers a Pill-lab layout choice) selects which recipe renders — `presentation.compare ? presentation.layout : 'v3'`. A host-owned preference reaching into composition. The WHY at :99-102 is explicit that the gate exists so a stale lab setting cannot change the shipped pill.

`restructureForV1Cluster` mutates the CANDIDATE list (un-stacking color→fill and strokeColor→lineStyle→strokeWidth into top-level controls, folding arrowheadEnd into arrowheadStart) as a precondition of V1_COMPACT_RECIPE. Recipe and candidate-shape are coupled by convention only — nothing in the type system says V1_COMPACT_RECIPE requires restructured candidates.

reusableAsIs: composeContextualControls — /home/bam/systemsketch/src/contextualMenus/contextualControlRegistry.ts:424-439. THE resolver, 16 lines, zero imports touched: build `new Map(candidates.map(c => [c.kind, c]))`, then `recipe.groups.flatMap(...)` pulling each named kind out of the map. Two behaviours fall out of the flatMaps and both are load-bearing: a candidate whose kind the recipe does not name is SILENTLY DROPPED, and a group that ends up with zero controls is NOT EMITTED (which is what stops the renderer's `groupIndex > 0` separator from hanging over a gap). Pinned by contextualControlRegistry.test.ts:68-75. Ports verbatim.

bindContextualControl — .../contextualControlRegistry.ts:411-421. Nine lines: `{ ...CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY[kind], ...binding, kind }`. The trailing `kind` re-pin is deliberate — a binding can never overwrite the identity it was looked up by. Its parameter type is itself the whole contract: `Pick<ContextualControl,'id'|'value'|'onSelect'> & Partial<Pick<ContextualControl,'automaticOption'|'customColorOpacity'|'customSize'|'rungPx'|'modeControl'|'modePlacement'>>` — three required, six optional, and nothing else a surface may say. Ports verbatim.
contextualControlIds — :441-443. Two lines, pure. Used by every test and by the lab's readout.

isAutomaticContextualSelection — :473-477, WITH its five-line WHY at :462-472. Pure. Guards a real shipped bug: `control.automaticOption?.value === current?.value` is `undefined === undefined` → true for every control with no Automatic concept the moment its value went mixed, which painted an 'A' badge on Color and Line style for every disagreeing selection. Pinned twice (contextualControlRegistry.test.ts:102-128).

contextualTriggerLabel — :479-491. Pure string builder; the only place a stacked control's label leaks into the host's trigger text (`'${stacked} ${own}'`, :489), and only for `trigger === 'icon' && modePlacement === 'above'`.

selectedContextualOption — :448-460. Pure APART from the one `isCustomColor(value)` call at :456 and its hardcoded `kind === 'color' || kind === 'strokeColor'` test. Port the 12 lines, make the custom-value escape hatch a per-control injection.

sharedValueAcross + combineSharedStyles — /home/bam/systemsketch/src/contextualMenus/sharedValues.ts:19-35 and :38-46. 28 lines total, generic over T, optional equality comparator (used for a 0.01px font tolerance — sharedValues.test.ts:28-35). `undefined` readings mean 'this subject abstains' and are skipped, never counted as disagreement; an all-abstain set folds to `undefined`, never a fabricated value. Only the SharedStyle type import stands between this file and total portability.
contextualSurfaceRegistry.ts in full — :1-54. ZERO imports. A Record of surface id → ordered item ids plus a one-line accessor. Only the id vocabulary is SystemSketch-specific.

All ten option vocabularies — .../contextualControlRegistry.ts:146-254 (FILL 146-151, DASH 160-167, SIZE 169-174, STROKE_WIDTH 182-186, FONT 188-193, ALIGN 195-199, VERTICAL_ALIGN 201-205, LINE_SHAPE 213-217, ARROWHEAD 219-229, GEO 233-254). Plain `as const` literals built by the 1-line `option()` helper (:136). Only two cells are impure: DASH_OPTIONS:165 references ASYNC_LINE_VALUE and CODE_LANGUAGE_OPTIONS:231 maps the code-language import.

menuLabModel.ts ENTIRE MODEL — /home/bam/systemsketch/src/prototypes/menuLab/menuLabModel.ts:49-388. labRecipe :245-255, labValue :257-265, bindLabControl :274-288, labCandidates :295-314, labDangling :325-335, labComposition :337-342, labRecipeSource :345-351, setLabControl :353-364, moveLabControl :373-388, labPresetDrift :222-242, LAB_PRESETS :129-183, LAB_PRESET_RECIPES :200-205. All pure functions over plain objects; the module's only import is the registry. 388 lines that need no re-expression at all once the registry ports.

stackedModes — /home/bam/systemsketch/src/contextualMenus/ContextualControls.tsx:240-249, with its WHY at :233-239. Ten-line pure walk up the `modeControl` chain, unshifting so the outermost section renders last. Not engine-coupled despite living in the renderer.

All four test files — contextualControlRegistry.test.ts (129), contextualSurfaceRegistry.test.ts (33), sharedValues.test.ts (53), menuLabModel.test.ts (172). Plain vitest + vi.fn(), NO editor, NO DOM, NO tldraw import anywhere in any of them. 387 lines of acceptance that can be committed into the trunk BEFORE any porting work starts.
mustBeReExpressed: `SharedStyle<string>` must become a locally-defined value type (e.g. `ControlValue<T> = {type:'mixed'} | {type:'shared', value:T}`). It is the type of EVERY control's `value` (registry.ts:99) and the return of both folds (sharedValues.ts:22, :41), so it is the single most load-bearing borrowed type in the surface — and the cheapest to replace (5 lines).

The COLOR PALETTE must be injected, not imported. `color.options` (registry.ts:264) and `strokeColor.options` (:278) are computed at module load from FIGJAM_COLOR_NAMES, and `columns` (:266, :279) from FIGJAM_PALETTE_COLUMNS. A host-agnostic kit cannot ship FigJam's 21 colours as the vocabulary; the registry must take a palette (names + column count) as construction input — which means CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY stops being a module-level `const` and becomes a factory.
Same for `codeLanguage.options` (registry.ts:231, from CODE_LANGUAGES) — a domain vocabulary that belongs to the app, not the kit.

`meta?: StrokeMetaField` (registry.ts:69-70) is a tldraw-shape-metadata concept sitting in a presentation vocabulary. It is read ONLY by the binding site to branch on how to write (AppearanceControls.tsx:205-209) and by one test (:38). Either drop it from the definition and let the host carry its own tag, or make it an opaque `hostTag?: string`.

`ContextualCustomSize` (registry.ts:84-94) is already a correctly-shaped port — but all four of its members are read through tldraw's `useValue` at the call sites (ContextualControls.tsx:176-200, :271-278, :465). The trunk has no signal system: these have to become plain values recomputed by the host per render, or a `useSyncExternalStore`-shaped subscription the host supplies. Same for `rungPx` (registry.ts:105-113, read at ContextualControls.tsx:194, :360).

The glyph contract `render(value, editor)` (AppearanceGlyph.tsx:44-51) must lose its Editor. Only the `swatch` family needs it (to resolve a colour NAME to a hex off the live theme, :65). Re-express as an injected `resolveSwatchHex(name) => string` prop, or have the palette carry hexes so no resolver is needed at all.

`popoverMode: 'selection' | 'editing'` (ContextualControls.tsx:43) is not a design concept — it names WHICH popover implementation to mount (tldraw's TldrawUiPopover at :514-547 vs Radix at :546-573). In the trunk this must become a host-supplied popover slot/render-prop; the composed menu should not know either library exists.

The custom-value escape hatch in `selectedContextualOption` (registry.ts:456) hardcodes `kind === 'color' || kind === 'strokeColor'` and calls `isCustomColor`. Re-express as an optional per-control predicate/labeller on the definition or binding, so a new control type with a free-form value needs no edit here.

The `ContextualSurfaceId` / `ContextualSurfaceItemId` vocabularies (contextualSurfaceRegistry.ts:1-21) are entirely SystemSketch domain nouns (branch, behavior-tree, block, propagation-focus, code-actions). The MECHANISM is generic and ports as-is; the two unions must become host-supplied type parameters.

`restructureForV1Cluster`'s implicit contract (appearanceModel.ts:434-458) — V1_COMPACT_RECIPE only composes correctly against restructured candidates, and nothing in the types says so. The registry's own WHY at :356-374 records that a first pass here silently lost `lineShape` for every connector selection and was caught only by selecting a real connector fixture. In the trunk this precondition must be expressed, not commented.

The stacked-mode chain (`modeControl`/`modePlacement`, registry.ts:114-115) is built by three separate ad-hoc sites in appearanceModel.ts (:151-152 dash→lineStyle, :172-173 lineStyle→strokeWidth 'above', :194-195 strokeWidth 'beside') and again in the lab (menuLabModel.ts:295-314). The lab's version is the general one — a single fold that stacks each marked control onto the next included one. That fold is what should travel; the three product sites are ad-hoc layout code.
`LabState.popoverMode` (menuLabModel.ts:78) is the only field of the otherwise-pure lab model that names an engine concern; it must follow whatever the popover slot above becomes.

The lab's popover re-parenting (`node.closest('.tlui-dialog__positioner')`, ContextualMenuLab.tsx:102-104) and the whole `<Tldraw>` wrapper (:64-71) do not port at all — they are the host's z-order and portal problem, which the trunk's law explicitly refuses.
openQuestions: Is `ContextualControlKind` still a CLOSED 16-member union in the trunk? Closing it is what makes `Record<Kind, Definition>` exhaustive, what makes `composeContextualControls`'s Map lookup total, and what the first test asserts key-by-key (contextualControlRegistry.test.ts:17-25). But those 16 names are SystemSketch's shape-drawing concepts (geo, arrowheadStart, codeLanguage) — a generic kit probably wants an open registry keyed by string with the closed union living in the app. That choice cascades into every signature here.

Module-level `const` singletons vs a factory. CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY (registry.ts:260) is a frozen module constant, which is exactly why palette/language injection is currently impossible. Deciding factory-vs-constant is the first fork of the port and changes all five recipe literals too.

Reactivity model. Every live read in the current renderer goes through tldraw's `useValue` (7 sites, ContextualControls.tsx:62-465). The trunk has no signal library. Does the port take plain props the host recomputes, or a subscription-shaped binding? `ContextualCustomSize` (registry.ts:84-94) is the one place this is a real design question rather than mechanical.

Does the menuLab port as a Storybook STORY? Its levers are literally a variant gallery over the same objects, and the workflow note says variant galleries in one story are the deliverable. `labRecipeSource` (menuLabModel.ts:345-351), which prints the recipe literal you just composed, is a strong argument for it — but the standalone `?menu-lab` route and the Settings-embedded panel (ContextualMenuLab.tsx:9-13) are two entry points and only one survives.

Glyphs. Does the trunk ship the vendored icon sets (appearance/excalidrawIcons/, appearance/figjamIcons.ts, appearance/tldrawGeoIcons.tsx — reached from AppearanceGlyph.tsx:101-177) or take a `glyphs: Partial<Record<Family, Record<value, ReactNode>>>` prop map? The three-layer precedence the current code implements (ownDrawing → Excalidraw vendored → FigJam traced → own drawn, AppearanceGlyph.tsx:207-230) is real behaviour that must be decided, not inherited. Licensing of the vendored Excalidraw icons was not examined in this survey.

`ContextualSurface.tsx` is 20 lines of caller-supplied ReactNode slots (:10-20) and already host-agnostic. Is the whole-menu layer in scope for this port, or only the control layer? It is the piece that most directly answers 'use them in any host', and it is nearly free.

The V1/V3 recipes (registry.ts:375-409) are LAB VARIANTS that got shipped (V3 is the current default — AppearanceControls.tsx:99-103, 'Zach: please set v3 to the default'). Do they travel as part of the kit's vocabulary, or are they app-level configuration the kit should never know about?

`AppearanceControlId = Exclude<Kind,'bold'|'addText'>` (registry.ts:26) encodes a style-control/command split by subtraction. The trunk probably wants that split stated positively (a `commands` vs `styles` discriminant), but doing so changes `recipeOrder`'s filter (appearanceModel.ts:256-260) and the `trigger: 'toggle'|'action'` branches in the renderer (ContextualControls.tsx:96-145).

surveys.surface: Contextual controls renderer + popover surfaces + floating-pill placement math + the rich-text/title formatting toolbar (SystemSketch `src/contextualMenus/`, `src/chrome/`, `src/appearance/`)

anatomy.description: Screenshot (a)'s dark rounded bar. `TldrawUiToolbar orientation="horizontal"` inside a positioned wrapper div. 40px min-height, 13px radius, inverse surface, `flex-wrap: wrap` (NOT overflow-x — a scroll container breaks tldraw's `usePassThroughWheelEvents`), `max-width: calc(max(160px, 100vw - 40px) / var(--systemsketch-interface-scale))`.

Maps a `ContextualControlComposition` to groups of triggers, drawing a 1px full-height hairline `.systemsketch-appearance__separator` between every group after the first (`groupIndex > 0`). Wraps at both levels (`.systemsketch-appearance` and `__group`).

anatomy.part: ControlTrigger (icon+chevron cell / swatch+chevron cell / text combobox cell)
anatomy.description: Screenshot (a)'s cells. `forwardRef` button spreading Radix's injected props. 40px tall; icon variant 56px (24px glyph butted to a 16px chevron, 8px each side); swatch variant 54px (18px disc in a 22px ring box); text variant `[data-trigger='text']` is a 144px combobox, name left at 11px, chevron right. Carries `data-control`, `data-kind`, `data-trigger`, `data-mixed`.
Identical filled 16x16 path on every trigger, from `CHEVRON_PATH`/`CHEVRON_VIEWBOX`. Re-declared (not imported) inside ArrangeTrigger so the two read as one family.

Screenshot (c)'s B. `control.trigger === 'toggle'` → 40px square button, literal `B`, `aria-pressed`, background `var(--ss-accent)` when pressed. Hard-coded glyph — the only control whose face is not registry data.

`control.trigger === 'action'` → chevron-less button whose face is registry data via `FIGJAM_TRIGGER_ICON[control.kind]` (today only `addText` → 'trigger/Add text'). Explicit WHY against per-kind conditionals.

Screenshot (c)'s "A v" cell — the Block-title Colour control whose shared value is its declared `automaticOption`. 24px monospace 800-weight "A"; gets an inset accent ring when it is the checked cell in a swatch grid.
Screenshot (c)'s "Large 36". Muted 11px tabular numeral after the rung name, from `control.rungPx(currentValue)` through `formatFontPx`. Suppressed when `customPx` is showing. WHY verbatim below.

Screenshot (b)'s floating surface. Column flex, 8px padding, same 13px radius and surface as the pill, three-layer shadow. `role="menu"`, `data-layout={control.layout}`, `data-mode={control.modePlacement}`.

anatomy.part: StackedModeSection (the Solid / Hatched / Transparent / No fill row)
anatomy.description: Screenshot (b)'s top row. A chain of `modeControl`s with `modePlacement: 'above'`, unshifted outermost-last by `stackedModes()`. Rendered as `.systemsketch-appearance__mode`: 32px row, bleeds -8px into the panel padding, ends in a full-width hairline, palette starts 12px below. The highlighted cell is `--systemsketch-pill-accent` (#9747ff, the CHIP purple) — distinct from the icon-cell purple.

The alternative `modePlacement: 'beside'` — a connector's thickness row beside its dash row, one full-height 1px rule between (`margin: -8px 0` so it cuts the panel's padding). Panel becomes `flex-direction: row`.

`role="menuitemradio"` + `aria-checked`. Five layouts off one component: `row` (24px cells, 8px gap), `chips` (labelled, 16px glyph in a 24px slot), `list` (24px rows, 16px check slot, label, right-aligned px), `library` (5-col grid, 268px max-height, scrolls), `swatches` (grid, `gridTemplateColumns: repeat(columns, 24px)` written inline from `control.columns`).

Screenshot (b)'s grid. 21 colours from `FIGJAM_PALETTE`, `columns: FIGJAM_PALETTE_COLUMNS` = 11, so 11 + 10 wrapping to a second row. 24px discs on a 32px pitch with a 20%-white inner hairline so white reads as a disc; chosen swatch gets `0 0 0 2px surface, 0 0 0 4px #8a38f5` (2px gap then 2px of the DEEPER purple); mixed gets a diagonal-slash gradient.

Screenshot (b)'s last cell. Its own nested `ContextualPopover` with `side="bottom"`. 32px box with `margin: -4px` so it overhangs its 32px-pitch slot; idle = conic wheel under a white radial highlight; active = the picked colour as the disc with the wheel reduced to a 2px border-box ring.

The `Custom [__] px` row under the Font-size presets. Local draft state resynced from `binding.sharedPx()`, commits on blur and Enter, reverts on unparseable input, `placeholder="Mixed"`. Deliberately reuses the Code-width popover's `.code-width-custom` CSS from another module so the ONE size menu keeps one visual language.

Screenshot (c)'s popover. `layout: 'list'` draws `FIGJAM_CHECK_ICON` ('menu/Check') in every row at `opacity: 0`, flipped to 1 on the checked row; each row's label is drawn at its own size from `FONT_SIZE_LADDER` (s:12 m:13 l:14 xl:16); checked row keeps the PANEL surface and ink (check alone, never a fill).

Screenshot (a)'s "100%" slider. Native `<input type=range>` min 0 max 100 step 10, 72px wide, `accent-color` = pill accent; visually-hidden label; 30px tabular-nums percent readout; mixed pins the thumb to 100 and prints "Mixed" at 0.6 opacity; `value === null` renders nothing. Own `border-left` sets it off as a segment.

Screenshot (a)'s align-icon+chevron cell. 32px-tall trigger whose face is Excalidraw's AlignLeftIcon; opens a `layout="stack"` panel of 33x32 grid buttons in up to four groups (z-order always; align at 2+; distribute at 3+) with a full-width 1px rule between groups and `aria-orientation` flipped to horizontal when stacked. Never auto-closes on click.
The `border-left` that sets Arrange off from Opacity lives on a wrapper div in the pill's row, NOT on the panel — because the buttons moved into a popover and the segment line had to stay behind.
20 lines: looks up an ordered item-id list for a surface id and renders the host's supplied ReactNode per slot, `?? null`. This is the "which sections, in what order" seam.

Same `ContextualControls` renderer with `popoverMode="editing"` (Radix) over `BLOCK_TITLE_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE`: type (font, size) | emphasis (bold) | ink (color) | alignment (align) — exactly "Aa v | Large 36 v | B | A v | align v". Its size rungs read `BLOCK_TITLE_FONT_PX` = {s:18, m:24, l:36, xl:44}, which is literally the "Small 18 / Medium 24 / Large 36 / Extra large 44" list in the screenshot.

tldraw's OWN `.tlui-rich-text__toolbar` — SystemSketch ships only a 55-line CSS reskin (inverse surface, 13px radius, 7px button radius, accent on `[data-isactive]`, focus-ring colour). There is no SystemSketch React component for it; grep for RichText/rich-text across src returns zero toolbar components. Its own WHY says this is deliberate.

A `position: fixed` bottom-left lab chip with two `<select>`s (Layout: default/V1 Excalidraw Compact/V3 Figma Segmented; Style: default + 5 skins), rendered only when `presentation.compare` is true. Needs `pointer-events: auto` to escape the host's `pointer-events: none`.

Three-layer glyph dispatch: registry `glyph` family → `GLYPH_FAMILIES` table (11 drawn renderers) with an `ownDrawing` escape; Excalidraw vendored icons OUTRANK FigJam traced icons; FigJam traced icons outrank the drawn fallbacks. Wide traced icons (typeface wordmarks) keep their own aspect via `data-natural`; arrowheads mirror via `data-flipped`.

surveys.dataModel:
Everything the renderer draws comes from ONE file: `src/contextualMenus/contextualControlRegistry.ts`.

TYPES (all exported from that file):
- `ContextualControlKind` (:8-25) — 16-member union: geo | color | fill | lineStyle | strokeColor | strokeWidth | codeLanguage | size | font | align | verticalAlign | lineShape | arrowheadStart | arrowheadEnd | bold | addText.
- `AppearanceControlId` = Exclude<ContextualControlKind, 'bold' | 'addText'> (:26).
- `ContextualControlLayout` = 'swatches' | 'row' | 'chips' | 'list' | 'library' (:27).
- `ContextualControlTrigger` = 'value' | 'icon' | 'text' | 'toggle' | 'action' (:28).
- `ContextualGlyphFamily` (:41-53) — 12-member union naming the PREVIEW family, deliberately separate from `kind`.
- `ContextualControlOption` = { value: string; label: string } (:55-58).
- `ContextualControlDefinition` (:60-71) = { kind, label, options, layout, trigger, glyph?, columns?, custom?, meta? }.
- `ContextualCustomSize` (:84-94) = { sharedPx(): number|'mixed'|null; onPresetRungs(): boolean; applyPx(px): void; minPx; maxPx }.
- `ContextualControl extends ContextualControlDefinition` (:96-116) adds: `id`, `value: SharedStyle<string> | null`, `onSelect(value?, {continuous?})`, `automaticOption?`, `customColorOpacity?`, `customSize?`, `rungPx?(value): number|null`, `modeControl?: ContextualControl` (recursive), `modePlacement?: 'above'|'beside'`.
- `ContextualControlGroup` / `ContextualControlComposition` (:118-126) — { id, controls } / { id, groups }.
- `ContextualControlRecipe` (:128-134) — { id, groups: [{ id, items: ContextualControlKind[] }] }.

DATA:
- `CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY` (:260-309) — one `ContextualControlDefinition` per kind. THE vocabulary; surfaces bind values and commands and may not re-declare labels/options/previews.
- Five recipes: `SHAPE_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE` (:311), `CONNECTOR_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE` (:332), `BLOCK_TITLE_CONTEXTUAL_RECIPE` (:346), `V1_COMPACT_RECIPE` (:375), `V3_SEGMENTED_RECIPE` (:403).
- Option vocabularies: `FILL_OPTIONS` (:146), `DASH_OPTIONS` (:160), `SIZE_OPTIONS` (:169), `STROKE_WIDTH_OPTIONS` (:182), `FONT_OPTIONS` (:188), `ALIGN_OPTIONS` (:195), `VERTICAL_ALIGN_OPTIONS` (:201), `LINE_SHAPE_OPTIONS` (:213), `ARROWHEAD_OPTIONS` (:219), `GEO_OPTIONS` (:233).
- Constants `CUSTOM_LABEL = 'Custom'`, `MIXED_LABEL = 'Mixed'` (:445-446).

FUNCTIONS:
- `bindContextualControl(kind, binding)` (:411-421) — spreads definition + binding.
- `composeContextualControls(recipe, candidates)` (:424-439) — Map-by-kind, drops empty groups. NOTE: a candidate absent from the recipe is SILENTLY DROPPED (this bit them twice; see V1 recipe's WHY).
- `contextualControlIds(composition)` (:441-443).
- `selectedContextualOption(control)` (:448-460).
- `isAutomaticContextualSelection(control)` (:473-477) — a predicate that exists solely because `undefined === undefined` was silently true.
- `contextualTriggerLabel(control)` (:479-491) — builds "Label, value" / "Label, stackedvalue value".

WHOLE-MENU MODEL: `src/contextualMenus/contextualSurfaceRegistry.ts` — `ContextualSurfaceId` (6 values), `ContextualSurfaceItemId` (12 values), `CONTEXTUAL_SURFACE_REGISTRY`, `contextualSurfaceItems(surface)`.

SHARED-VALUE FOLD: `src/contextualMenus/sharedValues.ts` — `sharedValueAcross<T>(values, equals?)` and `combineSharedStyles<T>(readings, equals?)`. THE one reduce for "do these agree?"; `undefined` readings are skipped, never counted as disagreement.

PLACEMENT MODEL: `src/chrome/floatingToolbarPlacement.ts` — `Rect`, `Size`, `SelectionMenuSide = 'above'|'below'|'pinned'`, `SelectionMenuPlacementInput`, `SelectionMenuPlacement`, plus constants `SELECTION_MENU_GAP=16`, `SELECTION_MENU_MARGIN=20`, `SELECTION_OVERLAY_INSET=5`, `SELECTION_MENU_MIN_WIDTH=160`.

ARRANGE MODEL: `src/contextualMenus/ArrangeControls.tsx` — `ArrangeAction { id, label, icon: ComponentType<{className?}> }`, `ArrangeActionGroup { id, actions }`, `ArrangeControlsProps { groups, onAction, disabled?, layout?: 'row'|'stack' }`, `ArrangeTriggerProps { icon, label }`.

OPACITY MODEL: `src/contextualMenus/OpacityControl.tsx` — `OpacityChangeOptions { continuous? }`, `OpacityControlProps { value: number|'mixed'|null, onChange, label }`.

VISUAL TOKENS: `src/appearance/figjamTokens.ts` (45 exported constants, every one measured from FigJam's running editor), `src/appearance/figjamIconMap.ts` (`FIGJAM_TRIGGER_ICON`, `FIGJAM_CHECK_ICON`, `FIGJAM_EYEDROPPER_ICON`, `FIGJAM_ICON_FOR`, `figjamIconName()`), `src/appearance/figjamPalette.ts` (`FIGJAM_PALETTE` 21 rows, `FIGJAM_PALETTE_COLUMNS = 11`, `FIGJAM_COLOR_NAMES`, `FIGJAM_COLOR_HEX`, `FIGJAM_COLOR_LABELS`, `readableInk()`, `colorFromSwatch()`).

THE ONE ENGINE TYPE IN THE MODEL: `SharedStyle<string>` imported from `tldraw` at contextualControlRegistry.ts:1 and sharedValues.ts:1. It is a two-case union `{type:'shared', value} | {type:'mixed'}` — trivially re-declarable locally.

engineCoupling.what: Imports `TldrawUiPopover`, `TldrawUiPopoverContent`, `TldrawUiPopoverTrigger`, `useContainer`, `useEditor`, `useValue`, `type Editor` from `tldraw`, plus `@radix-ui/react-popover`. The single biggest blocker: the renderer that draws every screenshot cell imports the engine directly.

`const editor = useEditor()` at the top of `ContextualControls` — the editor is pulled from tldraw React context and then threaded as a prop through `ContextualControlItem` → `ControlTrigger` → `ControlPanel` → `OptionButton` → `CustomColorCell`. Every one of those signatures carries `editor: Editor`.

`useValue('systemsketch trigger font px', ...)` and `useValue('systemsketch trigger rung px', ...)` — tldraw's signals hook is the reactive-read mechanism for the trigger's px readout. Needs to become a plain prop (the value) or a generic subscribe callback.
`useValue('systemsketch target on preset rungs', () => customSize.onPresetRungs())` gates whether preset check marks are withheld. Same signals dependency.
`useValue('systemsketch option rung px', ...)` — per-row px in the Font-size list. Same signals dependency, once per option row.

`ContextualPopover` is a DUAL-ENGINE disclosure: `TldrawUiPopover`/`Trigger`/`Content` when `mode === 'selection'`, raw Radix `Popover.*` when `mode === 'editing'` (so a live canvas text editor survives). Both branches pass `side`, `align="center"`, `sideOffset={POPOVER_GAP}`, `collisionPadding={POPOVER_COLLISION_PADDING}`, and suppress first-button autofocus. Host-agnostic version needs one popover primitive with a `keepFocus`/`modal` escape hatch.

`EditingPopover` calls `useContainer()` for the Radix portal target and `onPointerDown={editor.markEventAsHandled}` on the panel so the canvas does not eat the click. Both are host facts: portal container and "this pointer event is mine".
`<TriggerGlyph control={control} value={current?.value} editor={editor} />` — the glyph layer receives the editor purely so a colour swatch can resolve its hex from the live theme.

`ColorSwatch` calls `editor.getCurrentTheme().colors[editor.getColorMode()]` inside a `useValue` to turn a colour NAME into a hex. This is the only reason `editor` travels through the glyph tree at all. Must become `hexFor(name): string | undefined` supplied by the host (the data already exists statically as `FIGJAM_COLOR_HEX`).

`import { useValue, type Editor } from 'tldraw'`; `GlyphFamilyRenderer.render(value, editor)` puts `Editor` in the renderer-table signature; `AppearanceGlyph` and `TriggerGlyph` both take `editor: Editor`. Mechanical once ColorSwatch is de-coupled — drop the parameter from the table.
`CustomColorCell` calls `registeredHex(editor, active)` through `useValue` to paint the custom-colour disc. Must become a prop.

`<CustomColorPicker editor={editor} ... />` — the entire picker sub-dialog takes an `Editor` and writes through `editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint`, `editor.getSharedOpacity`, `editor.setOpacityForSelectedShapes`, `editor.setOpacityForNextShapes`, `editor.undo`/`redo` (appearance/CustomColorPicker.tsx:65, 111, 137-138, 202-206). The picker cannot travel without being rewritten to props-in/callbacks-out; it also self-measures with `getBoundingClientRect()` at :269 and :276 for its hue/SV drag geometry.
`import type { SharedStyle } from 'tldraw'` — the value type of every control. Two-case union; declare it locally.

Registry imports `FIGJAM_COLOR_NAMES`/`FIGJAM_PALETTE_COLUMNS` (figjamPalette.ts, which imports `DEFAULT_THEME`/`TLDefaultColor`/`TLTheme` from tldraw AND declares `module '@tldraw/tlschema'` augmentation at :25-37), `isCustomColor` (customColors.ts), `ASYNC_LINE_VALUE`/`StrokeMetaField` (strokeMeta.ts, tldraw-coupled), and `CODE_LANGUAGES`/`CODE_LANGUAGE_LABELS` (code/codeModel.ts). So the pure-looking registry transitively pulls tldraw in four ways. Splitting the 21 palette NAMES out of the theme-building half is the fix.
`import type { SharedStyle } from 'tldraw'` on an otherwise 100%-pure fold. Same local-type fix.

`MANIPULATING_STATES` — hard-coded tldraw state-machine paths (`select.translating`, `select.resizing`, `select.rotating`, `select.dragging_handle`, `select.brushing`, `select.scribble_brushing`, `select.crop`) tested with `editor.isIn(path)`, OR'd with `btDndDragState.get(editor) !== null` (a dnd-kit lane's editor-scoped atom). This is pure interaction geometry: must become an `isManipulating: boolean` prop.

`usePassThroughWheelEvents(ref)` — tldraw's hook so a wheel over the pill still pans the canvas. It is also the reason the bar wraps rather than scrolls (the hook refuses to redispatch through ANY scrollable descendant). The WRAPPING must survive the port even though the hook does not.

`useAtom` + `useQuickReactor` — tldraw's signal primitives drive the per-frame position write. A host-agnostic component instead takes `{x, y, side, visible}` as props (or a render-prop) and never runs a reactor.

SELF-MEASUREMENT: a `ResizeObserver` on its own element bumping a size epoch, plus `element.getBoundingClientRect()` read inside the reactor, plus a second epoch bump on `useInterfaceScale()` change (a transform fires no ResizeObserver). The core must not measure itself; the host owns this.

`editor.getSelectionRotatedScreenBounds()` and `editor.getViewportScreenBounds()`, converted to container-relative viewport space by subtracting the viewport's screen origin. Pure camera/engine reads — the `selection` and `viewport` Rects become inputs.

DOM QUERY into the host's chrome: `editor.getContainer().querySelector('.tlui-layout__bottom__main')?.getBoundingClientRect()` to find the bottom tool belt's top edge. `bottomObstacleTop` is already a clean optional number in the placement API — the querySelector is the only dirty part and belongs to the host.

Writes `--systemsketch-selection-menu-x/y` CSS custom properties and `dataset.side` / `dataset.visible` imperatively on its own node, rather than rendering them. Deliberate (the stylesheet keeps ownership of how interface scale composes with the anchor) but it is direct DOM mutation.

`onPointerDown={editor.markEventAsHandled}` on the wrapper, and `TldrawUiToolbar` supplying toolbar semantics (roving tabindex, grouping) that `ArrangeControls` explicitly declines to duplicate (ArrangeControls.tsx:83-88). The port needs its own toolbar-semantics primitive or `ArrangeControls` loses roving focus.

`z-index: var(--tl-layer-menus, 400)` on `.systemsketch-selection-menu` — an engine-owned stacking token. Same token at chrome/pill-presentation-chip.css:19. Z-order is explicitly host-owned and must not travel.

`usePillPresentation()` reads `window.localStorage['systemsketch.pill-presentation.v1']` via `useSyncExternalStore`, and stamps `data-ss-pill-layout` only while `compare` is on. A lab affordance, not product behaviour.

`useInterfaceScale()` reads `window.localStorage['systemsketch.interface-scale.v1']` (80-160%). It feeds BOTH the CSS `scale()` transform and `selectionMenuMaxWidth(viewport, scale)`. The scale must become a prop/CSS variable the host sets.

The whole binder file — `useEditor`, `useRelevantStyles`, `useValue`, `DefaultSizeStyle`, `LineShapeSplineStyle`, `startEditingShapeWithRichText`, `editor.setStyleForSelectedShapes`/`setStyleForNextShapes`/`markHistoryStoppingPoint`/`run`, `applyArrowPresetToSelection`. This is the ADAPTER and is correctly host-side — it does not travel, but the trunk needs an equivalent seam documented so a host can write its own.

The screenshot-(c) binder: `useEditor`/`useValue`, `editor.updateShape`, `editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint`, and a `requestAnimationFrame` + `editor.getContainer().querySelector('[data-testid="block-inline-title"]')?.focus({preventScroll:true})` focus-return. The focus-return is real product behaviour (a formatting choice is part of editing, not a commit boundary) that must become an `onAfterApply` callback.

`excalidrawIcon()` clones a vendored `<svg>` with a className to satisfy `ArrangeControls`' `ComponentType<{className?}>` prop, and `ArrangeAdapter` holds ALL the selection-count policy (z-order at 1+, align at 2+, distribute at 3+) plus `editor.sendToBack/sendBackward/bringForward/bringToFront/alignShapes/distributeShapes`. `ArrangeControls` itself is clean; only this adapter is coupled.

`OpacityAdapter`: `editor.getSharedOpacity()` → 0-100 percent, `editor.setOpacityForSelectedShapes(percent/100)`, and a `draggingRef` that marks ONE history stopping point at drag start so a whole slider drag is one undo step. `OpacityControl` itself is already clean.

`CustomFontSizeCell` renders `className="code-width-custom"` — styles owned by a DIFFERENT feature's stylesheet (`src/code/code-block.css`). Deliberate (one visual language for exact-entry fields) but it is a hidden cross-module CSS dependency that will silently render unstyled if only `appearance.css` is ported.

FOUR nested `flex-wrap: wrap` declarations (bar → appearance strip → control group; and arrange cluster → arrange group), each added by a separate Codex review round after a fixed-width child overflowed as one unbreakable block. Every wrap level is load-bearing; dropping any one reproduces a clipped-button bug.

Every pill colour/radius/pad is `var(--systemsketch-pill-*, <the exact previous literal>)`, scoped on `.systemsketch-app[data-ss-pill-skin]` at the APP ROOT — not the pill wrapper — because popover panels portal out of the pill's subtree via `useContainer()`. Thirteen token names: surface, ink, divider, hover, accent, accent-radio, accent-ink, radius, trigger-radius, shadow, bar-pad, trigger-pad, divider-margin. Good theming seam already; the app-root scoping requirement is the portal-coupled part.

Every selector is `.systemsketch-app .tlui-rich-text__toolbar ...` — it styles tldraw's OWN toolbar DOM. There is no component here to port; a host-agnostic rich-text toolbar would have to be built from scratch (or the `ContextualControls` renderer re-aimed at rich-text commands).

`position: fixed`, `z-index: var(--tl-layer-menus, 400)`, `pointer-events: auto` to escape the host's `pointer-events: none`, and localStorage-backed state. A lab tool bound to this app's surface host; almost certainly should not travel at all.
`import { MIXED_LABEL } from './contextualControlRegistry'` — the one line that drags the (tldraw-importing) registry into an otherwise 100%-pure component.
`STROKE_WIDTH_PX` and `strokeWidthPxForRung` are imported from `strokeMeta.ts` (600 lines, heavily tldraw-coupled) for what is a 3-key lookup table {thin:2, medium:3.5, thick:7}. Extract the table.

reusableAsIs: `src/chrome/floatingToolbarPlacement.ts:1-343` — the ENTIRE file. Zero tldraw imports; its only dependency is `@floating-ui/core` (`computePosition`, `offset`, `Middleware`, `Platform`). It takes plain `{selection: Rect, menu: Size, viewport: Size, bottomObstacleTop?, overlayInset?}` and returns `{x, y, side}`. `makeSyntheticPlatform` (:191-201) is a DOM-free Floating UI platform — the whole module runs headless and its test proves it. This is already exactly the 'layout geometry is portable' shape the trunk's law asks for. Port verbatim.

`src/chrome/floatingToolbarPlacement.ts:126-133` — `isSelectionOnScreen(selection, viewport)`: a four-comparison intersection predicate. Explicitly documented as needing no positioning engine. Note its WHY: intersection, NOT midpoint, because an Expanded Block routinely fills the viewport with its centre off-screen (tldraw's own primitive gets this wrong).

`src/chrome/floatingToolbarPlacement.ts:169-178` — `selectionMenuMaxWidth(viewport, scale = 1)` = `max(160, viewport.w - 40) / scale`. Pure arithmetic. Survived four Codex rounds; the `/scale` on the WHOLE max (not just the viewport term) is the correctness-critical detail.

`src/chrome/floatingToolbarPlacement.test.ts:1-252` — the differential test is itself portable and is the SPEC. It sweeps 2 viewports x 2 obstacle states x 6 x-positions x 6 y-positions x 4 widths x 4 heights x 2 menu sizes = 4,608 cases against a frozen hand-rolled oracle (:32-75) copied verbatim from the pre-Floating-UI implementation, and asserts bit-identical {x,y,side}. Port it alongside the module; it is the only thing that makes the port checkable.

`src/contextualMenus/ArrangeControls.tsx:1-166` — the ENTIRE file. Its only import is `CHEVRON_PATH`/`CHEVRON_VIEWBOX` from figjamTokens (pure constants). Zero editor import, zero selection-count logic, zero tldraw: icons arrive as `ComponentType<{className?}>` props, groups arrive as data, clicks report an id upward, `disabled` is a `ReadonlySet<string>`. Already props-in/DOM-out. Its own doc says so explicitly at :90-92.

`src/contextualMenus/OpacityControl.tsx:1-80` — pure but for ONE import (`MIXED_LABEL` at :3). Native `<input type=range>`; the continuous/final split (`onInput` → `{continuous:true}`, `onChange` + `onPointerUp` → final) is a deliberate contract documented at :29-41 and mirrors `ContextualCustomSize.applyPx`. Both tests (OpacityControl.test.tsx) run through `renderToStaticMarkup` with no editor at all.

`src/contextualMenus/sharedValues.ts:19-47` — `sharedValueAcross` and `combineSharedStyles`. Pure folds; only `SharedStyle`'s TYPE is imported. Its WHY (:3-18) is load-bearing history: four hand-rolled copies of this fold used to disagree with each other, one menu saying 'mixed' while its neighbour claimed a value.

`src/contextualMenus/ContextualSurface.tsx:1-20` + `contextualSurfaceRegistry.ts:1-54` — twenty lines of renderer over a `Record<SurfaceId, ItemId[]>`. No React state, no engine, no DOM. The SurfaceId/ItemId vocabularies are SystemSketch domain words but the mechanism is generic.

`src/appearance/figjamTokens.ts:1-145` — 45 measured constants, zero imports of anything. Every number came from `getComputedStyle` on FigJam's running editor or from sampling a 2x capture; the file header says they are exported precisely so CSS and components cannot drift and so a reviewer can check the copy against the source rather than against taste.

`src/appearance/figjamIconMap.ts:1-113` — pure lookup tables (`FIGJAM_TRIGGER_ICON`, `FIGJAM_CHECK_ICON`, `FIGJAM_EYEDROPPER_ICON`, `FIGJAM_ICON_FOR`, `figjamIconName`); its only import is two TYPES from the registry. Its deliberate PARTIALNESS is the design (:1-9): a value FigJam has no icon for falls through rather than getting an invented FigJam-looking one.

`src/appearance/figjamIcons.ts` — `FIGJAM_ICONS`, generated by `tools/figjam/emit_icons.py` from traced JSON, keys namespaced by control ('arrowhead/Line arrow', 'trigger/Typeface', 'menu/Check'). Data only, no imports. Marked do-not-hand-edit.

`src/appearance/excalidrawIcons/icons.tsx` (771 lines) + `createIcon.tsx` — vendored Excalidraw glyphs as pre-built `<svg>` elements. Portable; the one gotcha is already solved twice in this repo: `createIcon` sets only a `viewBox`, never width/height, so an unstyled vendored svg renders at the browser default and blows out the pill (wrapper at AppearanceGlyph.tsx:154-175; className-clone at SystemSketchChrome.tsx:330-340).

`src/appearance/AppearanceGlyph.tsx:330-506` — the drawn-glyph functions `FillGlyph`, `DashGlyph` (+ `DASH_ARRAYS`), `SizeGlyph` (+ `SIZE_HEIGHTS`), `StrokeWidthGlyph`, `FontGlyph` (+ `FONT_STACKS`), `AlignGlyph` (+ `VERTICAL_ALIGN_ROWS`), `RoutingGlyph`, `ArrowheadGlyph`, and the `Svg` wrapper. Every one is `(value: string|undefined) => ReactNode` with no editor. `ColorSwatch` (:307-328) is the ONLY exception in that block.

`src/appearance/figjamPalette.ts:43-80` — `FIGJAM_PALETTE` (21 [name, hex, label] triples, FigJam's own order, sampled from swatch centre pixels), `FIGJAM_PALETTE_COLUMNS = 11`, `FIGJAM_COLOR_NAMES`, `FIGJAM_COLOR_HEX`, `FIGJAM_COLOR_LABELS`. Pure data. The tldraw coupling in this file is entirely below line 82 (`colorFromSwatch`, the theme builder, the `@tldraw/tlschema` module augmentation) — the split point is clean.

`src/appearance/appearance.css:1-699` and the pill rules in `chrome/systemsketch-chrome.css:825-1172` — every colour/radius/pad is already a `var(--systemsketch-pill-*, <literal>)`, so the stylesheet is themeable as-is. Only `z-index: var(--tl-layer-menus, 400)` at :836 has to go.
mustBeReExpressed: **Editor-as-prop must die.** `editor: Editor` is threaded through six component signatures (`ContextualControlItem`, `ControlTrigger`, `ControlPanel`, `OptionButton`, `CustomColorCell`, `AppearanceGlyph`/`TriggerGlyph`, plus `GlyphFamilyRenderer.render(value, editor)` in the dispatch table). It exists for exactly TWO reads: `ColorSwatch` resolving a colour name to a hex, and `registeredHex` for the custom-colour disc. Replace with one prop — `resolveSwatchHex?(name: string): string | undefined` — and the parameter disappears from all six.

**Reactivity must become plain props.** Four `useValue(...)` call sites (ContextualControls.tsx:177, 194, 271, 360) subscribe to tldraw signals for `customPx`, `rungPx`, `onPresetRungs`, and per-row `rungPx`. In a host-agnostic component these are just values the host computed. `ContextualCustomSize.sharedPx()`/`onPresetRungs()` and `rungPx(value)` should become `sharedPx: number | 'mixed' | null`, `onPresetRungs: boolean`, and `rungPx: Record<string, number | null>` — data, not thunks the component subscribes to.

**The dual-mode popover must become one primitive with a focus contract.** `ContextualPopover(mode: 'selection' | 'editing')` picks tldraw's popover vs raw Radix. The REAL requirement underneath is: (1) portal to a host-supplied container, (2) do not steal focus from a live text editor (`onOpenAutoFocus` prevented / `autoFocusFirstButton={false}`), (3) tell the host 'this pointer event is mine' (`editor.markEventAsHandled`). Express as props: `portalContainer?: Element`, `autoFocus?: boolean`, `onPointerDownCapture?`. Its exported-for-reuse WHY (:502-513) is worth preserving verbatim: building a second copy is how two menus end up flipping, offsetting and portalling differently.

**Popovers do NOT stay open by accident — that is policy.** SystemSketchChrome.tsx:460-464 documents that the pill's popovers deliberately do not auto-close on click (align-then-distribute is the normal two-step, and closing would make Arrange the one popover that behaves differently). A ported component needs an explicit `closeOnSelect={false}` default, not an accident of which library it wraps.

**Placement must be lifted out of the component entirely.** `SelectionContextualMenu` should split in two: (1) the pure `placeSelectionMenu` module, ported verbatim; (2) a dumb `<FloatingToolbar x y side visible>` that renders and styles. Everything between — the manipulating-state gate, the ResizeObserver, the interface-scale epoch, the reactor, the bounds reads, the bottom-chrome querySelector, the stale-pass guard — is host code. The monotonic `placementPass` guard (:129, 173, 185) is real engineering (an async `computePosition` can resolve out of order onto a detached node) and must survive wherever the host runs it.

**Toolbar semantics need a home.** `ArrangeControls` renders plain `<button>` on purpose (:83-88) because the surrounding `TldrawUiToolbar` already supplies grouping and roving tabindex, and duplicating it 'would fight the surrounding toolbar rather than compose with it'. Port the pill without a toolbar primitive and the Arrange cluster silently loses roving focus. The trunk needs its own `Toolbar`/`ToolbarGroup` (or the components need to opt in).

**Wrapping, not scrolling, is a hard requirement with a non-obvious reason.** Four nested `flex-wrap: wrap` levels exist because tldraw's `usePassThroughWheelEvents` refuses to redispatch a wheel through ANY scrollable descendant (axis-agnostic `scrollWidth > clientWidth`), so an `overflow-x: auto` pill silently killed canvas panning on hover. A host without that hook might not need the constraint — but the max-width cap, the 160px floor, and their mirroring between CSS and `selectionMenuMaxWidth()` all have to move together or drift.

**Interface scale is a two-place invariant.** The `/ var(--systemsketch-interface-scale)` in the CSS `max-width` (systemsketch-chrome.css:919) and the `scale` parameter of `selectionMenuMaxWidth()` (floatingToolbarPlacement.ts:169) are the same formula written twice, on purpose, so the math stays unit-testable without a DOM. A port must keep them mirrored or re-derive one from the other.

**The registry's tldraw type and its four tldraw-transitive imports.** `SharedStyle<string>` → local `{type:'shared',value:T} | {type:'mixed'}`. The `color`/`strokeColor` entries need `FIGJAM_COLOR_NAMES` split out of the theme-building half of figjamPalette.ts. `lineStyle` needs `ASYNC_LINE_VALUE` ('async') and `StrokeMetaField` extracted from the 600-line strokeMeta.ts. `codeLanguage` needs `CODE_LANGUAGES`/`CODE_LANGUAGE_LABELS` — or that entry should simply not be a bbox-ui concern and become host-injectable.

**`meta?: StrokeMetaField` is a SystemSketch document-model leak in the middle of a presentational registry.** `bindAppearanceControl` (AppearanceControls.tsx:200-213) branches on `control.meta === 'pattern' | 'color' | 'width'` to pick a write path. That dispatch belongs to the host's binder, not to the shared definition table.

**The `addText` action's write is an engine call disguised as an option.** `startEditingShapeWithRichText(editor, shape, {selectAll: true})` (AppearanceControls.tsx:174) — the component only needs `onSelect()`; the shape-entering is the host's.

**The focus-return-to-editor behaviour must become a callback.** BlockTitleFormattingMenu.tsx:37-44 does `requestAnimationFrame` → `querySelector('[data-testid="block-inline-title"]')` → `.focus({preventScroll: true})`, with an explicit WHY (:61-63): 'A formatting choice is part of editing, not a commit boundary.' That is real product taste the port must keep, expressed as `onApplied?()`.

**`ContextualSurfaceId`/`ContextualSurfaceItemId` are SystemSketch's domain vocabulary** ('branch-selection', 'behavior-tree-selection', 'propagation-focus'). The mechanism generalises; the enum does not. Make the surface registry generic over a host-supplied id union.

**Selection-count policy is not in `ArrangeControls` and must not sneak in.** z-order at 1+, align at 2+, distribute at 3+ lives entirely in `ArrangeAdapter` (SystemSketchChrome.tsx:424-433), and `ArrangeControls`' own doc says it 'holds no selection-count logic of its own'. Preserve that boundary.

**The CustomColorPicker is a separate port project.** It needs `editor` for opacity plumbing, history stopping points, undo/redo keybindings, and the `previewCustomColor` retire-as-you-drag registration scheme (one registered enum value per pixel of pointer travel otherwise). Props-in/callbacks-out is a real rewrite, not a mechanical one. Its two `getBoundingClientRect()` calls (:269, 276) are legitimate pointer-geometry for a slider drag — arguably allowed, since they measure the control's own track, not the host.

**`.code-width-custom` must be brought along or renamed.** `CustomFontSizeCell` styles itself from `src/code/code-block.css:117-156`, a different feature's stylesheet. The cross-module reuse is deliberate (one exact-entry idiom for the whole app) but the port must either vendor those 40 lines or the Custom-px row renders unstyled with every build green.
openQuestions: The screenshot's 'align icon + chevron' cell is ambiguous between TWO controls that both exist and both look like that: the `align` appearance control (text alignment, `trigger: 'value'`, Excalidraw `TextAlignLeftIcon`) and `ArrangeTrigger` (whose face is deliberately the same Excalidraw `AlignLeftIcon` — SystemSketchChrome.tsx:374-383 explains Excalidraw ships no 'arrange' glyph, so align-left is borrowed). Worth confirming with Zach which one the port must reproduce first, because one is a radio row and the other is a stacked action panel.

There is NO SystemSketch rich-text toolbar component — only a 55-line CSS reskin of tldraw's `.tlui-rich-text__toolbar` whose own header says keeping it as a class-scoped adapter 'preserves tldraw's reliable editor behavior instead of cloning six commands into app-owned React state'. So 'port the rich-text toolbar' means either (a) port nothing and note the gap, or (b) build a genuinely new component and re-implement six commands. That is a product decision, not a porting one.

`packages/bbox-ui` is frozen v1 and the trunk is `apps/storybook-basics/src/components/` — but this surface needs CSS (699 + ~350 lines) plus a design-token layer plus vendored icon data (771 + 85 lines). The trunk's shadcn sibling-rule (`../lib/utils` up-and-over, `lib/utils.ts` landing at `components/lib/utils.ts`) means a multi-file component family with its own `icons/` and `tokens/` subdirectories may need its own registry-target reasoning. Not answerable from SystemSketch.

`SharedStyle` — should the ported components speak a three-state value (`shared | mixed | absent`) at all, or is `mixed` a canvas-multi-selection concept a general editor kit should not bake in? Everything in this surface (the mixed-glyph fade at appearance.css:111-113, the mixed swatch face, `MIXED_LABEL`, the whole `sharedValues.ts` fold) assumes it. Worth an explicit decision before the design phase, because it is pervasive.

The 21-colour FigJam palette, the FigJam traced icons, and the Excalidraw vendored icons are three separate borrowed visual vocabularies. `figjamIcons.ts` is 'traced from the running application' and `figjamPalette.ts`'s hexes were 'sampled from FigJam's own colour popover'. Whether those travel into a public component kit is a licensing/provenance question I cannot settle. The Excalidraw icons are the clearer case (MIT, and Zach explicitly asked for them: 'use the excalidraw icons exactly ... so we don't need to reinvent another visual icon grammar').

`PillPresentationChip` + `pillSkins.css` are a comparison LAB, explicitly 'deliberately kept out of the app's live --ss-* theme vocabulary ... none of these is a decision yet'. Does the port take the five skins (as a Storybook gallery, which matches how Zach reviews), take only the thirteen `--systemsketch-pill-*` token NAMES as the theming contract, or take neither?

`V1_COMPACT_RECIPE`, `V3_SEGMENTED_RECIPE`, and the pre-lab `'default'` layout are three live pill layouts; V3 is the shipped default since 2026-09-08. `restructureForV1Cluster` (appearanceModel.ts) un-stacks and re-folds controls for V1 specifically. Does the port carry all three, or only V3?

`SELECTION_OVERLAY_INSET = 5` is measured against tldraw's specific selection-handle rendering ('a selected 240x140 rectangle at (700,380) paints selection blue from (695,375) to (944,524)'). It is already a parameter, but its DEFAULT is engine-specific — should the ported API drop the default and force the host to state it?

The registry silently drops any candidate control absent from the active recipe (`composeContextualControls`, :431-437). That has already caused two real bugs (`lineShape` lost for every connector under V1 — Codex judge round 1, 2026-09-08). Should the ported version keep the silent-drop (a feature for optional slots) or fail loudly in dev? Not my call, but it should be a conscious one.

surveys.surface: The bottom tool toolbar — SystemSketch's Figma-style main toolbar (select / frame / System-family / bbox-family / shape / draw / text / divider / library "+"), rendered into tldraw's `components.Toolbar` slot.

anatomy.description: `SystemSketchFigmaToolbar` reads the active tool and active geo style from the editor, then renders eight children into tldraw's `DefaultToolbar` with responsive limits `minItems={4} maxItems={8} minSizePx={255} maxSizePx={380}`. Its own WHY, verbatim: "P1: project seven Figma-style families through tldraw's public DefaultToolbar. / P2 remains a deliberate shell-only escape hatch: if DefaultToolbar's extra chrome or responsive DOM becomes constraining, replace this composition with an owned TldrawUiToolbar. Keep toolbarModel, tool overrides, Curve side effect, library catalog, and tests unchanged." The rounded-bar look is NOT in this component — it is CSS overriding tldraw's `.tlui-main-toolbar__tools` (46px min-height, 3px pad, 1px `--ss-border`, 11px radius, `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ss-surface-raised) 97%, transparent)`, `--ss-shadow-1`, `contain: layout style`, `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)`).

anatomy.part: SimpleToolSlot (cell 1 Cursor, cell 2 Frame, cell 7 Text)
anatomy.description: A plain toggle cell with no chevron. Props already look component-shaped: `{tool, fallbackIcon, title, active, disabledTitle}`. Derives `disabled = !tool`, sets `aria-pressed={active}`, `data-value`/`data-testid` from `title.toLowerCase()`, renders `tool?.icon ?? fallbackIcon`, and calls `tool?.onSelect('toolbar')`. Instantiated at :578 (`tools.select`, `tool-pointer`, active when `activeToolId==='select'`), :579 (`tools.frame`, `tool-frame`), :590 (`tools.text`, `tool-text`).

anatomy.part: FamilyToolSlot (the split button — the chevron-under-icon cells)
anatomy.description: The abstraction the whole toolbar rests on: a Radix dropdown root whose TRIGGER is itself an armable tool button. One cell = the remembered member's icon + a chevron badge pinned bottom-right. Press arms the remembered tool AND opens the menu. The split is implemented as two handlers: `onPointerDown={(event)=>{ if (event.button===0) onSelect() }}` and `onClick={(event)=>{ if (event.detail===0) onSelect() }}`, with the verbatim WHY: "Pointer activation already happened before Radix opened the menu, which lets the menu keep focus and preserve one-press Escape." Menu content is anchored `side="top" align="center" sideOffset={11} alignOffset={0} collisionPadding={12}`. Props today: `{family:'shape'|'draw'|'system'|'bbox', icon, label, active, onSelect, children}` — the family string is used for the tooltip (`${label} · Open ${family} tools`), `data-family`, `data-value` and `data-testid`.

Pure CSS, not a component: `.systemsketch-family-tool__chevron` absolutely positioned `right:2px bottom:2px`, 13×13 grid, `z-index:4`, `pointer-events:none`, `--ss-text-muted` at rest, `--ss-text` on hover or `[data-state='open']`, and `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ss-accent-text) 78%, transparent)` when the cell is active. The inner icon is forced to 9×9 with `!important`. The JSX side is just a `<span aria-hidden>` wrapping `<TldrawUiButtonIcon icon="chevron-down" small />`.

anatomy.part: ToolMenuItem (a row inside a family popout)
anatomy.description: Four-column grid row: `{icon, label, shortcut?, selected, onSelect}`. Renders icon (small), label, an optional `<kbd>` shortcut, and a trailing check column that prints '✓' when selected. The grid is `grid-template-columns: 22px minmax(0,1fr) auto 14px; gap:7px; min-height:34px; border-radius:7px`, and `[data-isactive='true']` paints `--ss-accent-soft`. Note the row is marked selected via `data-isactive`, which is ALSO what the bar-level active style keys off — one attribute, two meanings.

Bare `<div class="systemsketch-tool-menu__heading">` (9px, 800 weight, .075em tracking, uppercase, `--ss-text-muted`) and `<div class="systemsketch-tool-menu__separator" role="separator">` (1px `--ss-border`). Headings in use: "Shapes", "Arrows · repeat A to cycle", "System design", "bbox-ui", "Drawing". The popout itself is a fixed 220px-wide 11px-radius card with `--ss-shadow-2`.

13 members in `SYSTEM_MENU_ITEMS`: Block (B), Branch, Loop, Async region, Behavior Tree, Code, Pill (P), Port, Type, Type Mapping, Callout, Icon, Table. Each icon is a bespoke React component (`<BlockIcon/>`, `<BranchIcon/>`, …). Current-member resolution is a hand-written 13-arm ternary chain (:355-381) falling through to `preferences.lastSystemTool`, and `isActive` is a hand-written 13-clause `||` (:383-395) — the two lists are maintained separately and can drift. Carries a contextual FOOTER: when exactly one unlocked Callout card is selected, a separator plus an "Add leader to selected Callout" row appears. Verbatim WHYs on the member list: "Block keeps B; Branch has no key yet and lives one click deeper on purpose, because it is used far less often than a Block and Zach wants the toolbar, not the right-click menu, to be where that muscle memory forms."; "A loop is the same kind of region as a Branch, one click deeper for the same reason…"; "A Behavior Tree is a region like Branch and Loop: its nodes are real Blocks, so it lives in the same family slot rather than on its own."; "Code is an authored literal reached from this family or S-search; C/O intentionally converge on Ellipse for drawing muscle memory."; "A pill is a variable: a literal argument, a named result, or both. P."; "Type intentionally has no key: T stays stock text, so a Type is reached from this shared slot rather than a letter collision."; "Same reasoning as Type, one slot over: an alias mapping is a sibling grammar on the same Block shape, not a different kind of primitive."; "Callout intentionally has no key: its two-click interaction is reached from the shared system-design muscle-memory slot, not from a letter collision."; "A standalone Icon has no key either — it is reached here or by tool search (\"glyph\" is the alias), the same way Type and Callout are."; "Same reasoning again: reached from this slot or by tool search (\"grid\" is the alias), no letter key of its own."

5 members: bbox-block, bbox-port, bbox-pill, bbox-glyph, bbox-textbox. This is the CLEAN version of the same pattern: `current = isBboxFamilyTool(activeToolId) ? activeToolId : preferences.lastBboxTool` and `isActive = isBboxFamilyTool(activeToolId)` — one predicate, two uses, no ternary chain. Verbatim WHY: "The bbox-ui family: a second, parallel set of primitives vendored from the separate bbox-ui repo (src/bboxUi/, see adapter/tools.ts's own WHY) so Zach can test his design-system components on the same board as the existing System design family, in their own toolbar slot, until he is ready to migrate and retire the old one. Reuses the existing Block/Port glyphs on purpose — same concept, a different implementation — the separate slot and this heading are what disambiguate the two." And at the slot: "The bbox-ui family's own toolbar slot — a second FamilyToolSlot beside SystemFamilySlot, one click deeper, the same composition as every other family here (never a second toolbar)." Placement comment at :582-586 names deleting this slot as the retirement path.

Two sections in one popout. Section 1 "Shapes": Rectangle (R), Ellipse (C / O), Triangle, Diamond, Line (L). Section 2 "Arrows · repeat A to cycle": three arrows labelled with their press count — 'A', 'A × 2', 'A × 3' — both the ORDER and the labels derived from the rotation, never typed. Current resolution differs from every other family because tldraw models geo shapes as one tool plus a style: `if (activeToolId==='line') current='line'; if (activeToolId==='arrow') current='arrow-'+preferences.lastArrowPreset; if (activeToolId==='geo' && isSupportedShapeTool(geo)) current=geo`, else `preferences.lastShapeTool`. Tooltip label is hardcoded `${currentItem.label} · R C/O L A`. Verbatim WHY on the arrow rows: "The arrows, listed in the order A walks them and labelled with how many presses that is. Both come from the cycle itself, so the rows stay honest when the starting preset moves — it now starts on Elbow, which is also the shape a new data edge takes."

Two members: Pen (D) and Highlighter (⇧ D). Current resolution `activeToolId === 'highlight' ? 'highlight' : preferences.lastDrawTool`. Tooltip label is `${currentItem.label} · ${currentItem.shortcut}`. The simplest complete instance of the family/slot pattern and the best template for the port.

Not a dropdown — a `TldrawUiPopover` with local `useState` open, anchored `side="top" align="end" sideOffset={12} collisionPadding={12} autoFocusFirstButton={false}`. Trigger is a `plus` icon button with `aria-pressed={isOpen}`. The divider before it is CSS on the popover wrapper itself: `.systemsketch-library-popover { margin-left:2px !important; padding-left:3px; border-left:1px solid var(--ss-border) }`, and the trigger is narrowed to 40px. The panel body is an `<aside>` with an eyebrow/title header ("Library" / "Shapes"), a `cross-2` close button, and `<ShapeLibraryBrowser>` — a separate 198-line surface with its own catalog model, localStorage recents and editor insert. `onWheel` is stopped on the aside so the canvas does not zoom under the open panel. Sized `min(340px, 100vw-24px)` × `min(590px, 100vh-104px)`.

Every cell is 43×40 (39px wide under `@media (max-width: 620px)`), inner hit rect inset 2px with 7px radius. Hover paints `--ss-surface-hover`; `[aria-pressed='true']` or `[data-isactive='true']` paints `--ss-accent` with `--ss-accent-text` foreground — that is the blue first cell in the screenshot. Disabled cells drop to `opacity:.38`. Inside tldraw's overflow menu the family cells are re-sized to 40px with margins/borders stripped.

surveys.dataModel:
Everything the toolbar remembers lives in ONE record, `ToolbarPreferences` (src/toolbar/toolbarModel.ts:29-36):

  interface ToolbarPreferences {
    version: 1
    lastShapeTool: ShapeFamilyTool
    lastArrowPreset: ArrowPreset
    lastDrawTool: DrawFamilyTool
    lastSystemTool: SystemFamilyTool
    lastBboxTool: BboxFamilyTool
  }

Exact exported names and where they live — all in `src/toolbar/toolbarModel.ts` unless noted:

TYPES
- `ArrowPreset = 'straight' | 'curve' | 'elbow'` (:5)
- `ShapeFamilyTool` (:7-16) — 'rectangle'|'ellipse'|'triangle'|'diamond'|'line'|'arrow-straight'|'arrow-curve'|'arrow-elbow'. Note the arrow members are SYNTHETIC ids that do not exist as tldraw tools; `selectShapeFamilyTool` maps them through `ARROW_TOOL_IDS` (toolbarIntegration.ts:54-58) to 'systemsketch-arrow-straight' etc.
- `DrawFamilyTool = 'draw' | 'highlight'` (:17)
- `SystemFamilyTool` (:19-20), doc comment verbatim: "The system-design family under the Block slot: nodes, regions, code, values, types, free ports, Callouts, and Icons."
- `BboxFamilyTool` (:22-27) — 'bbox-block'|'bbox-port'|'bbox-pill'|'bbox-glyph'|'bbox-textbox'
- `ToolbarPreferences` (:29-36)

VALUES
- `DEFAULT_TOOLBAR_PREFERENCES` (:45-52) — rectangle / elbow / draw / block / bbox-block
- `STORAGE_KEY = 'systemsketch.toolbar-preferences.v1'` (:54, module-private)
- Validation arrays, module-private: `ARROW_PRESETS` (:55), `SHAPE_TOOLS` (:56-65), `DRAW_TOOLS` (:66), `SYSTEM_TOOLS` (:67), `BBOX_TOOLS` (:68)
- `ARROW_PRESET_ROUTING: Record<ArrowPreset, ConnectionRoutingKind>` (:118-122)

FUNCTIONS
- `isBboxFamilyTool(value: string): value is BboxFamilyTool` (:73-75)
- `parseToolbarPreferences(value: unknown): ToolbarPreferences` (:85-105) — field-independent fallback: a corrupt `lastArrowPreset` resets ONLY that field (proved in toolbarModel.test.ts:73-99)
- `nextArrowPreset` (:107-109), `connectionRoutingForArrowPreset` (:124-126), `arrowPresetPressCount` (:135-139), `arrowPresetsInPressOrder` (:142-144), `arrowPresetForActivation(currentToolId, lastArrowPreset)` (:146-151), `shapeToolForArrowPreset` (:153-155)
- `getToolbarPreferences()` (:182-185), `updateToolbarPreferences(update: Partial<Omit<ToolbarPreferences,'version'>>)` (:187-205), `useToolbarPreferences(): ToolbarPreferences` (:212-214)

PERSISTENCE MECHANISM (this is the seam, not the shape). A module-level singleton: `let snapshot` (:157), `let hydrated` (:158), `const listeners = new Set<()=>void>()` (:159). `hydrate()` (:161-171) lazily reads `window.localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)` once, JSON-parses, and runs it through `parseToolbarPreferences`; any throw resets to defaults. `persist()` (:173-180) writes back, swallowing errors with the verbatim WHY: "Preferences are helpful feedback, never a reason to block drawing." `updateToolbarPreferences` (:187-205) does a hand-written 5-field equality check and returns the SAME object identity when nothing moved — so `useSyncExternalStore` does not re-render. `useToolbarPreferences` (:212-214) is `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getToolbarPreferences, () => DEFAULT_TOOLBAR_PREFERENCES)` — the server snapshot is always the default.

WHO WRITES IT. The component never calls `updateToolbarPreferences`. Writing is done entirely in `toolbarIntegration.ts` by WRAPPING tldraw's tool items: `wrapTool(tool, beforeSelect)` (:188-200) returns `{...tool, onSelect(source){ beforeSelect(); tool.onSelect(source) }}`. `overrideTools` (:223-268) wraps rectangle/ellipse/triangle/diamond/line → `lastShapeTool`, draw/highlight → `lastDrawTool`, and rebuilds `arrow` to advance the preset. `rememberSystemTools` (:274-281) and `rememberBboxTools` (:295-302) do the same per family. So the memory is written at the TOOL layer, which means it updates whether the user came from the toolbar, a keyboard shortcut, or tool search — that is the property the port must preserve.

MENU-ITEM SHAPES (src/toolbar/SystemSketchToolbar.tsx).
