Four near-identical, separately declared row types — `ShapeMenuItem {id,label,icon: string|TLUiIconJsx, shortcut?}` (:57-62), the inline `DRAW_MENU_ITEMS` type (:95-100), the inline `SYSTEM_MENU_ITEMS` type (:116-121, `icon: TLUiIconJsx` only), the inline `BBOX_MENU_ITEMS` type (:164-170). Data: `GEO_MENU_ITEMS` (:64-70), `ARROW_LABELS` (:72-76), `ARROW_MENU_ITEMS` derived (:84-91), `SHAPE_MENU_ITEMS` (:93), `DRAW_MENU_ITEMS` (:101-103), `SHAPE_BY_ID` (:105-108), `SYSTEM_MENU_ITEMS` (:122-153), `BBOX_MENU_ITEMS` (:171-176).

THE FAMILY/SLOT ABSTRACTION, STATED EXACTLY. A family is (a) a closed string union of tool ids, (b) an ordered item list of `{id,label,icon,shortcut?}`, (c) one `last*Tool` field on `ToolbarPreferences`, (d) a "is one of mine" predicate, and (e) a `select<Family>FamilyTool(tools, id, source='toolbar')` dispatcher (toolbarIntegration.ts:428-461 — three of the four are the identical one-liner `tools[tool]?.onSelect(source)`; only the shape one remaps arrows). A SLOT renders `current = <mine, if the active tool is mine> ?? preferences.last<Family>Tool`, paints the current member's icon on the trigger, marks the trigger active iff the active tool is mine, arms `current` on press, and lists every member in the popout with `selected === current`. Today a host "declares a family" by editing six places at once: the union, the validation array, the `ToolbarPreferences` field + default, a `remember*Tools` wrapper, an item-list constant, and a bespoke `<XFamilySlot>` component. Nothing enumerates those six — the `isBboxFamilyTool` WHY at toolbarModel.ts:70-72 is a scar from exactly that: "kept beside the validation array so a new family member cannot join one and miss the other (the slot's inline ternary chain did not scale past two)."

engineCoupling.what: Sixteen named imports from `tldraw`: DefaultToolbar, GeoShapeGeoStyle, TldrawUiButton, TldrawUiButtonIcon, TldrawUiButtonLabel, TldrawUiDropdownMenu{Content,Item,Root,Trigger}, TldrawUiPopover{,Content,Trigger}, TldrawUiToolbarButton, useEditor, useTools, useValue, TLUiIconJsx, TLUiToolItem. Every visible element of this surface is a tldraw UI primitive; there is no engine-free DOM in the file.

`<DefaultToolbar minItems={4} maxItems={8} minSizePx={255} maxSizePx={380}>` — the bar's responsive overflow (which cells collapse into tldraw's overflow menu) is decided by tldraw measuring its own DOM width. This is exactly the self-measurement the core forbids.

`useValue('systemsketch active tool', () => editor.getCurrentToolId(), [editor])` and `useValue('systemsketch active geo', () => editor.getSharedStyles().getAsKnownValue(GeoShapeGeoStyle), [editor])` — the two inputs that drive every slot's `current` and `isActive` are pulled from the editor's reactive signal graph, not passed in.
`useTools()` called inside each of the four family slots — an ambient tldraw context is the action registry. Each slot then dispatches via `select*FamilyTool(tools, id)`.

`useEditor()` + `useValue('SystemSketch selected Callout card', () => { const selected = editor.getOnlySelectedShape(); return isCalloutCard(selected) && !selected.isLocked ? selected.id : null }, [editor])` — SystemFamilySlot reads the canvas SELECTION to decide whether to render an extra menu row. A popout whose contents depend on what is selected on the canvas.
`startAddingCalloutLeader(editor, selectedCalloutId)` — a menu row invokes a SystemSketch editor command that puts the app into a two-click leader-placement mode (src/callout/CalloutTool.ts:31).

Sixteen imports of SystemSketch domain modules for tool ids and icons: BLOCK_TOOL_ID/PILL_TOOL_ID/TYPE_MAPPING_TOOL_ID/TYPE_TOOL_ID from '../blocks', BranchIcon, LoopIcon, BehaviorTreeIcon, CodeIcon, CalloutIcon, IconIcon, TableIcon, AsyncRegionIcon, FloatingPortIcon, PillIcon, BlockIcon, TypeIcon, TypeMappingIcon, the five BBOX_*_TOOL_ID, plus `isCalloutCard`/`startAddingCalloutLeader` and `ShapeLibraryBrowser`. The item lists are compiled into the component, so no other host can declare its own families.

String icon names ('geo-rectangle','geo-ellipse','geo-triangle','geo-diamond','tool-line','tool-arrow','arrow-arc','arrow-elbow','tool-pencil','tool-highlight','tool-text','tool-pointer','tool-frame','chevron-down','plus','cross-2') resolved through tldraw's asset registry (`getAssetUrlsByImport()`, App.tsx:130). A string icon name means nothing outside tldraw; the `icon: string | TLUiIconJsx` union has to collapse to ReactNode.

`tool?.onSelect('toolbar')` and `tool?.icon ?? fallbackIcon` — the `TLUiToolItem` record (id/label/icon/kbd/onSelect(source)) leaks into SimpleToolSlot's props, including the tldraw-specific `TLUiEventSource` string.

`onPointerDown={(event)=>{ if (event.button===0) onSelect() }}` plus `onClick={(event)=>{ if (event.detail===0) onSelect() }}` — real pointer/keyboard interaction wiring inside the trigger, ordered so activation beats Radix's open. The behavior must survive; the handlers themselves are the split-button's own semantics, not canvas interaction, so they can stay in the component if expressed as `onArm`.

`const setOpen = (open) => { if (!open) editor.menus.clearOpenMenus(); setIsOpen(open) }` — LibrarySlot reaches into tldraw's global open-menu registry so the canvas re-enables interaction when the popover closes.
`onWheel={(event) => event.stopPropagation()}` on the library panel — a pointer listener whose only job is to stop the canvas zooming under an open panel.

`<ShapeLibraryBrowser autoFocus onCancel onInserted />` — an entire second surface (198 lines) with its own catalog model, its own localStorage recents (`SHAPE_LIBRARY_RECENTS_KEY`, a `storage` + CustomEvent listener pair at ShapeLibraryBrowser.tsx:37-57) and `insertShapeLibraryItem(editor, …)`. The '+' cell must become a popover that takes `children`.

Module-level mutable singleton (`snapshot`, `hydrated`, `listeners`) backed by `window.localStorage` under the fixed key 'systemsketch.toolbar-preferences.v1'. Any two toolbars on one page share one store; a host cannot supply its own persistence, namespace the key, or render the toolbar controlled.

`useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getToolbarPreferences, () => DEFAULT_TOOLBAR_PREFERENCES)` — the server snapshot is hardcoded to defaults, so SSR/first paint deliberately shows the default member and swaps after hydration. Worth keeping as a documented choice, but it means the component cannot be rendered deterministically in a story without controlling the store.

`import type { ConnectionRoutingKind } from '../blocks/connections/connectionModel'` — the otherwise-pure model file imports a SystemSketch shape-domain type so `ARROW_PRESET_ROUTING` can be typed. Type-only, so erasable, but it is what ties `ArrowPreset` to SystemSketch's cable vocabulary.

The whole file is host-side: it imports `Editor`, `TLArrowShape`, `TLShape`, `TLShapeId`, `TLUiActionsContextType`, `TLUiEventSource`, `TLUiOverrideHelpers`, `TLUiOverrides`, `TLUiToolItem`, `TLUiToolsContextType`, `ArrowShapeKindStyle` from tldraw, plus 17 SystemSketch modules. None of it travels; but the FOUR `select*FamilyTool` dispatchers at :428-461 are the callback shape the component actually needs.

`applyArrowPreset` writes two tldraw next-shape styles: `editor.setStyleForNextShapes(ArrowShapeKindStyle, preset==='elbow'?'elbow':'arc')` and conditionally `ConnectionRoutingStyle`. Verbatim WHY: "One choice, two shapes. An arrow and a data edge are the same idea drawn on different subjects, so the preset writes both next-shape styles at once: pressing A until the arrow is elbowed leaves the next cable elbowed too, and switching to Curve curves both. Two `StyleProp`s, one gesture — tldraw's own next-shape channel does the rest, including for a cable created from a port press."

`hasConnectionShape(editor) { return editor.shapeUtils[CONNECTION_SHAPE_TYPE] !== undefined }` — a capability probe against the editor's registered shape utils, guarding a crash. Verbatim WHY: "…the stock-tldraw lab mounts tldraw *without* the Connection shape, so writing the cable routing there is not an ignored style — it is an unknown property in instance state, and tldraw fails the whole document with a validation error and its crash screen. So the second half of the preset is asked for, never assumed."

`registerToolbarSideEffects(editor)` calls `applyStoredArrowPreset(editor)` then `editor.sideEffects.registerBeforeCreateHandler('shape', …)` with `isDrawingArrowWithArrowTool(editor)`. Mounted from App.tsx:269 and EmbeddedCanvas.tsx:289. Pure host lifecycle; the toolbar component must not own it.

`applyArrowPresetToSelection` calls `editor.getSelectedShapes()` and `editor.updateShapes(...)` and then writes preferences — the appearance menu and the toolbar share one preference field, so selecting three arrows and clicking Curve also changes what the toolbar draws next.

`SYSTEMSKETCH_TOOLBAR_OVERRIDES: TLUiOverrides` — a 13-deep nested composition of `with*Tool(editor, …)` factories plus action and translation overrides. This is how the family members become selectable at all. Passed at App.tsx:349 / EmbeddedCanvas.tsx:421.

Eleven stock tldraw class selectors are overridden to produce the bar's look: `.tlui-main-toolbar__extras` and `__mobile-style-panel` (display:none), `--horizontal`, `__inner`, `__left`, `__tools`, `.tlui-button__tool` (+ `::after`, `:hover::after`, `[aria-pressed]`, `[data-isactive]`), `__overflow-content`, `.tlui-icon`. The visual identity of this surface currently lives in overrides of another library's DOM, so none of it ports as-is.

`.systemsketch-app:has(.systemsketch-family-tool[data-state='open']) .tlui-menu-click-capture { pointer-events: none }` — defeats tldraw's dismiss-only click-capture layer. Verbatim WHY: "Stock tldraw deliberately makes the first canvas click after opening any menu dismiss-only. A family tile is different: its opening press has already armed the displayed drawing tool, so let the next canvas gesture reach that tool while Radix's outside-pointer listener dismisses the picker. Scope this to our three family menus; context menus and every other stock menu retain tldraw's click-capture layer." Pure host interaction geometry — must NOT travel, but the product promise (press the family tile, then draw immediately) is a contract the port has to leave achievable.
`padding-bottom: calc(10px + var(--tl-sab))` — the mobile safe-area-bottom variable is tldraw's.

Every colour is a `--ss-*` token from src/theme/tokens.css, and in the tldraw theme those tokens themselves alias `--tl-color-*` / `--tl-shadow-*` (tokens.css:111-138). Under VS Code and Obsidian hosts the same tokens alias those hosts' variables instead (tokens.css:150-193) — so the token LAYER is already host-agnostic; only its tldraw binding is not.

`data-value`/`data-testid` strings are derived from display text (`title.toLowerCase()`) or the family key — `systemsketch-tool-cursor`, `systemsketch-tool-system`, `systemsketch-tool-shape`, `systemsketch-tool-library`, `systemsketch-library-panel`. The e2e smoke test selects on them (tests/toolbar_family_menu_smoke.mjs:50, 60, 106, 134, 189, 201), so renaming a title silently breaks a test.

reusableAsIs: src/toolbar/toolbarModel.ts:107-155 — the entire arrow-preset algebra: `nextArrowPreset` (:107-109), `ARROW_PRESET_ROUTING` (:118-122), `connectionRoutingForArrowPreset` (:124-126), `arrowPresetPressCount` (:135-139), `arrowPresetsInPressOrder` (:142-144), `arrowPresetForActivation` (:146-151), `shapeToolForArrowPreset` (:153-155). Pure: string-union in, string-union out, no imports but the erasable `ConnectionRoutingKind` type. `arrowPresetPressCount` is the interesting one — it computes the 'A × 2' hint as `((target - start + n) % n) + 1` from the cycle itself; verbatim WHY: "How many presses of A, from a freshly started app, land on this preset. The toolbar prints this beside each arrow, and it has to be derived rather than typed: the cycle is a rotation, so moving the starting preset silently renumbers every rung. Deriving it means the hint cannot drift from the key." Fully covered by toolbarModel.test.ts:17-70.

src/toolbar/toolbarModel.ts:77-105 — `isRecord`, `includes<T extends string>`, `parseToolbarPreferences`. Pure validation with NO I/O; the field-independent fallback (a bad `lastArrowPreset` resets only that field, everything else survives) is proved at toolbarModel.test.ts:73-99. Ports verbatim as the body of a generic `parsePreferences(registry, value)`.

src/toolbar/toolbarModel.ts:73-75 — `isBboxFamilyTool`, the family membership predicate. Three lines, but it is the SHAPE the port wants everywhere: one predicate feeding both `current` resolution and `isActive`. Verbatim WHY: "The BboxFamilySlot's \"is one of ours active\" check — kept beside the validation array so a new family member cannot join one and miss the other (the slot's inline ternary chain did not scale past two)."

src/toolbar/toolbarModel.ts:187-205 — `updateToolbarPreferences`'s identity-preserving merge (the 5-field equality check returning `snapshot` unchanged). The LOGIC ports verbatim as a reducer; only the surrounding singleton/localStorage does not. Same file :173-180 carries the verbatim WHY that must travel with any persistence adapter: "Preferences are helpful feedback, never a reason to block drawing."

src/toolbar/SystemSketchToolbar.tsx:84-91 — `ARROW_MENU_ITEMS`, the derivation of the arrow rows (order AND shortcut label) from `arrowPresetsInPressOrder()` + `arrowPresetPressCount()`, producing 'A' / 'A × 2' / 'A × 3'. Pure data transform over the pure algebra above.

src/toolbar/SystemSketchToolbar.tsx:105-108 and :178-180 — `SHAPE_BY_ID` (Object.fromEntries index) and `isSupportedShapeTool` (`value in SHAPE_BY_ID`). Pure; generalizes to the family registry's own lookup.

src/toolbar/toolbarIntegration.ts:49-52 — `arrowPresetForShape(shape)`: `kind==='elbow' → 'elbow'`, else `Math.abs(bend) < 0.001 ? 'straight' : 'curve'`. Reads three plain fields; pure. The 0.001 epsilon and the verbatim rationale at :105-113 ("tldraw stores both Straight and Curved as `kind: arc`; `bend: 0` is the straight state") are the whole content.
src/toolbar/toolbarIntegration.ts:66-72 — `isArrowShapeTool` / `arrowPresetFromShapeTool`: pure string prefix parsing over the synthetic 'arrow-*' ids.

src/toolbar/systemsketch-toolbar.css:138-166 — the menu-row geometry `grid-template-columns: 22px minmax(0,1fr) auto 14px; gap:7px; min-height:34px; padding:0 8px; border-radius:7px`, plus the `kbd` (9px/700/muted) and check-column (11px/900/accent, centred) rules. Pure layout geometry with no tldraw selector in it — ports verbatim once retokened.

src/toolbar/systemsketch-toolbar.css:72-102 — the chevron-badge geometry (absolute, right:2px/bottom:2px, 13×13 grid, pointer-events:none, 9×9 inner icon) and its three-state colour ramp (rest / hover-or-open / active). Only `.tlui-icon` in the child selector is engine-bound; the geometry is portable.
mustBeReExpressed: `activeToolId` becomes a prop. Today `SystemSketchFigmaToolbar` pulls it from `editor.getCurrentToolId()` via `useValue` (:565-569) and threads it to all four family slots. It is the single input that makes a cell look pressed and makes a popout row show its ✓. ShapeFamilySlot already takes its second input as a prop (`geo`, :302, sourced at :570-574) — that is the precedent to generalize: the core takes `{activeToolId, activeVariant?}` and never asks an editor.

One shared `resolveCurrent(items, activeToolId, remembered)` replacing four hand-written resolutions. BboxFamilySlot (:443-447) is the correct form — `isBboxFamilyTool(activeToolId) ? activeToolId : preferences.lastBboxTool`, one predicate used twice. SystemFamilySlot is the failure mode the port must not carry over: a 27-line ternary chain (:355-381) and a separately-maintained 13-clause `||` for `isActive` (:383-395) over the same 13 ids. ShapeFamilySlot (:305-310) is the genuinely different case — tldraw models geo as `activeToolId==='geo'` PLUS a style value — so the shared resolver needs an optional `variantOf(activeToolId, variant)` hook, not a special-cased component.

The family registry becomes DATA the host passes in, not four compiled-in constants. Today declaring a family means editing six disjoint places (union type, validation array, `ToolbarPreferences` field + default, a `remember*Tools` wrapper in toolbarIntegration.ts, an item-list constant, and a bespoke `<XFamilySlot>` component). The port wants one declaration shaped roughly `{ id, heading, items: {id, label, icon: ReactNode, shortcut?}[], prefKey }` — every existing family already fits it: GEO+ARROW (:64-93), DRAW (:95-103), SYSTEM (:116-153), BBOX (:164-176) are four spellings of the same record, differing only in whether `icon` is typed `string | TLUiIconJsx` or `TLUiIconJsx`.

`icon` becomes `ReactNode`, full stop. The `string | TLUiIconJsx` union (:60, :169, :217, :247) exists only so stock tldraw icon names can be passed; the comment at :166-167 records the compromise verbatim: "string admits stock tldraw icon names (TextBox reuses 'tool-text' — no SystemSketch primitive owns a closer glyph), same union ToolMenuItem takes." A host-agnostic component cannot resolve a name against another library's asset registry.

Preferences become controlled, with the localStorage store demoted to an optional adapter. The component must accept either `{preferences, onPreferencesChange}` or a supplied store hook; the module singleton keyed on 'systemsketch.toolbar-preferences.v1' (toolbarModel.ts:54,157-180) cannot ship in a copy-paste component — two toolbars on one page would share one memory, and a Storybook story could not render a chosen state. Keep verbatim the two rules the store encodes: "Preferences are helpful feedback, never a reason to block drawing" (:178) and the field-independent parse fallback (:85-105).

The split-button press contract becomes explicit props. Today it is `onSelect` called from BOTH `onPointerDown` (button 0) and `onClick` (detail 0), ordered against Radix. The component should expose `onArm(itemId)` (press arms the remembered member) separately from `onOpenChange` / item `onSelect`, carrying the verbatim WHY: "Pointer activation already happened before Radix opened the menu, which lets the menu keep focus and preserve one-press Escape."

The 'press a family tile then draw immediately' promise needs a host-side escape hatch, not CSS that reaches into the engine. Today it is `.systemsketch-app:has(.systemsketch-family-tool[data-state='open']) .tlui-menu-click-capture { pointer-events: none }` (css:110-112). The component can only offer the signal — e.g. a stable `data-state='open'` on the trigger and a documented `data-bbox-family-open` hook — and the host writes its own capture-layer rule. The verbatim WHY (css:104-109) must land in the component's docs so a future host knows why the hook exists.

A contextual FOOTER slot for the popout. SystemFamilySlot's 'Add leader to selected Callout' row (:416-430) appears only when `editor.getOnlySelectedShape()` is an unlocked Callout card and calls `startAddingCalloutLeader(editor, id)`. This must become `footer?: ReactNode` (or `extraItems?: MenuItem[]`) on the family slot — selection state and editor commands are host-owned and never travel.

The '+' library cell becomes a generic popover slot. `LibrarySlot` (:499-552) must reduce to a trigger + `TldrawUiPopover`-equivalent taking `children`, `open`/`onOpenChange`, a title/eyebrow header and a close button. `editor.menus.clearOpenMenus()` (:505) moves into the host's `onOpenChange`; `onWheel` stopPropagation (:535) becomes either a documented default or a host escape hatch; `ShapeLibraryBrowser` is entirely the host's content. The leading divider is CSS on the wrapper (css:168-174) and should become an explicit `<Separator/>` child so the bar's composition is readable.

Responsive overflow must stop being measured. `DefaultToolbar minItems={4} maxItems={8} minSizePx={255} maxSizePx={380}` (:577) is tldraw measuring the bar. The core should render a plain flex row of cells, exposing at most a declarative `overflowAfter?: number` plus an overflow-menu slot, and let the host decide breakpoints (SystemSketch already hardcodes its own at `@media (max-width: 620px)`, css:323-339).

`SimpleToolSlot`'s props must stop carrying `TLUiToolItem`. It currently takes `tool: TLUiToolItem | undefined` and derives `disabled`, `icon` and the click handler from it (:214-243). Re-express as `{icon: ReactNode, label, active, disabled?, disabledTitle?, onSelect()}` — the disabled/`disabledTitle` pair ("`${title} is unavailable`", :232) and the `opacity:.38` treatment (css:68-70) are worth keeping verbatim.

Test hooks must become explicit props, not derived from display text. `data-value`/`data-testid` are built as `systemsketch-${title.toLowerCase()}` (:233-234) and `systemsketch-tool-${family}` (:269-272); the e2e smoke test depends on them (tests/toolbar_family_menu_smoke.mjs:50,60,106,134,189,201). A portable component should take an explicit `id`/`testId` so a rename of visible copy cannot break a consumer's tests.

The keyboard-shortcut hints are DISPLAY-ONLY strings in the component ('R', 'C / O', 'L', 'B', 'P', 'D', '⇧ D', 'A', 'A × 2', 'A × 3'), while the actual keys are bound by tldraw's `kbd` fields inside the overrides (toolbarIntegration.ts wrapping + each `with*Tool` factory; toolbarIntegration.test.ts:96-115 asserts Block claims 'b' and Draw releases it). That split is fine for a host-agnostic component — hints are props — but the port must record that the hint is not the binding, or the two will drift. The one exception is the arrow hints, which ARE derived (see arrowPresetPressCount) and should stay derived.

The tldraw-only half of `ArrowPreset` must be stripped from the model. `ArrowPreset` and its press-count algebra are portable; `ARROW_PRESET_ROUTING`'s `ConnectionRoutingKind` binding (toolbarModel.ts:3,118-122) and everything in `applyArrowPreset`/`applyArrowPresetToSelection`/`registerToolbarSideEffects` are host wiring. The verbatim WHY that has to survive the split is toolbarModel.ts:38-44: "Elbow is the datum, for arrows and for data edges alike. / \"That is the most common one we use\" — so a fresh install draws an elbow before anyone has touched a control, and `lastArrowPreset` is the single value both the arrow tool and the edge layer read to know what that means." — i.e. the DEFAULT is a product decision the component must let a host state, and the 'one preference, two subjects' idea is the host's to honour.
openQuestions: Does the ported toolbar own an overflow menu at all? `DefaultToolbar`'s measured collapse (:577) plus the overflow-content CSS (css:314-321) is real shipped behavior, but it is self-measurement. Options: drop it (host wraps), expose a declarative `overflowAfter`, or ship a `useResizeObserver`-based variant explicitly marked host-side. Unresolved.

Does ShapeFamilySlot's tool-plus-style resolution (`activeToolId==='geo'` AND a separate `geo` variant, :308) generalize into the family registry, or does it stay a documented special case? It is the only family whose members are not 1:1 with tool ids, and it is also the only one whose synthetic ids ('arrow-straight' etc) get remapped at dispatch (toolbarIntegration.ts:444-453).

Do the three-section popouts (Shapes / separator / Arrows, :320-338) mean a family declares SECTIONS rather than a flat item list? Today only ShapeFamilySlot has two headings, and only SystemFamilySlot has a footer — a flat `items[]` plus optional `footer` covers both, but a `sections[]` shape would cover them uniformly. Not decided by the existing code.

How does the ported component express 'the popout row is selected' vs 'the bar cell is active' when both currently key off the same `data-isactive` attribute (row: :200 + css:149-152; cell: css:57-66)? Two different visual treatments (accent-soft tint vs solid accent fill) on one attribute name is a trap for a copy-paste consumer.

Is the `select` cell's blue fill a genuine 'active tool' state or a 'select is the resting tool' default? The screenshot shows cell 1 filled, and `active={activeToolId==='select'}` (:578) says it is just the active-tool paint — but nothing in the toolbar marks select as special, so a host that starts on a different tool gets no filled cell at all. Worth confirming that is intended before freezing the visual.

`packages/bbox-ui` already vendors a `dropdown-menu` and `tooltip` (stock shadcn new-york, per the repo CLAUDE.md), and this surface needs both plus a popover. Does the ported toolbar depend on those registry items (making it the first bbox item with `registryDependencies`), or inline its own menu primitive to keep the repo's 'no registryDependencies between bbox items' rule? The CLAUDE.md rule and this surface's needs collide.

The e2e smoke test (tests/toolbar_family_menu_smoke.mjs, 261 lines) asserts on `data-state`, `aria-pressed` and which inner button is focused after opening a family menu (:134-138, :189, :201). Which of those assertions are about the COMPONENT (focus order, aria, open state) and which are about tldraw's menu layer? Not separable without running it, and this was read-only reconnaissance.

Nothing in `SystemSketchToolbar.tsx` is unit-tested — both test files cover `toolbarModel.ts` and `toolbarIntegration.ts` only. So the split-button press semantics (:273-280), the current-member resolution chains (:305-310, :355-381, :443-447, :474), and the Callout footer condition (:347-354) have no characterization tests to port against. Those behaviors will have to be re-derived from the source rather than pinned by an existing suite.

surveys.surface: Top-left chrome bar — burger · divider · back/forward · home+breadcrumb · draft (branch) chip · depth count badge. Rendered by `SystemSketchTitleBar` (`chrome/TitleBar.tsx:344`), installed as tldraw's `MenuPanel` seam via `SystemSketchMenuPanel` (`chrome/SystemSketchChrome.tsx:158-180`). anatomy.description: `Toolbar.Root` from Base UI carrying `.systemsketch-top-left-shell .systemsketch-title-bar`. Flex row, `height: var(--systemsketch-top-height)`, 4px padding, 1px `--ss-border`, `border-radius: 15px`, `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ss-surface-raised) 96%, transparent)` background, `--ss-shadow-1`, `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)`, `z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)`, `max-width: calc(100vw - 230px)`. `aria-label="Board and depth navigation"`, `data-depth={model.depth}`. Zach's WHY for choosing `Toolbar.Root` over three sibling components is quoted in `engineCoupling` notes below — it buys one owner for the dividers plus free roving arrow-key focus.

`<SystemSketchFileMenu identity={identity} />` — tldraw's `DefaultMainMenu` with a File submenu (New / New window / Open… / Open recent → recents list / Save / Save As… / Export to tldraw… / Rename F2 / Copy Absolute Path / Show in Files / Move to Trash…) plus a Settings row above `DefaultMainMenuContent`. Rendered identically in both the legacy pill and V2; only what sits beside it differs.

`Toolbar.Separator` rendering shadcn `Separator orientation="vertical"`, `mx-1 h-6 w-px shrink-0 self-center bg-border`. One after the burger, one after the history group. No separator between the file crumb and the branch chip — deliberate.

shadcn `ButtonGroup aria-label="Navigation history"` holding two `Tooltip`-wrapped `Toolbar.Button render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm">}` with lucide `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`. `disabled={!snapshot.canGoBack/ canGoForward}`; tooltips read "Back to previous view" / "Forward to next view". These are DEPTH history (scope + camera + selection journal), not undo/redo — the app has no undo/redo control in this bar.

shadcn `Breadcrumb` → `BreadcrumbList` forced to `m-0 list-none flex-nowrap gap-1 p-0 text-xs` (Tailwind preflight is not loaded; without these the `<ol>` keeps UA markers, 1em margins and a measured 40px `padding-inline-start` dead run). Children in order: FileCrumb, DraftChip, then one `BreadcrumbSeparator` + segment per compacted depth level.

anatomy.part: FileCrumb (home icon + document name + status dot)
anatomy.description: A `BreadcrumbItem` holding (a) the Home target — a non-interactive `BreadcrumbPage` with a `Home` glyph when `atRoot`, otherwise a tooltipped ghost icon button calling `returnToDepthRoot`; and (b) the document name as a `DropdownMenuTrigger` nested inside a `ContextMenuTrigger`. Left click = file menu, double click = inline rename, right click = context menu with Rename hoisted to the top. `<i data-state={identity.statusKind}>` is the 6px status dot: `--ss-success` clean, `--ss-warning` dirty/saving, `--ss-danger` conflict/missing/future/quarantined/error. Width `min(24vw, 210px)`, inner `truncate` span draws the ellipsis, full name stays on `title`.

One `FileAction[]` (`{id,label,shortcut?,disabled?,destructive?,run()}`) renders into both the dropdown and the context menu so they cannot drift. Rows: Return to board root (disabled at root), Rename (F2), Save As…, Copy Absolute Path (disabled without a path), Show in Files, Move to Trash… (destructive, disabled when not persisted). `FileActionIcon` maps id → lucide glyph. Both menus wrap their rows in a `*MenuGroup` because shadcn's `*MenuLabel` is Base UI `Menu.GroupLabel`, which throws and takes the whole canvas down with tldraw's error screen if no Group is above it.

`SystemSketchFileTitleEditor` swaps in for the name while `identity.isRenamingInline`. Same footprint (28px in this bar) so the chrome never jumps. Enter commits, Escape cancels, helper text doubles as the error slot, status dot repeats at the end.

`<DraftsControl renderTrigger={…} />` inside a `BreadcrumbItem`. The trigger is `Toolbar.Button render={<Button variant="outline" size="sm">}`, `h-7 gap-1.5 px-2 text-inherit`, holding lucide `GitBranch` + a `max-w-32 truncate` label (`activeDraftName ?? 'Main'`) + a secondary `Badge` with `draftCount` when > 0 + a 60%-opacity `ChevronDown`. `data-active` is set to `isDraftMode || undefined` — never the string `"false"` — because both the CSS and the journeys treat it as a presence test. Active state paints `border-color: var(--ss-accent)`, `background: var(--ss-accent-soft)`, ink stays `--ss-text`.

Radix `Popover.Content sideOffset={8} align="start" collisionPadding={14}` portaled into `.systemsketch-theme-root`. Header "Drafts"; a Main row (`data-current={activeDraftId === null}`); one `DraftRow` per draft; a "New draft" footer button. Each row: a current-marker ``, `name` + `` secondary label, and a hover-revealed action pair (pencil → inline rename, trash → two-step "Discard?" confirm that resets on blur).

Local `InlineRename`: autofocus + select on mount, Enter commits (empty → "Give this draft a name."), Escape cancels AND `stopPropagation`s so Radix's dismissable-layer handler does not close the whole popover, blur commits, and a `mousedown` within 400 ms of mount is `preventDefault`ed so a habitual double-click's second click does not collapse the selection to a caret. Focus returns to the pencil button on close.

When `compactDepthBreadcrumbs` elides levels, the `…` becomes a real `DropdownMenu` labelled "Hidden levels" whose rows jump to each skipped ancestor (`stepToDepthAncestor`), disabled with an explanatory `title` when the ancestor is not Expanded, depth number in the shortcut slot. `segmentBreadcrumbs` recovers the actual hidden entries from the compactor's `hiddenCount`, which only reports how many were dropped.

Current level = `BreadcrumbPage h-6 max-w-56 px-2 font-medium` with the ellipsis on an inner span (truncate on the flex box itself clips mid-glyph with no "…" — measured). Ancestor level = `BreadcrumbLink` rendered through `Toolbar.Button`/ghost `Button size="xs"`, `max-w-40 truncate`, click → `stepToDepthAncestor`. Raw name always on `title`.

A secondary `Badge` rendered as a `Toolbar.Button` that is itself a `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `ml-1 shrink-0 cursor-default tabular-nums`, showing `model.depth`. Its menu is the structural path: a label `Structural path · N level(s)`, a Home row for the board root (checked + disabled at root, shortcut "0"), then one row per `DepthPathEntry` with a `Check` on the current level and the depth number in the shortcut slot.
`Current scope: {currentName}, depth {model.depth}` — the only announcement of a depth change.

surveys.dataModel:
Four independent models feed this one bar; none of them is a single prop object today.

1. DEPTH — `depth/depthNavigation.ts:9-29`
   `DepthNavigationSnapshot { scopeId: TLShapeId | null; canGoBack: boolean; canGoForward: boolean }`
   `DepthPathEntry { id: TLShapeId; name: string; depth: number; canFocus: boolean; isCurrent: boolean }`
   `DepthNavigationModel { pageId: TLPageId; pageName: string; current: BlockShape | null; entries: DepthPathEntry[]; depth: number; parent: DepthPathEntry | null }`
   `pageName` is the hard-coded literal `'Board'` (`depthNavigation.ts:427`), NOT the file name — the board name shown in the crumb comes from `identity.title`, not from the depth model. `current` is a live `BlockShape` (a tldraw record), so `DepthNavigationModel` cannot cross the core boundary unchanged.
   Commands: `goBackInDepthHistory`, `goForwardInDepthHistory`, `returnToDepthRoot`, `stepToDepthAncestor` — all `(editor, …) => boolean` (`:506, :521, :499, :475`).

2. BREADCRUMB COMPACTION — `depth/depthBreadcrumbs.ts:1-8`
   `DepthBreadcrumbItem { kind?: never; id: string; name: string; isCurrent: boolean }`
   `CompactDepthBreadcrumbItem<Entry> = Entry | { kind: 'elision'; hiddenCount: number }`
   `compactDepthBreadcrumbs<Entry>(rootName: string, entries: readonly Entry[], budget = 150): CompactDepthBreadcrumbItem<Entry>[]` — generic over any item with `{id,name,isCurrent}`, zero tldraw. `TitleBar.tsx:136-160` adds the bar-local `CrumbSegment = { kind:'entry'; entry } | { kind:'elision'; hidden: DepthPathEntry[] }` and `segmentBreadcrumbs()` to re-hydrate the hidden run from `hiddenCount`.

3. DOCUMENT IDENTITY — `workspace/LocalWorkspace.tsx:1364-1520`
   `type DocumentIdentity = ReturnType<typeof useDocumentIdentity>`, a 20-field bag mixing state and commands: `{ title, path, statusKind, statusLabel, renameNeedsCopy, isRenamingInline, renameDraft, renameError, renameBusy, titleInputRef, beginInlineRename, cancelInlineRename, commitInlineRename, setRenameDraft, requestTrash, reveal, copyPath, saveAs, isPersisted }`. `statusKind` ranges over `clean | saving | dirty | conflict | missing | quarantined | future | error | opening` (label map at `:1404-1421`), and that enum is exactly what the status dot's three-colour CSS table keys off.

4. DRAFTS — `drafts/draftModel.ts:37-61`, `drafts/DraftProvider.tsx:108-160`
   `DraftRecord { id; name; baseLabel; baseDigest: string | null; createdAt; updatedAt }`
   `VersionRecord { id; label; name; createdAt; note? }`
   `DocumentDraftState { version: 1; activeDraftId: string | null; drafts; versions }`
   `DraftContextValue` is much wider than the chip needs — it also carries `changes: BoardCompare`, `hasConflict`, `hasUnpromotedEdits`, `merge`, `rebaseDraftAction`, `previewRebase`, `getCompareSnapshots`, `attachEditor(editor)`. The chip and popover use only `{ activeDraft, activeDraftId, drafts, isDraftMode, switchTo, createDraftAction, renameDraftAction, discard, versions }`.
   `DraftsControl`'s render-prop state is already the narrow contract the bar wants: `{ isDraftMode: boolean; draftCount: number; activeDraftName: string | null }` (`DraftsControl.tsx:231-235`).

Shared helper: `storedTextOr(value, fallback)` (`textFidelity.ts:7`) — every label that crosses into the chrome goes through it; `relativeTime(timestamp, now = Date.now())` (`history/historyModel.ts:75`) supplies the draft row's \"based on Main · 3 hours ago\".

engineCoupling.what: `const editor = useEditor()` — the component's root dependency. Every command (`goBackInDepthHistory`, `returnToDepthRoot`, `stepToDepthAncestor`) is called as `fn(editor, …)`. Must become callbacks: `onBack`, `onForward`, `onReturnToRoot`, `onJumpToLevel(id)`.

`useSyncExternalStore(subscribeDepthNavigation(editor,…), getDepthNavigationSnapshot(editor))` plus tldraw's `useValue('SystemSketch depth navigation model', () => getDepthNavigationModel(editor, snapshot.scopeId))`. The bar subscribes to a tldraw-keyed WeakMap store. Both must collapse into one plain prop: `{ crumbs, depth, canGoBack, canGoForward }`.
`usePassThroughWheelEvents(ref)` from tldraw — stops chrome wheel events reaching the canvas. Pure host concern; drop it from the core and let the adapter attach it to the shell's ref.

`useDepthHistoryInputs(editor, ref, snapshot)` installs FOUR capture-phase listeners on `rootRef.current.ownerDocument`: `mouseup` (unconditionally `preventDefault`s buttons 3/4), `keydown` (BrowserBack/GoBack/BrowserForward/GoForward), `pointerdown` (buttons 3/4). This is document-wide interaction geometry — it cannot travel. The core exposes `onBack`/`onForward`; the host keeps the hook.

`themeRoot()` — `document.querySelector('.systemsketch-theme-root')` at render time, handed to every `container=` prop so Base UI popups portal inside the `--ss-*` token scope instead of `<body>`. Direct DOM measurement/lookup. Must become a `portalContainer?: HTMLElement` prop (or be left entirely to the host's menu primitives).
A second, independent copy of the same `document.querySelector('.systemsketch-theme-root')` for the Radix popover's `Popover.Portal container`. Same fix, and porting is the moment to stop having two.

`isLegacyTitleBarEnabled()` reads `window.location.search` for `?title-bar=legacy`, resolved once at module scope in `SystemSketchChrome.tsx:135`. A URL feature flag — SystemSketch-specific scaffolding for the V1/V2 comparison; it does not port at all.

The burger IS tldraw: `DefaultMainMenu`, `DefaultMainMenuContent`, `TldrawUiMenuGroup`, `TldrawUiMenuSubmenu`, `TldrawUiMenuItem`, plus `useDialogs()` for the Settings dialog. Nothing about this element is portable today — the port needs a host-agnostic menu built on the trunk's own `dropdown-menu.tsx`, taking a declarative `items` tree (labels, `kbd`, `disabled`, `onSelect`, nested groups/submenus) as a prop.

`useDocumentIdentity()` calls `useLocalWorkspace()` (throws outside its provider), `useConfirm()` and `useToasts()`. Three ambient providers behind what looks like a display prop. The core must take `title`, `statusKind`, `statusLabel`, `path` as data and `onRename`, `onSaveAs`, `onCopyPath`, `onReveal`, `onTrash` as callbacks; confirmation and toasts belong to the host.

`restoreTitleFocus()` — `document.querySelector('[data-testid="systemsketch-file-title"]')?.focus()` inside a `requestAnimationFrame`. A global DOM lookup by test id to restore focus after a rename. Replace with a ref the component already owns.

The F2 shortcut is a `window.addEventListener('keydown')` living inside `useDocumentIdentity`, with the documented constraint "Mount it ONCE per bar: the F2 listener lives in here, so a second live instance would answer one keypress with two rename editors." A global key binding is host-owned; the core exposes `onBeginRename` and the host wires F2.
`copyPath()` uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText` and fires a toast on success/failure. Platform API + provider. Becomes `onCopyPath()` on the host side.

The inline rename field is `SystemSketchUiInput`, which wraps tldraw's `TldrawUiInput` (focus, select-on-entry, IME, Enter/Escape, iOS scrolling). The trunk already ships `editableText.tsx`; the port has to re-express the same commit/cancel contract through it rather than import tldraw.

`useDrafts()` throws outside `DraftProvider`; `DraftProvider` itself imports `loadSnapshot`/`serializeTldrawJson` from tldraw, holds an `editorRef`, writes debounced snapshots to localStorage and reads fresh Main off disk (`DraftProvider.tsx:29, :159, :170-179`). The chip must take `{ isDraftMode, draftCount, activeDraftName, drafts, activeDraftId }` as props and `onSwitchTo / onCreate / onRename / onDiscard` as callbacks.

The popover is Radix (`@radix-ui/react-popover`) while the bar around it is Base UI — two popup engines in one 30-pixel-wide seam. The port should pick one; the trunk already vendors Base-UI-flavoured `dropdown-menu.tsx`/`tooltip.tsx`.

`performance.now()` mount-time guard (`RENAME_MOUSEDOWN_GUARD_MS = 400`) plus `event.preventDefault()` on `mousedown` — real pointer interaction, but purely local to the input and not canvas geometry. Ports as-is.

`event.stopPropagation()` on Escape to stop Radix's dismissable-layer closing the whole popover. Engine-specific workaround; whichever popup engine the trunk picks needs the equivalent, and the WHY must survive.

`.systemsketch-title-bar-popup { z-index: var(--systemsketch-layer-modal, 500) }` — a z-index applied to every popup positioner, with a documented reason (shadcn's generated content opens an `isolate z-50` stacking context, so a z-index on the popup inside it can never rise above the canvas). The core forbids z-index; this becomes a host-supplied `positionerClassName`/`popupClassName` prop.

The shell's own `z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)` and `max-width: calc(100vw - 230px)` — a tldraw layer variable and a hard-coded reservation for the right cluster's width. Both are host placement, not component style.

Every rule doubles up `.systemsketch-top-left-shell.systemsketch-title-bar` purely to out-specify `systemsketch-chrome.css`, and `:60-66` restyles `.tlui-button` (tldraw's own 40px button) down to the 28px rung. Specificity warfare against sheets that will not exist in the trunk — delete, do not port.

`const GHOST = 'bg-transparent text-inherit'` and the `list-none m-0 p-0` on `BreadcrumbList` exist only because this app loads Tailwind's theme+utilities but NOT preflight (preflight repaints ~12% of the tldraw canvas). In a normal Tailwind app these are unnecessary; in the trunk they must be re-evaluated rather than copied blind.

`ContextMenuTrigger` wraps the `DropdownMenu` in a `display:contents` span because both Base UI triggers resolve their store from the NEAREST `MenuRootContext` — composing them on one element silently binds both to the inner root (measured: left click toggled the context menu's store, file menu never opened). Pure Base UI mechanics; ports with the engine choice, and the WHY must travel.

shadcn's `*MenuLabel` is Base UI `Menu.GroupLabel`, which THROWS — taking the whole canvas down with tldraw's error screen — unless a `Menu.Group` is above it. The tldraw error screen is the host's; the throw is the engine's. Keep the Group wrappers and the comment.
`storedTextOr(...)` guards every stored label. Pure, engine-free, and it encodes the truthful-property-rendering rule — port verbatim.

Placement: `SystemSketchMenuPanel` is handed to tldraw as the `MenuPanel` component and `tests/test_stock_boundary.py` asserts that seam list literally. The bar never positions itself — tldraw's layout does. Same for `SystemSketchSharePanel` as `SharePanel`.

The right cluster is built from `TldrawUiButton` / `TldrawUiPopover` / `useEditor()` / `useDialogs()` throughout, plus `exportPortableTldraw(editor)` and a `document.createElement('a')` download. Every control is engine-bound; only the visual grammar (30px circular avatar, icon row, one primary button) ports.

(Frames panel, adjacent surface.) `useEditor`/`useValue`, `editor.updateShape`, `editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint`, and `event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect()` for drop placement — self-measurement plus direct store mutation. Noted here only because it was in the read list; it belongs to the frames-panel lane.

reusableAsIs: `depth/depthBreadcrumbs.ts:1-58` — `compactDepthBreadcrumbs` in full. Zero imports of any kind. Generic over `Entry extends {id,name,isCurrent}`, takes `(rootName, entries, budget = 150)` and returns entries interleaved with `{kind:'elision',hiddenCount}`. It counts characters (`SEPARATOR_LENGTH = 3` for ` › `) and deletes from level 1 forward, never the last two. Ports verbatim, and `depthBreadcrumbs.test.ts:1-51` ports with it as the oracle.

`chrome/TitleBar.tsx:130-160` — `isElision()` and `segmentBreadcrumbs()`. Pure array arithmetic that re-hydrates each elision's hidden run from the compactor's `hiddenCount` by walking a cursor through the source order. No React, no tldraw. The only change on the way over is the element type (`DepthPathEntry` → whatever crumb shape the component defines).

`textFidelity.ts:1-9` — `storedTextOr`. Nine lines, no imports, and it is the executable form of Zach's truthful-property-rendering rule. Everything that renders a stored label in this surface already routes through it.

`history/historyModel.ts:75-98` — `relativeTime(timestamp, now = Date.now())`. Pure, injectable clock, handles null/non-finite and clock skew (`< 45_000` → 'just now'). Used by the draft popover's secondary label; the trunk has no equivalent.

`chrome/TitleBar.tsx:162-181` — the `FileAction` type and `FileActionIcon` switch. The type (`{id,label,shortcut?,disabled?,destructive?,run()}`) is already the declarative menu-row contract a portable menu wants, and it is precisely what keeps the dropdown and context menu from drifting. The icon switch is a pure id→lucide map.

`chrome/TitleBar.tsx:369-382` — the `actions` array's SHAPE (six rows, their labels, shortcuts, disabled predicates and destructive flag). The `run()` bodies are editor/identity-bound, but the row table is the product decision and is worth porting as a default `items` fixture for the story.

`drafts/DraftsControl.tsx:146-154` — the `secondaryLabel` derivation. Pure conditional on `versions.length`, and it carries a real correctness note: `draft.baseLabel` is fabricated until a version is actually pinned, so it shows the truthful creation-time form instead.

`workspace/LocalWorkspace.tsx:1404-1421` — the `statusKind` → `statusLabel` map. A pure nine-branch expression; the matching three-colour dot table is `workspace/local-workspace.css:34-60`. Together they are the whole StatusDot component, engine-free.
mustBeReExpressed: Depth state as one plain prop. Today: `useSyncExternalStore` + tldraw `useValue` against an editor-keyed WeakMap (`TitleBar.tsx:350-357`). Needs: `crumbs: Crumb[]` (`{id, name, isCurrent, canFocus, depth}` — plain strings, no `TLShapeId`), `depth: number`, `canGoBack`, `canGoForward`. Note `model.pageName` is the literal `'Board'` (`depthNavigation.ts:427`) while the visible board name is `identity.title` — the port must not conflate them.

Every navigation command as a callback. `goBackInDepthHistory(editor)` / `goForwardInDepthHistory(editor)` / `returnToDepthRoot(editor)` / `stepToDepthAncestor(editor, id)` → `onBack()`, `onForward()`, `onReturnToRoot()`, `onJumpToLevel(id)`. All four currently return `boolean`; the component ignores every return value (`void`-prefixed at `:370, :417, :430, :456, :531, :562, :601, :614`), so the prop type can be `() => void`.

Global input gestures leave the component. `useDepthHistoryInputs` (mouse buttons 3/4, BrowserBack/Forward keys, four capture-phase document listeners) and the F2 `window` keydown inside `useDocumentIdentity` both become host wiring against the same callbacks. Preserve the measured WHY: only `mouseup` cancels mouse-button navigation in real Chrome, and the gesture is swallowed unconditionally because at the ends of the journal Chrome would otherwise leave the board entirely.

The burger becomes a declarative menu. `DefaultMainMenu` + `TldrawUiMenuSubmenu`/`TldrawUiMenuItem`/`useDialogs()` → a `MenuSpec` tree of groups, items, submenus, `kbd` strings, `disabled` predicates and `onSelect` callbacks, rendered through the trunk's own `dropdown-menu.tsx`. The `FileAction` type at `TitleBar.tsx:163-170` is already most of that contract; generalise it to nest.

Document identity becomes data + callbacks. `DocumentIdentity` (a 20-field hook bag reaching `useLocalWorkspace`/`useConfirm`/`useToasts`) → `{ title, statusKind, statusLabel, path? }` in, and `onBeginRename / onCommitRename(next) / onCancelRename / onSaveAs / onCopyPath / onReveal / onTrash` out. Rename EDIT state (`isRenamingInline`, `renameDraft`, `renameError`, `renameBusy`) can be controlled-or-uncontrolled inside the component; the async commit and its failure message stay the host's.

Drafts become props on the chip. `useDrafts()` (throws outside `DraftProvider`, which holds an editorRef, writes localStorage and reads disk) → `{ activeDraftName: string | null, draftCount: number, isDraftMode: boolean, drafts: DraftSummary[], activeDraftId }` plus `onSwitchTo(id | null)`, `onCreate()`, `onRename(id, name)`, `onDiscard(id)`. `DraftsControl`'s existing `renderTrigger` state (`{isDraftMode, draftCount, activeDraftName}`) is already the right shape — keep the render-prop seam, it is what let the shipped pill and V2 share one popover.

Portal container and popup layering become props. `themeRoot()`'s `document.querySelector` (twice) → `portalContainer?: HTMLElement`, and `.systemsketch-title-bar-popup`'s `z-index: var(--systemsketch-layer-modal, 500)` → a host-supplied `popupClassName`. The core must not query the DOM and must not set z-index.

One popup engine, not two. Base UI (bar, menus, tooltips) beside Radix (drafts popover) is an accident of history. Pick the trunk's engine; carry over the engine-specific fixes that were paid for in measurement: the `display:contents` ContextMenu/DropdownMenu nesting (`TitleBar.tsx:267-276`), the mandatory `*MenuGroup` above every `*MenuLabel` (`:319-322, :519-523`), and Escape's `stopPropagation` inside the rename input (`DraftsControl.tsx:99-106`).

Tailwind assumptions get re-checked, not copied. `GHOST = 'bg-transparent text-inherit'`, `text-inherit` on the draft chip, and `list-none m-0 p-0` on the breadcrumb list exist ONLY because this app omits Tailwind preflight (it repaints ~12% of the tldraw canvas). The trunk's Tailwind setup is different; these are compensations for an absent reset, not styling decisions.

Colours move from `--ss-*` to the trunk's tokens. The draft-active tint (`--ss-accent` border on `--ss-accent-soft`, ink stays `--ss-text`) and the three-state dot (`--ss-success` / `--ss-warning` / `--ss-danger`) carry a measured accessibility rule: accent-on-accent-soft measures 2.6–4.3:1 in every palette here, so copy on a tint is ink plus an accent edge, never accent copy. That rule must survive the token rename.

The shell stops placing itself. `position: relative; z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels); max-width: calc(100vw - 230px); margin: var(--systemsketch-chrome-inset) …` (`systemsketch-chrome.css:4-26`) is tldraw-layout coupling. The component owns its own internal rhythm (the 28px rung, 2px gap, 6px inline padding, 15px radius, blur) and nothing about where it sits.

`data-active` stays a presence test. `data-active={isDraftMode || undefined}` — never `false` — because both the CSS and the journeys treat it as presence and `data-active="false"` would light the chip up (`TitleBar.tsx:484-488`). Any port that writes the boolean straight through silently inverts the state.
openQuestions: Does the bar port as ONE `ChromeBar` component or as a composable set (`ChromeBar` shell + `ChromeMenuButton` + `HistoryButtons` + `PathBreadcrumb` + `BranchChip` + `CountBadge`) that a host arranges? SystemSketch's own WHY argues for a shell that owns the dividers and roving focus (`TitleBar.tsx:18-24`), which points at slot-based composition rather than one monolith — but the trunk has no `Toolbar.Root` equivalent today.

Which popup engine does the trunk adopt? `apps/storybook-basics/src/components/` already has `dropdown-menu.tsx` and `tooltip.tsx` but NO breadcrumb, separator, button-group, context-menu, popover or toolbar. Four to six new stock shadcn primitives have to land before this surface can be expressed, and that choice decides which of the measured Base-UI/Radix workarounds travel.

Does the depth breadcrumb belong in bbox-ui at all, or is `compactDepthBreadcrumbs` + `segmentBreadcrumbs` a pure `lib/` algorithm with a generic `Breadcrumb` component above it? The compaction is genuinely reusable; "depth" as a concept is SystemSketch's.

Is the branch/draft chip a bbox-ui component or a SystemSketch app control? The chip itself is generic (glyph + label + count badge + chevron + active tint); the popover it opens is thick with drafts semantics — Main row, fork-point labels, two-step discard, `baseLabel` fabrication guard. A `BranchChip` trigger plus a host-supplied popover body may be the honest split.

How does the status dot's nine-state `statusKind` enum port? It is workspace-save vocabulary (`clean/saving/dirty/conflict/missing/quarantined/future/error/opening`), not canvas vocabulary. Either the component takes an opaque `tone: 'ok' | 'pending' | 'error'` plus a label, or the enum travels and becomes bbox-ui's business.

The right cluster (avatar / compare / panel toggle / Share) was not in this survey's file list and is a distinct tldraw seam (`SharePanel`). Is it a second component in this same port, or a separate lane? It shares the shell CSS with the left bar (`systemsketch-chrome.css:4-18`), so whoever ports the shell touches both.

The trunk has `editableText.tsx`; does the file-name rename reuse it, or does the bar need its own field? The current one wraps tldraw's `TldrawUiInput` specifically for IME composition and iOS scrolling — is that behaviour already in `editableText.tsx`, and if not, is losing it acceptable?

Nothing in this surface is undo/redo. The back/forward arrows are a camera+scope+selection journal (`depthNavigation.ts:32-37, 506-537`), and `history/` is version-file diffing. If a future host wants real undo/redo in the same slot, is the component's prop contract (`canGoBack`/`onBack`) neutral enough to serve both, or should it be named for navigation explicitly?
