anatomy.description: The floating dark column itself. Fixed id `systemsketch-right-popout`, aria-label = the panel title, `data-surface={rightSurface}` so CSS and tests can key on which panel is inside, `data-systemsketch-chrome`, and `onWheel={e => e.stopPropagation()}` so the canvas never scrolls under it. Positioned absolutely inside `.systemsketch-surface-host` (an inset-0 pointer-events:none layer at SystemSketchChrome.tsx:1076), pinned to the right inset, top = chrome inset + top bar height + 12px, bottom = bottom clearance, width min(316px, 100vw - 2*inset), radius var(--systemsketch-panel-radius), 1px border, blurred 97%-opaque raised surface, --ss-shadow-2, and a 150ms enter animation (disabled under prefers-reduced-motion).

Three visual elements in a flex row: the EYEBROW (a <span> rendering the literal string "Right panel", CSS-uppercased to "RIGHT PANEL" at 8px/850-weight/.12em tracking), the TITLE (<h2>, 15px), and the CLOSE X (a <button> whose text content is the character ×, aria-label=`Close ${rightTitle}`). min-height 58px, 13/14/11px padding, bottom border. Note: the stylesheet styles EVERY button inside this header as a 30×30 icon square (171-184) — SystemSketchChrome.tsx:1119-1122 records that as a constraint, verbatim: "WHY the switcher sits below the header rather than inside it: `systemsketch-chrome.css` styles EVERY `button` in `.systemsketch-popout__header` as a 30×30 icon square, which would squash a labelled tab into an unreadable chip."

A plain 5-arm ternary mapping RightSurface → title string: 'board-overview'→"Frames", 'diagnostics'→"Problems", 'variable-registry'→"Variables", 'inspector'→inspectorSubjectTitle(subject), else "Comments". The registry of surfaces is this ternary plus the union type — there is no table, no registration API.

A second if-chain mapping the same RightSurface union to a component: 'board-overview'→<BoardOverview/> (takes no props at all — it reaches for the editor itself), 'diagnostics'→<BoardDiagnosticsPanel editor/>, 'variable-registry'→<VariableRegistryPanel editor/>, 'inspector'→<InspectorDock editor subject onClose/>, fallback <LocalCommentsPanel editor readOnly/>. So "registering a panel" = adding a string to the union in chromeState.ts:7, an arm to rightTitle, and an arm here.

The shell can hand its header to the body. `data-inspector-header` is set to 'body' or 'frame' from inspectorSubjectOwnsHeader(subject) — only for the inspector surface. Verbatim comment: "Which element draws the header, and the stylesheet obeys it rather than repeating the list. `body` means the panel below supplies its own title and close button; `frame` means it does not, and the dock's header stays. Before this the inspector hid the header for every subject, which left a cable, an ordinary shape and an empty selection in a headerless column with no pointer way out." The inverse taste is recorded at ShapeFactsPanel.tsx:122-124: "No eyebrow: the dock's own header already reads \"Right panel / Selection\" directly above this, and repeating the word is the same double-titling the Comments panel has. The kind is the new fact."

The scroll container for the panel content: flex:1, min-height:0, padding 10px, overflow-y:auto, overscroll-behavior:contain. Two classes on one element — `board-overview` supplies scroll/padding, `frames-panel` supplies every visual rule.

The second, inner header the screenshot shows: eyebrow "Board navigation" (CSS-uppercased, 750-weight, .07em tracking),

"Frames"

at 14px, and {items.length} items — this is the "46 items" count, a raw `model.items.length` with no singular form. Right-aligned beside it is the view-options control.

The button on the header's right (glyph ☷, aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded, aria-label "Frames panel view options"). Opened state is local React `menuOpen`; the popup is a hand-rolled absolutely-positioned div[role=menu] at top:31px/right:0 holding two role=menuitemradio buttons: "Thumbnail cards" and "Compact list". Picking one sets `mode` and closes. There is no outside-click or Escape dismissal — only re-clicking the trigger or choosing an item closes it.
One 10px muted sentence, hardcoded: "Frames, regions, and saved camera views in one navigable order."

A <form> with label "Save current camera view" (9px/750, block), an <input id=systemsketch-landmark-name maxLength=80> pre-filled with the suggested name ("View 1", "View 2"…), and a submit <button>Save</button> (min 45×29, --ss-accent background, --ss-text-inverse ink — this is the blue button in the screenshot). Both are disabled when `landmarkMutationLocked`. Submit calls addBoardLandmark; on success it re-suggests the next name, on failure it renders the inline alert below.

Up to three stacked role=status paragraphs, each 9px on --ss-warning-soft: "This document is read-only. Saved views cannot be changed." (readonly), "Saved-view metadata uses an unknown format and will not be changed." (landmarksProtected), "Frame ordering uses an unknown format and will not be changed." (orderState.kind==='protected'). Plus a separate role=alert message for a failed save: landmarkFailureMessage() returns the single string "Saved-view names must be distinct and contain 1–80 characters."

display:grid, gap 6px, list-style none. The density mode is expressed purely as a class on the <ul>: `.is-list` shrinks item min-height 41→33 and name min-height to 28, and the row itself stops rendering the thumbnail button.

One row: flex, min-height 41px, 4px padding, 1px border, 9px radius, sunken background. Carries `data-kind` (target|landmark), `data-dragging`, `data-drop-position` (before|after) and a per-item data-testid. Double-clicking anywhere that is not the grip or the ⋯ menu starts an inline rename. Children in order: DragHandle, thumbnail button (cards mode only), name button OR rename input, ItemMenu, and an optional inline error paragraph.

A <span aria-hidden title="Drag to reorder"> whose entire content is the character ⠿ (Braille U+283F — the "6-dot grip" in the screenshot is literally a text glyph, not an icon). 17px wide, --ss-text-faint, cursor:grab. `draggable={!reorderLocked}` and it is the element that starts the HTML5 drag.

A hand-drawn inline <svg viewBox="0 0 168 92" role=img aria-label=`${name} preview`> inside a 92×50 button: a fixed 4×4 grid path, a dashed rounded rect for the viewport, one --ss-accent rect per intersecting page shape (min 2px so a tiny shape stays visible), and — when nothing intersects — a circle-plus empty mark. Its last child is the <text x=8 y=85> uppercase caption: 'SAVED CAMERA VIEW' for a landmark, otherwise `item.target.kind.toUpperCase()` — which is exactly the 'BRANCH' / 'EXPANDED-BLOCK' text in the screenshot (the hyphen is the raw enum value, uppercased, not a display name). Clicking the button focuses the item.

Either a focus <button class=__name title={`Focus ${label}`}> or, while renaming, a <div class=__name> wrapping an <input>. Both lead with a 14px accent-coloured icon span from iconFor(): '⌖' landmark, '▣' frame, '⑂' branch, '▤' expanded-block. The label truncates with ellipsis (overflow hidden / text-overflow ellipsis / nowrap on the last span) — this is the "run_09_branch()" text. Rename commits on blur or Enter, reverts on Escape.

A native <details>/<summary> disclosure (summary text is ⋯, ::-webkit-details-marker hidden) containing a div[role=menu] positioned top:29px/right:0 with up to three role=menuitem buttons: "Focus", "Rename" (disabled when mutationLocked), and — landmarks only — "Delete saved view". Each handler closes the menu by walking the DOM: `event.currentTarget.closest('details')?.removeAttribute('open')`.

Rendered instead of the list when there are no items: a dashed-border card with a ▣ glyph, "No frames or saved views yet" and

"Add a Frame or save the current camera view."

. Distinct from the shell-wide `.systemsketch-panel-empty` pattern (solid tile, 46px glyph) used by the inspector's empty state.

Not an element — a ::before/::after on the row, 2px accent bar inset 5px left/right, at top:-4px for 'before' and bottom:-4px for 'after', driven entirely by `data-drop-position`. The dragged row drops to opacity .45.

The bottom utility strip's icon button — title "Board overview and saved views", aria-expanded={rightSurface==='board-overview'}, aria-controls="systemsketch-right-popout". Calls toggleRight('board-overview') and closes the Dev/Help popovers. So the shell's open/closed state is owned by a sibling component, not by the panel.

surveys.dataModel:
Three layers, all typed against tldraw today.

**(1) The shell's surface registry** — `src/chrome/chromeState.ts`. `LeftSurface = 'shapes'|'behaviors'|'files'` (6), `RightSurface = 'comments'|'inspector'|'board-overview'|'diagnostics'|'variable-registry'` (7), `ToolbarSurface = 'commands'|'find-replace'` (8), `ChromeSurfaceId = \`left:${LeftSurface}\` | \`right:${RightSurface}\` | \`toolbar:${ToolbarSurface}\`` (10-13), `ChromeState {leftSurface, rightSurface, toolbarSurface, openOrder: ChromeSurfaceId[]}` (15-20), `ChromeAction` (29-34), `reduceChromeState` (49-96). `openOrder` is an LRU stack so Escape closes the most recently opened zone. **This whole file already imports nothing from tldraw** and is the most portable thing in the survey. The controller interface `ChromeController` (ChromeProvider.tsx:20-29) adds setLeft/toggleLeft/setRight/toggleRight/setToolbar/toggleToolbar/closeLatest/closeAll.

**(2) The Frames list model** — `src/chrome/framesPanelModel.ts`. `FramesPanelItem = {key: \`shape:${string}\`, kind:'target', target: BoardOverviewTarget} | {key: \`landmark:${string}\`, kind:'landmark', landmark: BoardLandmark}` (8-11). `FramesPanelOrderState = {kind:'ready', order:string[]} | {kind:'protected'}` (12). `FramesPanelDropPosition = 'before'|'after'` (13). `FramesPanelBox {x,y,w,h}` (15). `FramesPanelPreview {viewport: FramesPanelBox; shapes: FramesPanelBox[]}` (16-21) — the only thing the thumbnail needs, already engine-free. `getFramesPanelModel(editor)` returns `{items, orderState, landmarksProtected}` (40-57). Order is persisted on tldraw page meta under `FRAMES_PANEL_ORDER_META_KEY = 'systemSketchFramesPanelOrder'`, version 1 (5-6).

**(3) The two item sources.** `BoardOverviewTarget {id: TLShapeId; pageId: TLPageId; kind: 'frame'|'branch'|'expanded-block'; label: string; selected: boolean}` (boardOverviewModel.ts:13-21) — `label` already runs through `storedTextOr` (46, 55, 64), Zach's truthful-rendering helper, so fallbacks are \"Untitled frame\"/\"Untitled Branch\"/\"Untitled Block\". `BoardCameraPose {x,y,z}` and `BoardLandmark {id: string; name: string; camera: BoardCameraPose}` (boardLandmarks.ts:10-11) — plain JSON, no tldraw types at all; `BoardLandmarkState` (13-16) and `LandmarkMutation` / `LandmarkFailureReason` (19-24) are the result algebra the panel's error strings come from. Landmarks persist on page meta under `BOARD_LANDMARKS_META_KEY='systemSketchLandmarks'` v1 (6-7), max name length 80 (8).

View-local state lives only in `BoardOverview` (91): `mode: 'cards'|'list'`, `menuOpen`, `name`, `message`, `dragging: string|null`, `dropTarget: {key, position}|null`, plus three refs (`dragCommitted`, `activeDrag`, `activeDropTarget`). **None of it is persisted** — the density toggle resets to 'cards' on every remount; there is no localStorage anywhere on this surface.

engineCoupling.what: The panel takes ZERO props. It calls useEditor() and three useValue() subscriptions itself: getFramesPanelModel(editor), editor.getIsReadonly(), getFramesPanelPreviews(editor, model.items). Every datum on screen is pulled, not passed. Zach's taste here must survive verbatim (88-89): "WHY: preview cards are a view projection, not a subscription per row. One derivation keeps a long Frames panel from multiplying editor listeners."

getFramesPanelModel reads editor.getCurrentPageId(), editor.getCurrentPage(), getBoardOverviewModel(editor) and getBoardLandmarkState(editor, pageId), then merges. Carries the panel's core product taste (51-52): "WHY: frames and landmarks share navigation intent, while the landmark icon preserves its camera distinction instead of splitting the panel."

getFramesPanelPreviews is the thumbnail's whole geometry source and is pure tldraw: editor.getPageShapeIds(pageId), editor.getShapePageBounds(id) per shape, and editor.getViewportScreenBounds() to convert a saved camera into a page-space rect (screen.w / camera.z, screen.h / camera.z, x = -camera.x). The OUTPUT type (FramesPanelPreview) is already engine-free, so the cut line is exactly here: the host computes previews, the component renders them.

reorderFramesPanelItems writes the order: editor.getIsReadonly(), editor.getCurrentPage(), re-derives the live key set via getFramesPanelModel, editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint('reorder frames panel'), editor.updatePage({meta}). Documented intent at 124: "Persist only the order projection: Frame records remain owned by tldraw."

focusItem() → focusBoardLandmark(editor, id) or focusBoardOverviewTarget(editor, target). Both are camera/selection moves into tldraw. boardOverviewModel.ts:100-102 records why it may not be a raw camera set: "WHY: Overview is a flat landmark index, but its jumps must respect the current isolation boundary. The shared transaction makes an outside target visible and keeps Back/Forward coherent instead of bypassing depth." It bottoms out in depthNavigation.ts:580-593 (moveToScope, editor.getAncestorPageId) and :558 navigateViewport.

renameItem() writes the shape directly: editor.getShape(id), picks 'name' for a frame and 'title' otherwise, editor.markHistoryStoppingPoint('rename frame panel item'), editor.updateShape(... as never). The `as never` cast is a smell the port should not carry across.

Landmark mutations called straight from JSX handlers: removeBoardLandmark(editor, id), addBoardLandmark(editor, name), suggestedLandmarkName(landmarks). addBoardLandmark itself snapshots editor.getCamera() (boardLandmarks.ts:130) — the component's Save button therefore silently depends on "the host has a camera".

write() persists through editor.updatePage + markHistoryStoppingPoint. Verbatim taste to preserve: "WHY: page metadata shares tldraw's undo history. A separate mark keeps a bookmark edit from coalescing with a preceding drag or text edit." Also 163-165: "WHY: recalling a saved view is an automatic focus change, so it goes on the viewport journal — Back returns to wherever the person was looking when they picked it, not to the last Step In."

DOM self-measurement: placementFor() calls event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect() TWICE in one expression to decide before/after from the pointer's clientY against the row's midpoint. This is interaction geometry and is explicitly host-owned under the trunk's law.

Hand-rolled HTML5 drag-and-drop wired directly onto the row: draggable on the handle, onDragStart setting dataTransfer.effectAllowed/'text/plain', onDragEnterCapture preventDefault, onDragOverCapture, onDropCapture reading dataTransfer.getData('text/plain'), onDragEnd. Plus three refs mirroring state because dragEnd fires after React state is stale (91, 96-102). No dnd library. A portable component should expose reorder as data (source key, target key, position) and let the host own the gesture.

The shell sets `position: absolute` + `z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)` — a TLDRAW-OWNED CSS custom property. That single declaration is the shell's only hard engine dependency, and it is exactly the z-index the trunk forbids.

onWheel={(event) => event.stopPropagation()} on the shell, and usePassThroughWheelEvents(ref) on the sibling top shells (SystemSketchChrome.tsx:163, 187-188). Both exist only to stop canvas zoom leaking through a floating panel — pure host concern.

A window-level capture-phase keydown listener implements Escape→closeLatest, with a hand-written exemption for the inspector. Verbatim: "The inspector is the one surface nobody asks for: it follows the selection, so it is open most of the time a person is working, and swallowing Escape for it would take the key away from the canvas that needs it. Measured: drawing a rectangle selects it, which opened the dock, so the Escape that should have returned the geo tool to select closed the dock instead — leaving the tool armed and no selection pill. Escape closes the surfaces a person opened; the dock closes with its own × or by clearing the selection." Global listener = host-owned; the exemption is policy that must travel as configuration.

Every open/close emits emitRecorderDiagnostic({lane:'action', name:'chrome-right', …}) into SystemSketch's global recorder module. A portable controller cannot import that; it becomes an optional onSurfaceChange callback.

The shell positions itself against four app-global tokens — --systemsketch-chrome-inset, --systemsketch-top-height, --systemsketch-bottom-clearance, --systemsketch-panel-radius (theme/tokens.css:79-82, overridden at 94-95 under 560px). Portable as tokens, but the component must not assume a top bar or bottom toolbar exists.

`.systemsketch-app:has(.systemsketch-preview-mode[data-placement='below']) .systemsketch-popout` and a `body:has(.systemsketch-recorder-indicator[data-placement='below'])` twin push the panel's top down by 58px. The shell's own position is therefore a function of two unrelated app widgets, reached by :has() across the document.

Two DOM walks inside handlers: closeMenu does `event.currentTarget.closest('details')?.removeAttribute('open')` (imperative DOM mutation to close a native <details> menu), and directDoubleClick does `(event.target as Element).closest('.systemsketch-frames-panel__handle, .systemsketch-frames-panel__item-menu')` to decide whether a double-click should start a rename — class-name-coupled event routing.

"Registering a panel" is three hand-edited switch arms across two files plus a string added to the RightSurface union (chromeState.ts:7). There is no registry object, no children slot — the shell knows every panel by name and imports all of them. A host-agnostic shell must invert this: the host passes the title, the eyebrow and the body.

Open/close is owned by an unrelated component (the bottom utility strip), which also reaches into two other popovers (setDevOpen(false), setHelpOpen(false)). The aria-controls/aria-expanded contract is duplicated by hand against the literal id 'systemsketch-right-popout'.

The row icon and the thumbnail caption are computed from the tldraw-derived kind union ('frame'|'branch'|'expanded-block') with a hardcoded glyph ternary and a bare .toUpperCase() — which is what puts the literal string "EXPANDED-BLOCK" on screen. Portable only if kind→{icon, caption} becomes data the host supplies.

PanelPreview hardcodes the thumbnail's 154×69 content box, 7px inset and 168×92 viewBox as magic numbers inside the render function, duplicating the 92×50 button size in CSS (systemsketch-chrome.css:419). Layout geometry, so it MAY live in the core — but it has to become named constants/props rather than four literals.

Every visual rule is a hand-written BEM block against --ss-* tokens, with no Tailwind and no class-merging seam. Notably the panel's two classes are welded onto one element (BoardOverview.tsx:103), so scroll behaviour and appearance cannot be separated without splitting them.

reusableAsIs: src/chrome/chromeState.ts:36-96 — `withoutZone`, `activate` and `reduceChromeState`. A pure (state, action) => state reducer over plain strings; the file imports nothing at all. The `openOrder` LRU that makes Escape close the most-recently-opened zone is the non-obvious part and it is already portable. This is the closest thing in the survey to a ready-made component API.

src/chrome/framesPanelModel.ts:86-102 — `moveFramesPanelItemKey(currentKeys, sourceKey, targetKey, position)`. Takes only strings, returns a new order or null. Guards duplicates, self-drop and stale drags. Zero editor references; ports verbatim and is the entire reorder algorithm.

src/chrome/framesPanelModel.ts:34-37 — `ordered(items, keys)`: stable sort by a position Map with unknown keys pushed to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (so a newly-created frame appends rather than disappearing). Generic over `{key: string}`.
src/chrome/framesPanelModel.ts:59-61 — `intersects(a, b)`: four-comparison AABB test on plain {x,y,w,h}. Pure.

src/chrome/framesPanelModel.ts:23-32 — `readOrder(page)`: the versioned-meta validator (version match, array-of-strings, no duplicates → otherwise 'protected'). Only its PARAMETER is a TLPage; the body only does `page.meta[KEY]`, so it ports as `readOrder(meta: Record<string, unknown>)` with a one-word change.
src/chrome/BoardOverview.tsx:35-39 — `clip(box, viewport)`: rectangle intersection returning the visible sub-rect or null. Pure, no React, no editor.

src/chrome/BoardOverview.tsx:41-55 — `PanelPreview`. Already props-in/DOM-out: it takes `{item, preview}` and emits SVG. Its only impurity is calling `itemName(item)` for the aria-label and reading `item.target.kind` for the caption; give it `{viewport, shapes, caption, label}` and it is a finished core component. The fit math at 43-45 (uniform scale = min(154/w, 69/h), centred with a 7px inset) is portable layout geometry and belongs in the core by the trunk's own rule.

src/landmarks/boardLandmarks.ts:32-57 — `object`/`finite`/`validName`/`normalizedName`/`validId`/`readLandmark`. Pure validators over `unknown`. The locale rule at 42-47 is a stated product decision worth carrying: "A board file must mean the same thing regardless of the browser locale that happens to open it. Locale-sensitive casing would make, for example, the Turkish dotted/dotless-I namespace vary between collaborators."

src/landmarks/boardLandmarks.ts:59-79 — `readState`: the versioned landmark parser, including the refusal recorded verbatim at 70-71: "WHY: a malformed record may be future tooling's data. Do not silently \"repair\" it during a normal save, rename, or delete by writing less." Pure over `unknown`.
src/landmarks/boardLandmarks.ts:94-97 — `hasName(landmarks, name, exceptId)`: pure duplicate-name check over the normalized form.

src/landmarks/boardLandmarks.ts:173-203 — `stableImportedId` / `stableImportedName`: pure string collision-resolution with an 80-char budget, carrying its own rationale at 192-194: "WHY: imported landmarks must remain writable after a collision. Reserve the ordinal first, then keep enough source identity to distinguish parallel pages while giving the original landmark most of the title." Import-only; probably out of scope for the port but it is genuinely pure.
src/landmarks/boardLandmarks.ts:241-245 — `suggestedLandmarkName(landmarks)`: pure; produces the "View 1"/"View 2" default the screenshot shows, skipping any ordinal already taken.
src/chrome/BoardOverview.tsx:10-11 — `itemName` / `iconFor`: pure one-liners, though `iconFor` should become a lookup the host supplies (see engine coupling).
mustBeReExpressed: The shell must stop knowing its panels. Today `RightSurfaceBody` (SystemSketchChrome.tsx:254-278) imports and switches over five concrete panels and `rightTitle` (1065-1073) hardcodes five strings. A host-agnostic shell takes `eyebrow` (default "Right panel"), `title`, `onClose`, `children`, and optional `data-*` passthrough — the host decides which body to mount.

Header ownership must become a prop, not an attribute the stylesheet sniffs. `data-inspector-header='body'|'frame'` (1162-1164) + inspectorSubjectOwnsHeader is genuinely a good idea — express it as `hideHeader?: boolean` (or a `header={false}` slot) so a body that supplies its own title and close control still has a pointer way out. The ShapeFactsPanel "no eyebrow" taste is the same rule seen from the other side.

The panel must accept its data. `BoardOverview` currently pulls `{items, orderState, landmarksProtected}`, `readonly` and `previews` from the editor (86-90). These become props: `items: FramesPanelItem[]`, `previews: Map<string, FramesPanelPreview>` (or previews attached per item), `readOnly: boolean`, `reorderLocked: boolean`, `landmarksLocked: boolean`.

Every mutation becomes a callback: `onFocus(itemKey)`, `onRename(itemKey, nextName)`, `onDelete(itemKey)`, `onSaveView(name)`, `onReorder(nextKeys)` (or `onMove(sourceKey, targetKey, position)`). The pure `moveFramesPanelItemKey` can run inside the component; only the persist step leaves.

Validation feedback must travel as data, not be re-derived. Today the panel guesses failure: `renameItem` returns a bare boolean and the component infers the reason, printing one catch-all string (BoardOverview.tsx:31-33, 73). `LandmarkMutation.reason` (boardLandmarks.ts:19-24) already carries 'invalid-name' | 'duplicate-name' | 'readonly' | … — the callback should return that and the component should render the message for it.

Drag-and-drop must be host-owned. The draggable attr, dataTransfer plumbing, the three stale-state refs and `placementFor`'s getBoundingClientRect (BoardOverview.tsx:76-79, 91-102, 95) are all interaction geometry. The core keeps `data-dragging` / `data-drop-position` as *presentational* props (`isDragging`, `dropPosition`) plus a render-prop or `dragHandleProps` spread so a host can bolt on dnd-kit, HTML5 DnD, or nothing.

The ⋯ menu must stop closing itself via DOM. `closest('details').removeAttribute('open')` (59) becomes controlled `open`/`onOpenChange` — in the trunk that is very likely the already-vendored `dropdown-menu` primitive rather than native <details>.

The density toggle must become a controlled prop with an uncontrolled default. Today `mode` is component-local and unpersisted (91); the screenshot's toggle is the only affordance and its choice dies on unmount. Expose `mode` / `defaultMode` / `onModeChange` and let the host persist if it wants.

Focus/navigation semantics must be declared, not assumed. `focusBoardOverviewTarget` deliberately does NOT enter an Expanded Block (depthNavigation.ts:587-588: "Overview is a flat landmark index... Selecting an Expanded Block here must not silently enter it: Step In remains the sole isolation action") and `focusBoardLandmark` deliberately goes on the viewport journal. A host-agnostic `onFocus` callback loses that nuance unless the item type distinguishes 'jump to shape' from 'restore camera' — which `FramesPanelItem.kind` already does.

The kind vocabulary must become data. `iconFor` (11) and the `.toUpperCase()` caption (53) hardcode SystemSketch's four kinds. A second host with different container types needs `kinds: Record<string, {icon: ReactNode; caption: string}>` — and that also fixes "EXPANDED-BLOCK" reading as a raw enum.

Thumbnail rendering and thumbnail *derivation* must split at `FramesPanelPreview`. `getFramesPanelPreviews` (framesPanelModel.ts:68-84) is pure tldraw and becomes an adapter; `PanelPreview` is already the core half. Keep Zach's one-derivation rule verbatim in the adapter: "preview cards are a view projection, not a subscription per row."

Positioning must leave the component. `position:absolute`, the four `--systemsketch-*` inset tokens, `z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)` and the two `:has()` reflow rules (systemsketch-chrome.css:110-143, 1211-1216) are all host layout. The core ships a panel that fills whatever box it is given; the host places it.

The open/close controller is worth porting as a headless hook, not as chrome. `reduceChromeState` + `useChrome` is a general "three docking zones, LRU close order, Escape closes the latest" machine. Its two SystemSketch-isms — `emitRecorderDiagnostic` and the hardcoded `right:inspector` Escape exemption (ChromeProvider.tsx:95) — become `onSurfaceChange?` and something like `escapeExempt?: (id) => boolean`.

One-statement-per-line density must not port. BoardOverview.tsx:104, 106 and 108 are each an entire component subtree on a single line (line 108 is ~1.4k characters). Whatever the trunk ends up with has to be readable; this is the main reason the port is re-expression rather than a copy.
openQuestions: The brief listed `src/frames/WrapSelectionControl.tsx`, `wrapSelection.ts` and `wrap-selection.css`, but they are NOT part of the right panel or the Frames panel. They are the "Wrap" tile in the floating selection pill (mounted at SystemSketchChrome.tsx:684). I read them anyway: `WRAP_TARGET_DESCRIPTORS` (wrapSelection.ts:43-58) is a fully portable menu-descriptor list (target/label/hint), the control is a TldrawUiPopover + a two-line-per-option menu, and the CSS borrows the appearance trigger's geometry from `appearance/figjamTokens.ts`. Someone should decide whether that belongs to the floating-toolbar lane instead — it does.

The panel is called "Frames" but is really "board navigation": frames, Branch regions, Expanded Blocks and saved cameras in one list (framesPanelModel.ts:51-52). Does the ported component keep that merged identity, or does the trunk want a generic `NavigatorPanel` whose item kinds are entirely host-supplied?

Order and landmarks both live on tldraw **page meta**, with a versioned-and-refuse-if-unknown contract (framesPanelModel.ts:23-32, boardLandmarks.ts:59-79) that produces three distinct user-visible "protected" notices. Does the portable component keep those three states in its props (`orderLocked` / `landmarksLocked` / `readOnly`), or collapse them to one `disabledReason`? The three messages currently say different, useful things.

`getFramesPanelPreviews` uses `editor.getViewportScreenBounds()` (framesPanelModel.ts:74) to turn a saved camera into a page rect — so a thumbnail's aspect ratio depends on the *current window size*, not on anything saved. Is that intended ("what you would see now") or a latent bug? Worth deciding before the geometry is frozen into a core component.

The ⋯ menu is a native `<details>` and the view-options menu is a hand-rolled div[role=menu] with no outside-click/Escape dismissal (BoardOverview.tsx:60, 104). The trunk already vendors `dropdown-menu`. Confirm the port is allowed to replace both with it — that changes markup the SystemSketch journeys assert on (`data-testid="systemsketch-frames-panel-view-menu"` and friends).

Rename has an inconsistency worth a decision: a landmark rename that fails shows the inline alert, but a landmark renamed to an unchanged value returns `{ok:false, reason:'unchanged'}` (boardLandmarks.ts:143) which the panel cannot distinguish from a real failure — it only checks `draft !== label` (BoardOverview.tsx:73). Port the current behaviour or fix it?

How far does the shell port go? `.systemsketch-popout` serves BOTH the left library popout (SystemSketchChrome.tsx:1100-1146, with its own tab strip below the header) and the right panel. If the core ships one `Panel` component, it should probably carry a `side` prop and a slot between header and body — but that is design, which is the next phase's call.

There is no persistence anywhere on this surface (no localStorage, no sessionStorage — grepped). The density toggle resets on every open. If the ported component is supposed to remember it, that is new behaviour and needs Zach's sign-off, not a default.

surveys.dataModel:
Everything the view consumes is declared in `/home/bam/systemsketch/src/diagnostics/diagnosticsModel.ts` and re-exported through `diagnostics/index.ts`. It is already a clean read model — "Diagnostics stay a read model: this reference never becomes source truth" (diagnosticsModel.ts:70-72).

THE VIEW'S CONTRACT (only these four types are touched by rendering):
- `BoardDiagnosticsModel` (diagnosticsModel.ts:116-120) — `{ diagnostics: BoardDiagnostic[]; pages: BoardDiagnosticPageGroup[]; counts: BoardDiagnosticCounts }`. Note `diagnostics` is the flat authoritative list AND `pages[].diagnostics` re-holds the same objects; the view filters the flat list, builds a `Set` of visible ids, then intersects each group against it (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:94-95, 149).
- `BoardDiagnostic` (diagnosticsModel.ts:90-101) — `{ id: string; code: BoardDiagnosticCode; severity: BoardDiagnosticSeverity; message: string; detail: string; pageId: TLPageId; primaryShapeId: TLShapeId; affectedIds: TLShapeId[]; source?: BoardDiagnosticSource; actions?: BoardDiagnosticAction[] }`. **`pageId`, `primaryShapeId` and `affectedIds` are tldraw branded types** (`TLPageId`, `TLShapeId`, imported at line 1) — they are opaque strings to the renderer, which only ever does `encodeURIComponent(page.pageId)` and passes ids straight back through `onActivate`. `source` and `actions` are declared but the view renders NEITHER (they are forward-looking: "A future analyzer may point at a Python span", diagnosticsModel.ts:69-72; "An optional command descriptor for a future quick-fix registry", :82).
- `BoardDiagnosticCounts` (:103-108) — `{ total, error, warning, info }`, all `number`.
- `BoardDiagnosticPageGroup` (:110-114) — `{ pageId: TLPageId; pageName: string; diagnostics: BoardDiagnostic[] }`. `pageName` is populated (:496, :550, and the defensive 'Unknown page' at :555-563) but the renderer ignores it (see anatomy → GroupHeader).
- `BoardDiagnosticSeverity` (:46) — `'error' | 'warning' | 'info'`.
- `BoardDiagnosticFilter` (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:13) — `'all' | BoardDiagnosticSeverity`. Declared in the panel file, not the model.

SYSTEMSKETCH'S RULE SET (the part that is NOT generic):
- `BOARD_DIAGNOSTIC_CODES` (diagnosticsModel.ts:35-42) — a frozen map of six rules: `blankBlockTitle: 'block-title.blank'`, `duplicatePortId: 'port-id.duplicate'`, `duplicatePortName: 'port-name.duplicate'`, `unsatisfiedInput: 'input.unresolved'`, `duplicateConnection: 'connection.duplicate'`, `dataflowCycle: 'graph.cycle'`. `BoardDiagnosticCode` (:44-45) is derived from it, so **the generic list component is currently typed against SystemSketch's six rule codes** — that union is the single strongest coupling in the type layer.
- The producers: `addBlockDiagnostics` (:250-357), `addDuplicateConnectionDiagnostics` (:359-389), `addCycleDiagnostics` (:445-485), assembled by `getBoardDiagnosticsModel` (:493-566).

TYPES THE MODEL PULLS FROM ELSEWHERE (all SystemSketch domain, none needed by the view): `BlockPort`, `BlockShape`, `BlockState`, `isBlockShape`, `isGhostPort`, `portDefaultValue` from `../blocks/blockModel` (blockModel.ts:214-215, 583, 755, 833, 1118); `BlockConnectionPort`, `PortHostShape`, `getPortHostPort`, `isPortHostShape` from `../blocks/connections/blockPorts`; `ConnectionBinding` and four helpers from `../blocks/connections/ConnectionBindingUtil`; `BlockPortLane`, `PortFace`, `CONNECTION_SHAPE_TYPE`, `portPolarity` from `../blocks/connections/connectionModel`; `ConnectionShape`; `navigateViewport` from `../depth/depthNavigation`; `isFloatingPortShape`; `storedTextOr` from `../textFidelity` (textFidelity.ts:7-9 — a two-line `value === '' ? fallback : value`).

INTERNAL-ONLY SHAPES (not exported, used by the analyzer): `BoundEndpoint` (:122-129), `SemanticConnection` (:131-139), `GraphEdge` (:141-145), `SEVERITY_ORDER` (:147-151).

engineCoupling.what: `import type { Editor } from 'tldraw'` in the renderer file. It is type-only and used ONLY by `BoardDiagnosticsPanelProps` (:175-177) and the container `BoardDiagnosticsPanel` (:180-191). `BoardDiagnosticsView` (:88-173) touches no engine type at all — the file is already split, it just is not split into two files.

The container component: owns `useState` filter, calls `useBoardDiagnosticsModel(editor)`, and binds `onActivate` to `focusBoardDiagnostic(editor, diagnostic)`. This whole function is the seam — it is the only thing in the view file that cannot travel.

`useBoardDiagnosticsModel(editor)` subscribes to `editor.store.listen(..., { scope: 'document' })` and re-derives the whole model on every semantic flush. A live-data subscription to the engine store — must become either a `model` prop or a host-supplied hook.

`boardDiagnosticsMayHaveChanged(changes: RecordsDiff<TLRecord>)` — a tldraw-diff-shaped throttle keyed on the literal shape-type strings `['block','branch','loop','connection']` and on `record.typeName === 'binding'`. Pure function, fully unit-tested, but its input type IS the engine's diff record. It is host-side optimization, not portable component logic.

`getBoardDiagnosticsModel(editor)` reads `editor.getPages()` (:494), `editor.getPageShapeIds(page)` (:499), `editor.getShape(id)` (:500). The entire analyzer is an engine-state projection — this is SystemSketch's rule set, the thing the brief says to separate from the generic list. It stays host-side.

`focusBoardDiagnostic(editor, diagnostic)` — `editor.getPage`, `editor.getShape`, `editor.getAncestorPageId`, then `navigateViewport(editor, {...})` from `../depth/depthNavigation:558`. This is the row's click behavior: select + fit + push viewport history. Pure interaction geometry; by the trunk's law it never travels. Must become an `onActivate(diagnostic)` callback — which the view already has (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:84).

`editor.getAncestorPageId(...)` used twice — once in `addCycleDiagnostics` to locate a cycle's page, once in `focusBoardDiagnostic` to drop dead/off-page shape ids before framing. Both live in the analyzer/activator, neither in the view.

`TLPageId` / `TLShapeId` branded types leak into the PUBLIC model shape that the view consumes. The renderer never interprets them, but the type signature imports tldraw. Porting means generalizing these to `string` (or a generic id parameter) on the component's own types.

`import { navigateViewport } from '../depth/depthNavigation'` — the model file reaches into SystemSketch's viewport-history subsystem purely to serve `focusBoardDiagnostic`. Splitting the activator out of the model file removes this import entirely.

`BoardDiagnostic.code` is typed as `BoardDiagnosticCode`, a closed union derived from SystemSketch's six `BOARD_DIAGNOSTIC_CODES`. A host-agnostic row component cannot be typed against another product's rule set — `code` has to widen to `string` at the component boundary.

`import './diagnostics.css'` — a side-effect global CSS import from inside the component. The trunk (`apps/storybook-basics`) is Tailwind v4 + `cn`; this 262-line BEM stylesheet is the whole visual design and must be re-expressed as classes, not shipped as a side-effect import.

Every color is a `--ss-*` token from `theme/tokens.css` (`--ss-text`, `--ss-text-muted`, `--ss-text-faint`, `--ss-border`, `--ss-danger`, `--ss-warning`, `--ss-accent`, `--ss-accent-soft`, `--ss-focus-ring`, `--ss-surface-hover`, `--ss-surface-sunken`, `--ss-success`). tokens.css:1-8 states it is the only file allowed to hold a chrome color literal, enforced by `tests/test_theme_tokens.py`. The port needs a token→Tailwind mapping decision; the semantics (danger/warning/accent/faint) are portable, the variable names are not.
`RightSurfaceBody` calls `useEditor()` and passes the live editor into `<BoardDiagnosticsPanel editor={editor} />`. The panel is never mounted with data; it is always mounted with the engine.

Panel chrome (title 'Problems', 'Right panel' eyebrow, close button, `aria-label`) lives in a ternary chain in the host shell, not in the component. A portable Problems panel either grows its own header or ships as a body that a generic `PanelShell` wraps — that is a design call, but the fact is the component today has NO header of its own.

The popout frame is `position: absolute` with `z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)` (a tldraw layer token), `top: calc(var(--systemsketch-chrome-inset) + var(--systemsketch-top-height) + 12px)`, `bottom: var(--systemsketch-bottom-clearance)`, fixed `width: min(316px, ...)`, `backdrop-filter: blur(18px)`, and an enter keyframe. Pure host placement + z-order — by the trunk's law none of this travels. The component itself contains zero positioning and zero z-index.

`RightSurface = 'comments' | 'inspector' | 'board-overview' | 'diagnostics' | 'variable-registry'` — the panel's open/closed state is a string in a host-global chrome store, not component state. Opening is `setRight('diagnostics')`; the component has no `open`/`onClose` concept.

The bottom toolbar calls `useBoardDiagnosticsModel(editor).counts.total` — a SECOND live subscription to the same analyzer, independent of whether the panel is open. This is why the throttle at useBoardDiagnosticsModel.ts:32 exists at all, and it means the count badge and the panel are two consumers of one model, not one component.

The trigger button + `99+` count badge use tldraw's `TldrawUiToolbarButton`, `aria-controls='systemsketch-right-popout'` (a hardcoded host DOM id), and `position: absolute` badge placement. If the badge ports, the tldraw button wrapper and the hardcoded id do not.

`data-testid="systemsketch-diagnostics-panel"` and the `systemsketch-*` BEM class prefix on every element — a product namespace baked into a would-be generic component. Trivial to rename but it is in ~20 places.

Every icon is a literal character in JSX/TS — `×`, `!`, `i`, `⌖`, `✓`, `⊘`, plus `×`/`!` in the counts (:111, :114). No icon component, no SVG, no lucide. The trunk has its own glyph story; these characters are the current design's actual pixels.

NEGATIVE FINDING, verified by grep across the whole folder: ZERO `localStorage`, ZERO `getBoundingClientRect` or any DOM measurement, ZERO `window.`/`document.` access, ZERO pointer listeners, ZERO `z-index`. The only `useRef` (useBoardDiagnosticsModel.ts:80) holds the previous `editor` object, not a DOM node. The view layer is already props-in/DOM-out; the coupling is entirely concentrated in the model + hook + container.

reusableAsIs: diagnostics/BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:88-173 — `BoardDiagnosticsView` in full. It is already the pure surface (its own docstring at :87 says so: "Pure presentation surface, exported so integration and accessibility stay testable"). It reads only `model`, `filter`, `onFilterChange`, `onActivate`; it calls no engine API, measures nothing, and its three tests (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.test.tsx:32-74) render it with `renderToStaticMarkup` and a hand-written literal model — proof it runs with no editor in scope. The only edits the port needs are cosmetic: widen `code` to `string`, widen the id types, and swap the class strategy.
diagnostics/BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:33-40 — `visibleDiagnostics(model, filter)`. Three lines, no imports, total function over the model. Ports verbatim.

diagnostics/BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:15-31 — the `FILTERS` array and the `SEVERITY_LABEL` / `SEVERITY_ICON` maps. Plain data keyed on the severity union; the only change is that a generic component should accept them as props/config rather than hardcode three severities.

diagnostics/BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:42-78 — `DiagnosticRow`. Pure; receives a diagnostic and a callback. The accessible-label composition at :58 (`${severity}: ${message}. ${detail}`) and the fixed `title` at :59 are behavior worth porting exactly — the test at BoardDiagnosticsPanel.test.tsx:43,45 pins both strings.

diagnostics/diagnostics.css:1-262 — the whole stylesheet is portable DESIGN (grid template `20px minmax(0,1fr) 16px`, the 17px circled severity glyph, the 11/9/8px type ramp, the `width: max-content` + ellipsis on the code chip, the inset accent bar on the pressed filter). It references only `--ss-*` semantic tokens, never a literal, so it re-expresses cleanly against any token set. Nothing in it positions or z-orders.

diagnostics/diagnosticsModel.ts:392-443 — `stronglyConnectedComponents(edges: GraphEdge[])`, an iterative-in-spirit Tarjan SCC with deterministic tie-breaking (adjacency sorted :400-402, component members sorted :435, components sorted :442). It touches `TLShapeId` only as an opaque string key; parameterize the id type and it is verbatim-portable graph math. NOTE: it carries NO source citation — under this repo's algorithm-provenance rule it needs one before it lands.

diagnostics/diagnosticsModel.ts:153-191 — the small pure helpers: `diagnosticId` (:153-155), `normalizedName` (:157-159), `endpointKey` (:161-163), `inputKey` (:165-167), `stableShapeSort` (:169-171), `uniqueShapeIds` (:173-175). Deterministic-id and stable-sort utilities; portable, though only the first two are of any use to a generic list.

diagnostics/diagnosticsModel.ts:536-546 — the diagnostic sort comparator (page order → severity order → code → primaryShapeId → id) and the counts fold. This is the ordering the screenshot shows and it is a generic diagnostics-list concern, not a SystemSketch one.

diagnostics/diagnosticsModel.ts:63-67 — `diagnosticSeverityState(severity)`. Three lines, no imports. Ports verbatim IF the destination has the `BlockState` vocabulary; its WHY block (:48-62) explains why it lives in the lint lane.

diagnostics/diagnosticsModel.ts:577-589 — `boardDiagnosticStateOverlay(model)`. Pure `model → Map<id, state>`, no editor argument. Currently unused by any painter (its own docstring says "Nothing paints from this yet") but it is the seam by which diagnostics would tint a Block in the trunk.
mustBeReExpressed: The live model itself. `BoardDiagnosticsPanel` (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:180-191) derives its data from an `Editor`; a trunk component takes `model: DiagnosticsModel` as a prop. The host keeps `useBoardDiagnosticsModel` + `getBoardDiagnosticsModel` entirely.

Row activation. `onActivate(diagnostic)` already exists as a prop (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:84) — but the ONLY implementation is `focusBoardDiagnostic(editor, diagnostic)` (diagnosticsModel.ts:592-611), which selects, fits, switches page and pushes viewport history. That is interaction geometry and stays host-owned. The component must not assume activation succeeds either — `focusBoardDiagnostic` returns `boolean` and returns `false` for a dead target (:593, :595, :602), and today the view ignores the result entirely. A portable row has no way to show 'that target is gone'; that is a real gap, not just a port detail.

The severity vocabulary. `'error' | 'warning' | 'info'` is hardcoded in the union (:46), the two icon/label maps (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:21-31), the `FILTERS` array (:15-19), the two count chips (:109-116), and four CSS selectors (diagnostics.css:49-55, 177-187). A generic component should take severities (id, label, glyph, tone) as config. Note `info` is a half-citizen today: counted, mapped to an icon and a color, but given no count chip and no filter button.

The rule codes. `BoardDiagnosticCode` (:44-45) is a closed union of SystemSketch's six rules. The component renders it as an opaque monospace chip (:72) and never interprets it — so it widens to `string` at the boundary, and the six codes stay in SystemSketch's rule module.

The group header. Today it renders the literal `Board` (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:155) while the model carries a real `pageName` (:496, :550) and a defensive `'Unknown page'` (:555-563). A portable grouped list must render the group's own label; the hardcoded string is SystemSketch shorthand for 'this board has one page you care about'.

Grouping itself. The component derives groups from `model.pages` — a page-shaped concept — and cross-filters them against a `Set` of visible ids built from the flat list (:94-95, 149-150). A host-agnostic component wants a generic `groups: { id, label, items }[]`, or a `groupBy` key, rather than a second parallel copy of the same objects.

Panel chrome and open/close. The title 'Problems', the 'Right panel' eyebrow and the × button live in the host (SystemSketchChrome.tsx:1065-1072, 1147-1174); open state is `RightSurface` in a global chrome store (chromeState.ts:7). A trunk component either grows `title`/`onClose` props or is explicitly a body designed to sit inside a separate `PanelShell`.

Panel placement. Absolute positioning, `z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)`, the 316px width, the chrome-inset/top-height/bottom-clearance calc and the backdrop blur (systemsketch-chrome.css:110-143) are all host layout. The component must ship as a `flex:1; min-height:0` column that fills whatever box it is given — which is exactly what diagnostics.css:1-7 already does.

The count badge as a separate consumer. `SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:211` subscribes to the same model just for `counts.total`, and `:678-690` renders the `99+` pill on a tldraw toolbar button. If a `ProblemsBadge` ports, it takes `count: number` and renders a span — the subscription and the toolbar button do not travel.

Styling strategy. `import './diagnostics.css'` (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:11) plus `systemsketch-*` BEM classes and `--ss-*` tokens must become the trunk's Tailwind + `cn` idiom. The design decisions inside the stylesheet survive; the delivery mechanism does not.

Scale. The screenshot shows 175 rows in a plain `<ul>` with no virtualization and no windowing (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:158-166). Whether a portable list owns virtualization or exposes a render-slot is an open design question the port forces.

Row state. There is exactly one interactive visual state — `:hover` — plus `:focus-visible`. No selected row, no current-diagnostic, no keyboard list navigation beyond native button tabbing. VS Code's Problems panel has all of those; if the port is meant to match that reference, they are new behavior, not ported behavior.

The forward-looking fields. `BoardDiagnosticSource` (:73-80) and `BoardDiagnosticAction` (:83-87) are on the type but rendered nowhere. Carrying them into the trunk type means deciding whether the component renders a source location line and a quick-fix affordance, or drops them.
openQuestions: `stronglyConnectedComponents` (diagnosticsModel.ts:392-443) is real graph math with NO provenance comment. The repo's algorithm-provenance rule (`.claude/feedback.md`, 2026-09-17) says every file implementing real math cites a donor file:line or a source actually read. This needs a citation (or an honest 'ours, ad hoc') before it lands in the trunk — and it is the only algorithm in this surface that qualifies.

Is `BoardDiagnosticsView`'s existing prop shape the intended trunk API, or is the split meant to be finer (DiagnosticsList / DiagnosticRow / SeverityFilter / DiagnosticsSummary as separately composable exports)? Today it is one 85-line component with one private row component; the screenshot's five visual bands map cleanly to five parts but nothing in the source anticipates that split.

Does the trunk want the `info` severity promoted to a real citizen (count chip + filter button), or kept as SystemSketch keeps it — counted and styled but never surfaced? The asymmetry is deliberate-looking but carries no WHY comment.

The group header renders `Board` and drops `pageName`. Is that a deliberate product call (SystemSketch boards are effectively single-page, so naming the page is noise) or drift? There is no WHY comment either way, and the model goes to real trouble to compute the name including an 'Unknown page' fallback.

`focusBoardDiagnostic` returns `false` for a stale row and the view discards it (BoardDiagnosticsPanel.tsx:188). Should the ported component expose a failure affordance ('this target no longer exists'), or does the host's re-derivation on every store flush make stale rows impossible enough to ignore?

Does the count badge (`ProblemsBadge`) port as its own trunk component, or is it out of scope for this surface? It is a second consumer of the same model, lives in a different file, and its existence is the stated reason the store-subscription throttle exists at all.

Does the port carry `boardDiagnosticStateOverlay` (diagnosticsModel.ts:577-589)? It is pure and portable, but its docstring says nothing paints from it yet — it exists only so the diff lane and the lint lane cannot drift into two vocabularies. Whether the trunk has an equivalent `BlockState` vocabulary to bind to is unknown from this surface.

How much of the 262-line stylesheet is intended to survive verbatim as design versus be restated in the trunk's own type ramp? The 11/9/8px sizes and 750/850/900 weights are a dense, deliberate scale tuned for a 316px column; a 'standard' Tailwind ramp would visibly change the row.

surveys.surface: The "Compare changes" dialog — SystemSketch's full-screen diff-review modal (`src/compare/`), plus the two modules it is inseparable from today (`src/history/` for the HISTORY rail, `src/diff/wordDiff.ts` for the intra-value ink). It serves three framings from one component: a plain Shift+D review, a Draft-vs-Main review, and a review-and-APPLY (Merge / Rebase) — the last is the "for use in git merging/rebasing" case in Zach's note.

A flex column of 3 children: titlebar, body, optional action bar.

`<h2>` reading 'Compare changes' or `${action.label} changes`, a `…__summary` badge triple (N added / N removed / N modified, summed across block+port+cable+shape tallies), and a `Dialog.Close` ✕ button.

Shared component, `density="comfortable"` here and `"compact"` in the Block inspector. One row = circular badge slot (version glyph 'v1'/'●' or an author initial) · title · meta line (relative time) · optional trailing pin ('before'/'after') · optional disclosure chevron. The chevron is a SIBLING button, never the row.

The way in: a `TldrawUiButton type="icon"` in the top-right shell with `aria-keyshortcuts="Shift+D"`. Its glyph is two overlapping rounded rects (a diff mark, deliberately not a clock).

surveys.dataModel:
Everything the surface renders flows from five exported shapes. All five are structural — none of them is a tldraw type.

**1. `CompareChange` + `FieldChange` + `BoardCompare` + `SubjectTally` — `src/compare/compareModel.ts:54-104`.** The wire format between model and view.
`ChangeKind = 'added'|'removed'|'modified'` (`CHANGE_KINDS`, :48-49). `SubjectKind = 'block'|'port'|'cable'|'shape'` (`SUBJECT_KINDS`, :51-52).
`CompareChange` fields, each with a stated invariant: `id` (stable within one comparison, keyed by both table and canvas); `subject`; `kind`; `name`; `element` ("a Block or a cable, NEVER a port", :69-73); `elementId`; `parentId` (set on a port change and nothing else — `elementId = parentId ?? id`, :288); `anchorBefore` / `anchorAfter` (`string|null` — null is an assertion the thing is not on that side, :78-81); `portId`; `fields` ("Empty on `added` and `removed` — by construction, not by accident", :84-88); `recordBefore` / `recordAfter: unknown|null` (the raw record, for the Code tab).
`BoardCompare = { changes, tally: Record<SubjectKind, SubjectTally>, total }` (:100-104).

**2. `RecordLike` / `RecordMap` — `compareModel.ts:121-131`.** `{ id, typeName, type?, props?, fromId?, toId? }` — "kept structural so tests need no store". This is the ONE seam that decouples the diff from tldraw, and it already exists.

**3. `PropertyRow` — `src/compare/propertyRows.ts:28-55`.** A three-arm discriminated union, and the union IS the load-bearing part (:5-9): `added` has no `previous` KEY AT ALL, `removed` has no `current`. Accessors `rowPrevious` / `rowCurrent` (:58-65) return `null` where the row asserts absence; `rowSupportsWordDiff` (:72-74) is the type guard. `STATE_LABEL` (:77-81), `STATE_ORDER` added→removed→modified (:90-94).
`ElementSummary` (:194-201) — `{ id, name, subject, status: 'added'|'edited'|'removed', changes, rowCount }`, with `ELEMENT_STATUS_LABEL` (:203-207). The `status` vocabulary is deliberately Figma's (Added·Edited·Removed) and is NOT the row's Added/Removed/Modified — a Block that only gained a port was not modified but WAS edited (:186-192).
Producers: `propertyRowsOf(change)` (:141-182), `elementSummaries(changes)` (:216-240), `orderChanges(changes)` (:243-247).

**4. `DiffLine` / `LineKind` — `src/compare/lineDiff.ts:25-34`.** `{ kind: 'context'|'removed'|'added', text, beforeNumber: number|null, afterNumber: number|null }`. Producers `stableJson` (:44), `lineDiff` (:98), `collapseContext` (:138), constants `CONTEXT_LINES = 3` (:129), `ELISION = '⋯'` (:163).

**5. `DiffToken` / `WordDiff` — `src/diff/wordDiff.ts:17-31`.** `{ text, kind: 'same'|'removed'|'added' }`, returned as two separate sides plus `changed`. `WORD_DIFF_TOKEN_LIMIT = 160` (:39). Also `tokenizeFieldValue` (:51), `compactFormerValue` (:178) and `WORD_DIFF_ELISION = '…'` (:157) — the last two are NOT used by this surface today, but are the same vocabulary.

**The rail's model:** `HistoryRecord` — `src/history/historyModel.ts:41-59` — `{ id, title, description?, timestamp: number|null, author: HistoryAuthor|null, badge, tone: 'added'|'removed'|'modified'|'mixed'|'current'|'none', isCurrent, path }`. Four fields is the whole spec, quoted from Zach at :5-8. `author` is null always and on purpose.
`VersionFile` / `VersionStep` — `src/history/boardHistory.ts:38-55` — the file-system-bound layer the dialog feeds `HistoryRecord`s from; `VersionStep.snapshot` is `TLStoreSnapshot|null`, which is where tldraw enters.

**Component prop types:** `CompareDialogProps` (CompareDialog.tsx:116-124), `CompareExplicitSource` (:65-70), `CompareAction` + `CompareActionOutcome` (:73-114), `CompareMode` / `CompareTab` / `CompareDock` (:46-49), `TableLayout = 'columns'|'figma'` (PropertyTable.tsx:66), `PropertyTableProps` (:319-331), `ElementReview` (:211-214), `BoardRenderProps` + `HighlightTarget` (BoardRender.tsx:66-76, 160-169), `HistoryListProps` + `HistoryDensity` (HistoryList.tsx:43-60), `CodeViewProps` (CodeView.tsx:16-18).

engineCoupling.what: `import { Box, type Editor, type TLShapeId, type TLStoreSnapshot } from 'tldraw'` — `Box` is a VALUE import (Box.From, Box.Common at :324-327, :433-442), so this is a runtime dependency, not just types.
`editor: Editor` is a required prop on the dialog itself. The shell cannot mount without a live tldraw editor.
`setAfterSnapshot(editor.store.getStoreSnapshot())` — the 'after' side is read directly off the host editor's store on mount.

The version-chain effect calls `discoverVersions(currentPath)` then `buildVersionChain(files, editor)` — HTTP fetches to `/api/workspace/file` and `/api/workspace/stat` plus the tldraw store schema. The rail's entire data source is a SystemSketch server.

`jumpTo` — `editor.getShapePageBounds(anchor as TLShapeId)`, `Box.From`, `Box.Common(boxes).expandBy(220)`, `afterEditor.zoomToBounds(..., {animation:{duration:180}})`. Selection→camera framing across BOTH panes.
Effect: every selection change frames the camera. 'One rule, so the camera cannot disagree with the counter about which change is on screen.'
`reframe.current` — `jumpTo(change)` or `afterEditor?.zoomToFit({animation:{duration:0}})`.

The stage-shape re-frame: `const stageShape = `${fullscreen}:${dock}`` plus TWO `window.setTimeout` re-frames at 140ms and 420ms, timed to tldraw's resize observer and a second CSS-grid settle. Pure host-layout timing — nothing about it can travel.
The open-framing effect: unions every change's anchor bounds across both editors and `zoomToBounds(frame.expandBy(120))`, keyed on `${beforeId}:${comparison.total}`.
`pickByShape(shapeId)` — canvas→table. The function body is pure id matching; the coupling is that it is FED by a tldraw selection listener.
`Dialog.Portal container={themeRoot()}` where `themeRoot()` is `document.querySelector('.systemsketch-theme-root')`. A global DOM lookup for a host-specific class, so the `--ss-*` palette resolves.
`import * as Dialog from '@radix-ui/react-dialog'` — focus trap, Escape, screen-reader modality. Not tldraw, but a host-shell decision the trunk should not make for a consumer.

`import '../blocks/ui/block-inspector.css'` — the whole 1629-line app inspector stylesheet is pulled in for one tab strip (`.block-inspector__tabs`, lines 100-140), plus `className={tab==='properties' ? 'is-active' : ''}` at :909/:919.
`<BoardRender snapshot=… onEditorChange=… onShapePicked=… />` × 2 — the panes are hard-wired to the tldraw renderer; there is no slot.
`useLinkedCameras(afterEditor, beforeEditor)` called at the top of the dialog body.
`z-index: 500` on the scrim and `501` on the modal, with `position: fixed; inset: 3vh 3vw`. The trunk law bans z-index outright; the fixed inset also makes the component decide it owns the viewport.
`z-index: 2` on the overlay's after pane so the crossfade layers correctly.
`z-index: 1` on the sticky `thead`.
`.systemsketch-compare__canvas .tl-container { inset:0; position:absolute }` — a rule reaching into tldraw's own DOM class from the shell stylesheet.

Imports `Tldraw`, `loadSnapshot`, `useEditor`, `useValue` plus TEN SystemSketch shape/binding-util modules (Excalidraw interop, Block, Branch, BranchArm, Loop, Code, Icon, Table, connections, stock primitives, arrows, themes). Deliberately not shared with App.tsx (`tests/test_stock_boundary.py` asserts the list literally inside App.tsx, :12-14).
`__TLDRAW_LICENSE_KEY__` — a build-time global injected by SystemSketch's Vite config.

`HighlightMark` — `useEditor()`, `useValue('compare-highlight', …)`, `editor.getShapePageBounds`, rendered through tldraw's `OnTheCanvas` seam so page space is free. The cable branch injects a runtime `<style>` string targeting `.tl-shape[data-shape-id="…"]`, with a guard refusing ids containing `"` or `\` (:135).

The highlight reaches the mark through React context, NOT through `components`, because `components` must keep one object identity for the mount's life — handing `<Tldraw>` a fresh object remounts and resets the camera on every row click.
`useState(createSystemSketchStore)` and `useEffect(() => () => store.dispose(), [store])` — a per-pane throwaway tldraw store with its own lifecycle.

`onMount`: `updateInstanceState({isReadonly:true})`, `setCurrentTool('hand')`; then the snapshot effect wraps `loadSnapshot` in `editor.store.mergeRemoteChanges` so it never lands on the undo stack, and calls `zoomToFit`.

`editor.store.listen(..., {scope:'session', source:'user'})` reading `getSelectedShapeIds()` for canvas→table picking — 'Reading the selection rather than the pointer keeps this on tldraw's own event lifecycle instead of guessing hit-testing.'
`useLinkedCameras` — two `store.listen` subscriptions with a reentrancy flag, calling `getCamera()`/`setCamera(..., {immediate:true})` in both directions.

`import type { BlockPort } from '../blocks/blockModel'` — and `blockModel.ts:2` imports `{ StyleProp, T, assetIdValidator, createShapeId, … } from 'tldraw'`. Type-only, so it erases at runtime, but it is the ONE thing stopping `compareModel.ts` from being a zero-dependency module. Inlining `BlockPort`'s four read fields (`id`, `name`, `type`, `defaultValue` — blockModel.ts:256-262) severs it.

`recordsOfSnapshot(snapshot: unknown)` — knows a tldraw store snapshot is either `{store: {...}}` or the bare map, and filters on `typeof record.typeName === 'string'`. Structural, no import; still a tldraw-shaped adapter that should sit OUTSIDE the ported core.

tldraw/SystemSketch record vocabulary baked into constants: `typeName === 'shape'` / `'binding'`, `type === 'block'|'connection'`, `props.inputs`/`props.outputs`, `props.terminal`, `fromId`/`toId`, and `IGNORED_PATHS = {x,y,rotation,index,parentId,opacity}`. This is domain vocabulary rather than engine API, but it is SystemSketch's domain, not a generic one.

`fetch('/api/workspace/file?path=…')`, `fetch('/api/workspace/stat?path=…')`, `inspectWorkspaceDocumentSource(source, editor.store.schema)`, `editor.store.getStoreSnapshot()`, and the `HISTORY_PROBE_DEPTH = 6` `.vN` sibling probe. The rail's whole supply chain is a SystemSketch HTTP API.
Same fetch + `inspectWorkspaceDocumentSource` again, in the superseded module. Do not port; it is kept alive only so a peer's in-flight import doesn't break (index.ts:26-31).

`TldrawUiButton type="icon"` for the trigger, plus `.systemsketch-shell-icon-button` from the app shell. The comment at :185-196 records that a raw `<button>` wearing the same class rendered as a filled dark chip — the styling is entirely the host's.

A global `window.addEventListener('keydown')` for Shift+D, guarded on `target?.closest('input, textarea, [contenteditable]')` and `editor.getEditingShapeId()`. Global keyboard ownership + an editor query.

The element-list resize handle: `setPointerCapture`/`releasePointerCapture`, `event.clientX` deltas, `touch-action:none`. Pointer listeners and self-measurement — but PANEL-internal, not canvas interaction, so it is host-independent in substance.
Inline style writing the CSS custom property `--systemsketch-review-list-width` onto the grid container. Trivially renamable.
`lucide-react` icons (`Box`, `Circle`, `Frame`, `Shapes`, `Square`, `Type`, `Waypoints`, `ArrowRight`, `type LucideIcon`). A dependency choice, not an engine one.

Every colour is a `--ss-*` token defined in `src/theme/tokens.css` (447 lines): `--ss-surface-raised`, `--ss-border`, `--ss-accent`, `--ss-accent-soft`, `--ss-success(-soft)`, `--ss-danger(-soft)`, `--ss-warning(-soft)`, `--ss-text(-muted|-faint)`, `--ss-overlay`, `--ss-shadow-1/2`, `--ss-focus-ring`, `--ss-code-text`, `--ss-surface-sunken/hover`, `--ss-accent-text`, `--ss-accent-soft-hover`, `--ss-border-strong`. review-table.css:24-31 already re-maps six of them to local `--review-*` aliases — that indirection is the porting seam.
The provider must sit ABOVE `<Tldraw>` while the trigger sits INSIDE tldraw's SharePanel seam, joined by React context. That split is a pure host-composition fact.
`import v1Source from '../../sketches/review/diff-review-modal.v1.systemsketch?raw'` — the tests bind to real repo fixture files through a Vite `?raw` loader.

Zero imports, and its own header states the contract: 'It has no React, no DOM and no colour in it: it answers which runs of two strings are shared and which are not, and the paint layer decides what that looks like' (:13-15). `tokenizeFieldValue` (:51-67), `coalesce` (:70-81), `commonSubsequence` (:84-113), `wordDiff` (:123-154), `compactFormerValue` (:178-196).
