`src/compare/compareModel.test.ts` (247 lines) and `src/diff/wordDiff.test.ts` (162 lines) port with their subjects. `compareFixture.test.ts` needs the three `.systemsketch` fixture files copied and its `?raw` imports repointed (compareFixture.test.ts:14-16).
mustBeReExpressed: **The two board panes become slots.** `CompareDialog.tsx:778-801` hard-wires `<BoardRender>`. The trunk version needs `renderBefore` / `renderAfter` render props (or `children`), receiving at minimum `{ side, highlight, label }`. Nothing about `BoardRender.tsx` can travel — it is a whole second tldraw mount with ten SystemSketch shape utils.

**Selection→camera framing becomes an outbound callback.** `jumpTo` (:314-330), the selection effect (:346-349), `reframe` (:366-373), the stage-shape effect (:386-407) and the open-framing effect (:419-444) are five separate places the component drives two tldraw cameras. All of it collapses to one prop the host implements: `onFrameChange(change: CompareChange | null)`. The component keeps `selectedId`; the host decides what framing means.

**Stage-shape transitions become a notification, not a timer.** The `window.setTimeout(…, 140)` / `(…, 420)` pair at :401-402 exists only because tldraw learns its size from a resize observer and CSS Grid settles twice. The trunk must expose `onStageShapeChange(shape: string)` (or just let the host observe its own slot) and delete the timers. The WHY at :375-385 must survive in the new prop's doc comment — keying on one named mode rather than the stage's shape is what cut the bottom off the board when the panel docked.

**Canvas→table selection becomes a controlled prop.** `pickByShape` (:447-456) is fed by `BoardRender`'s store listener. Re-express as `selectedChangeId` + `onSelectChange(id)`, with the host calling in when its canvas is clicked. The component already holds the id→change lookup.

**Camera linking leaves entirely.** `useLinkedCameras` (BoardRender.tsx:258-279, called at CompareDialog.tsx:208) is interaction geometry. It is host-owned by the trunk's law and must not travel. The Overlay slider's meaning depends on it, so the component's docs owe the host that constraint explicitly.

**Version discovery becomes data.** `discoverVersions`/`buildVersionChain` (CompareDialog.tsx:230-253) fetch from a SystemSketch HTTP API. The component should take `versions: readonly HistoryRecord[]`, `selectedVersionId`, `onSelectVersion(id)`, and `problem?: string` (so the amber notice is a prop, not a derived string). SystemSketch keeps `boardHistory.ts`'s I/O half as its adapter.

**Snapshot→comparison becomes an input.** `editor.store.getStoreSnapshot()` (:217), `recordsOfSnapshot` (:265) and the `compareBoards` memo should move out. Best shape: the component accepts `comparison: BoardCompare | null` directly; a convenience wrapper can accept two `RecordMap`s. `recordsOfSnapshot` stays in a tldraw adapter.

**The modal shell becomes optional.** Radix `Dialog.Root/Portal/Overlay/Content` (:653-680), `position:fixed; inset:3vh 3vw` and `z-index:500/501` (compare.css:25-48) make the component own the viewport. Split a headless `CompareReview` (the 3-column body, the bars, the panels — no positioning, no z-index) from a thin host-side modal wrapper. The Escape-unwinds-one-layer behaviour at :665-674 becomes an `onEscape` callback or a documented host duty.

**The portal target becomes a prop.** `themeRoot()` (:1117-1127) is `document.querySelector('.systemsketch-theme-root')`. If the shell survives at all, the container is a `container?: HTMLElement` prop with the global lookup deleted.

**Theme tokens become the component's own layer.** Both stylesheets resolve `--ss-*` from `src/theme/tokens.css`. `review-table.css:24-31` already shows the pattern — remap to component-local `--bbox-*` (or `--review-*`) names with sane fallbacks so a host that defines nothing still renders. Keep the accessibility rule stated at compare.css:19-22: a `-soft` value is a SURFACE and copy on it is body ink, never the accent itself, because mid-luminance-on-its-own-tint measures 2.6–4.3:1.

**The tab strip becomes local.** `import '../blocks/ui/block-inspector.css'` (:43) plus `.is-active` (:909, :919) pulls in a 1629-line app stylesheet for lines 100-140 of it. Copy those ~40 lines into the component's own CSS. But Zach's reason for the import must be carried as a doc note: *"Very important that we are consistent with what tabs look like."* — in bbox-ui that argues for reusing the trunk's own tab primitive, not for a private copy.

**The trigger and the keybinding leave.** `CompareTrigger` (CompareLauncher.tsx:182-231) is `TldrawUiButton` + the host shell's icon class; the Shift+D global listener (:108-131) queries `editor.getEditingShapeId()`. Both are host concerns. `CompareIcon` (:225-231) is the only part worth shipping — as a bare SVG.
**`__TLDRAW_LICENSE_KEY__`** (BoardRender.tsx:48) is a SystemSketch build-time global and must not appear anywhere in the trunk.

**`BlockPort` gets inlined.** compareModel.ts:45's type-only import reaches `blockModel.ts:2`'s tldraw import. Only `id`/`name`/`type`/`defaultValue` are read, so a four-field local interface severs the graph with no behaviour change.

**The `AcceptBox` semantics must be carried, not just the markup.** The checkbox is REAL but wired to no partial-apply path (CompareDialog.tsx:188-204), and the bar refuses with an explicit sentence rather than lying (:1043-1056). A ported component should expose `review?: ElementReview` AND a `noteFor(rejectedCount)`-shaped prop so a host that DOES support partial apply can change the copy without forking the bar.

**Test ids.** Roughly 40 `data-testid="compare-*"` attributes are hard-coded across the surface. `HistoryList` already solved this with a `testidPrefix` prop (HistoryList.tsx:54, 93, 109). Apply the same pattern, or a `testIdPrefix` on the root, before anyone mounts two of these.
openQuestions: Does the ported component own the diff ENGINE or only the VIEW? `compareBoards` (compareModel.ts:264-496) is pure but its vocabulary is SystemSketch's — `typeName:'shape'`, `type:'block'|'connection'`, `props.inputs/outputs`, `props.terminal`, binding `fromId`/`toId`. A bbox-ui host with a different graph model gets nothing from it. Two plausible shapes: (a) ship only the view, typed on `BoardCompare`, and let each host produce it; (b) ship the engine too, parameterised by a small `recordAdapter`. This decides whether `compareModel.ts` crosses at all.

Is the HISTORY rail part of this component or a separate one? `HistoryList` is already host-agnostic and is shared with the Block inspector (history/index.ts:1-7). Porting it as its OWN trunk component and letting the compare shell take it as a slot would match the trunk's composability, but the rail's 252px width, its footnote and its `pinOf` before/after tags are compare-specific (CompareDialog.tsx:752-771).

Do the `figma` and `columns` layouts BOTH survive, or was the A/B settled? `layout` defaults to `'figma'` because 'it is the layout Zach said he prefers' (CompareDialog.tsx:164-170); `columns` exists as a live A/B. Two layouts is roughly 180 extra lines in `PropertyTable.tsx` and a second header row. Likewise `gitHighlight` defaults OFF as the Figma baseline (:153-163) and `dock` is an explicit undecided A/B (:172-187). Shipping all three toggles ports three open questions into the trunk.

What replaces Overlay/blend when the host's panes are not two linked cameras? The crossfade (`opacity: blend/100` at :791) only means anything with `useLinkedCameras` running. If cameras are host-owned, does the component still offer the mode, gate it on a `canOverlay` prop, or drop it?

Should the FULLSCREEN stamp survive? Its whole design rests on the tree never unmounting and CSS promoting the stage to the viewport (:138-152) — which means `position:fixed` and `z-index`, both banned by the trunk's law. Does the component instead expose `fullscreen` as a data attribute and let the host do the promotion?

Where do the fixture tests land? `compareFixture.test.ts:14-16` imports three real `.systemsketch` files via `?raw`. Porting the tests means porting or synthesising fixtures. A bbox-ui fixture would be a mock, and the file's own header says the whole point is that the rules 'survive contact with an actual `.systemsketch` written by the real editor'.

`compactFormerValue` / `WORD_DIFF_ELISION` (wordDiff.ts:157-196) solve a measured overflow problem ('three per capture') but are NOT used by this surface — `ValueCell` renders full values in both cells (PropertyTable.tsx:178-185). Is that dead code, or a fix that regressed out? Worth resolving before the port cements the current behaviour.

Is `compareSource.ts` (111 lines) genuinely dead? index.ts:26-31 keeps it exported only so a peer's in-flight import does not break mid-track, and that note is dated. Confirm before carrying it — I found no importer outside the barrel.

Does bbox-ui accept `@radix-ui/react-dialog` and `lucide-react` as dependencies? `apps/storybook-basics` already vendors stock shadcn primitives (per CLAUDE.md), which are Base UI / Radix-adjacent — so this is probably settled, but the compare shell would be the first trunk component to need a Dialog.

surveys.surface: The draft-mode title bar (`DraftModeBar` + the `DraftsControl` chip/popover it shares state with) and the bottom-right floating status cluster (`SystemSketchNavigationPanel`'s utility strip + the `PrototypeSwitch` select above it)

anatomy.description: Full-width chrome row, `display:flex; justify-content:space-between`, height `--systemsketch-top-height` (46px), `--ss-surface-raised` with a 1px bottom border. It PUSHES the canvas down — App.tsx stacks it above `.systemsketch-app__canvas` in a flex column — it is not an overlay. Header comment records that an inverted/black bar and a hazard-stripe treatment were explicitly rejected.
Flex cluster, gap 6px, min-width 0: Exit button → 1px×22px divider → draft-name button (or its rename editor) → OverflowMenu (···) → optional conflict banner.
`← Exit` — a lucide `ArrowLeft` size 15 plus the word, 30px tall, transparent, `--ss-surface-hover` on hover. Calls `switchTo(null)`.

Click-to-rename in place: the button swaps for an `<input>` (width `min(220px,30vw)`, 30px, accent border, sunken background) plus a visually-hidden help span that becomes a floating error tooltip when `data-error='true'`. Enter commits, Escape cancels, blur commits; empty name shows 'Give this draft a name.' rather than silently reverting. Focus returns to the trigger button on an rAF.

A 30×30 icon button (lucide `MoreHorizontal` 16) opening a hand-rolled absolute-positioned menu (`role="menu"`, min-width 168px, 10px radius, `--ss-shadow-2`, blur(18px)) holding exactly one danger item: 'Discard draft' → 'Click again to discard' two-step confirm.

Advisory inline warning inside the left cluster: lucide `AlertTriangle` 14 + 'Main changed since this draft — review before merging'. Ink text on `--ss-warning-soft` with a 3px `--ss-warning` left bar and `border-radius: 0 8px 8px 0`; truncates (`min-width:0` + ellipsis span) so it can never push the right cluster off-screen.
Flex cluster: transient status line → Compare button → MergeSplitButton.
`role="status"` span, max-width 320px, ellipsis, muted — a self-clearing message (Rebase results, merge refusals) that expires after `STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000` via a `window.setTimeout` in an effect.

Secondary outline button labelled `Compare ${changes.total} Change${s}` — matches the screenshot's 'Compare 0 Changes'. Border is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ss-accent) 45%, transparent)` over `--ss-surface-raised`. Disabled (faint, `cursor:not-allowed`) when no compare controller is mounted.

GitHub split-button: a solid `--ss-accent` primary segment ('Merge') + a hairline-separated chevron segment (lucide `ChevronDown` 14) that opens a right-aligned menu holding 'Rebase'. Two independent click targets inside one 30px pill. Three visual states via data attributes on the wrapper: normal (accent), `data-disabled='true'` (sunken/faint — the screenshot's greyed 'Merge ▾'), and `data-blocked='true'` (same muted tokens, but the chevron KEEPS its accent to point at Rebase).

36px pill in the top-left shell: lucide `GitBranch` 15 + the word 'Drafts' + a count badge (`--ss-accent-soft` pill, min 16px). `border-right` separator instead of its own border so the shell reads as one continuous strip; `data-active` tints it when in draft mode.

The form actually in the screenshot: a `Toolbar.Button` rendering a shadcn `Button variant="outline" size="sm"` inside a `BreadcrumbItem`, showing `GitBranch` + 'Draft 1' (truncated at `max-w-32`) + a secondary `Badge` with the draft count + a 60%-opacity `ChevronDown`. Supplied through `DraftsControl`'s `renderTrigger` prop.

Radix `Popover.Content`, `width: min(300px, 100vw-28px)`, 15px radius, blur(18px), `sideOffset={8} align="start" collisionPadding={14}`. Contents: an uppercase 'DRAFTS' header, a scrolling list (`max-height: min(50vh,360px)`) of rows, and a dashed 'New draft' button at the bottom.

An 8px radio dot (`<i>`) + name `<b>` + secondary `<small>` + a hover-revealed action cluster (pencil rename, trash discard). Current row: `--ss-accent-soft` with `inset 3px 0 0 var(--ss-accent)` and a filled dot. Discard is a two-step confirm whose button swaps its icon for a 'Discard?' label and resets on blur. The 'Main' row is a plain button with no actions.

Same click-to-rename contract as the bar's, at popover scale (22px input): focus+select on mount, Enter commits, Escape cancels AND `stopPropagation()`s so Radix's dismissable layer does not close the whole popover, blur commits, empty shows the same 'Give this draft a name.' message.

A `TldrawUiToolbar` pinned `right/bottom: var(--tl-space-2)`, `min-height:44px`, 11px radius, 96%-opacity raised surface, `--ss-shadow-1`, `backdrop-filter: blur(16px)`. Its children are 45×42px segments separated by 1px `border-left` hairlines, first/last rounded — a segmented toggle-bar of panel launchers, not free-floating buttons. Active/expanded segment paints `--ss-accent-soft` (the screenshot's highlighted warning triangle).

First segment. Inline `BoardOverviewIcon` SVG (a framed rect with tick marks, 21×21, stroke 1.6). `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` point at the right popout; toggles the `board-overview` right surface (titled 'Frames').

Second segment: inline `ProblemsIcon` (warning triangle) plus a `.systemsketch-problem-count` badge absolutely positioned top-right — 14px circle, `--ss-danger` background, `--ss-text-inverse` text, 1.5px `--ss-surface-raised` ring, rendered only when `problemCount > 0` and clamped as `problemCount > 99 ? '99+' : problemCount`. Exactly the red '99+' in the screenshot. Title text pluralizes ('Problems — 1 issue' / 'Problems — N issues'); toggles the `diagnostics` right surface.

Optional `−` segment, tldraw's `<DefaultZoomMenu />` (the '45%' / '253%' readout, restyled to 59px wide, 13px/750 weight), optional `+` segment. The `−`/`+` segments render only when `showZoomButtons` is on in appearance preferences.

Inline `DevIcon` SVG (the `</>` chevrons-and-slash glyph, 22×22) plus `.systemsketch-preview-indicator` — a 7px `--ss-success` dot with a `--ss-surface-raised` ring and a `--ss-success-soft` halo, shown only when `hasNewPreview(status)`. Opens the Dev panel (a large right-anchored sheet of release channel, cable/tree/type-attribute toggles, isolated presets, recorder controls, version details).
Last segment, tldraw's `question-mark` icon. Opens a small Help panel with an intro line and one row that opens tldraw's `DefaultKeyboardShortcutsDialog`, showing `Ctrl Shift ?` in a `<kbd>`.

A `<label>` pinned `right: var(--tl-space-2); bottom: 64px` — directly above the strip — with an uppercase 10px 'PROTOTYPE' span and a `<select>` (max-width 260px) whose options are long sentences: 'Port editor · single line per port, drag-and-drop rows', 'Port editor · multi-line lanes, one solid box', 'Port editor · multi-line lanes, ragged lines (prototype)'. Dashed `--ss-border-strong` border, deliberately plain because it is not product UI. Shifts right by 280px when the inspector is docked, via `:has()`.

The strip, the prototype switch, the Dev/Help panels and the Preview-mode notice all live inside one `position:absolute; inset:0; pointer-events:none` layer at `--tl-layer-panels`; only the strip re-enables `pointer-events`.
Under 600px the strip and its panels snap to `right:8px`/`bottom:8px` and the panels go full-bleed `calc(100vw - 16px)`.

surveys.dataModel:
Draft bar / drafts chip — everything comes from one React context, `DraftContextValue`, exported from `drafts/DraftProvider.tsx:108-160` and read via `useDrafts()` (`drafts/DraftProvider.tsx:164-168`). Its fields: `activeDraftId: string | null`, `drafts: readonly DraftRecord[]`, `versions: readonly VersionRecord[]`, `activeDraft: DraftRecord | null`, `isDraftMode: boolean`, `changes: BoardCompare`, `hasConflict: boolean`, `hasUnpromotedEdits: boolean`, plus the actions `createDraftAction(name?)`, `switchTo(draftId|null)`, `renameDraftAction(draftId, name)`, `discard(draftId)`, `merge(draftId): Promise<MergeResult>`, `rebaseDraftAction(draftId): Promise<RebaseResult>`, `previewRebase(draftId): Promise<RebasePreview>`, `getCompareSnapshots(): Promise<CompareSnapshots>`, `attachEditor(editor)`.

The record types are pure and live in `drafts/draftModel.ts`: `DraftRecord { id, name, baseLabel, baseDigest: string|null, createdAt, updatedAt }` (`:37-46`), `VersionRecord { id, label, name, createdAt, note? }` (`:48-54`), `DocumentDraftState { version: 1, activeDraftId, drafts, versions }` (`:56-61`), `DraftStorage = Pick<Storage,'getItem'|'setItem'|'removeItem'>` (`:32`). Result shapes live in DraftProvider: `RebaseResult { ok, conflictCount }` (`:60-63`), `MergeResult { ok, driftCount, reason: 'drifted'|'unreadable'|null }` (`:74-79`), `CompareSnapshots { main, draftHead }` of `TLStoreSnapshot|null` (`:82-85`), `RebasePreview { outcome: 'ready'|'conflicted'|'unreadable', conflictCount, draftHead, main, proposed }` (`:96-106`).

The Compare/Merge/Rebase review handoff is typed in `compare/CompareDialog.tsx`: `CompareExplicitSource { beforeLabel, before: TLStoreSnapshot, afterLabel, after: TLStoreSnapshot }` (`:65-70`), `CompareAction { label, confirmLabel(changeCount): string, onConfirm(): Promise<CompareActionOutcome>, blockedReason? }` (`:92-114`), `CompareActionOutcome { ok, reason? }` (`:73-77`); the controller interface is `CompareController { isOpen, open(source?, action?), close(), toggle() }` in `compare/CompareLauncher.tsx:47-65`, obtained via `useCompare()` which returns `CompareController | null` (`:77-79`).

`DraftsControl`'s one prop is the render prop `renderTrigger?: (state: { isDraftMode: boolean; draftCount: number; activeDraftName: string | null }) => ReactElement` (`drafts/DraftsControl.tsx:225-236`) — already the closest thing on this surface to a host-agnostic seam.

Status cluster — `SystemSketchNavigationPanel` (`SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:177`) takes NO props at all. Its data comes from five separate ambient sources: `useEditor()` (tldraw), `useLocalWorkspace()`, `useActions()` (tldraw), `useDialogs()` (tldraw), `useAppearancePreferences()` for `showZoomButtons` (`:178-183`); `useChrome()` gives `{ rightSurface, setRight, toggleRight }` where `RightSurface = 'comments'|'inspector'|'board-overview'|'diagnostics'|'variable-registry'` (`chrome/chromeState.ts:7`, `chrome/ChromeProvider.tsx:20-29`). The badge number is `useBoardDiagnosticsModel(editor).counts.total`, where `BoardDiagnosticCounts` is `{ total, error, warning, info }` (`SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:211`; `diagnostics/diagnosticsModel.ts:119, 545-546`). Release/channel state is `ReleaseStatus` from `releaseClient.ts` with derived labels from `releaseModel.ts` (`SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:21-39, 184`).

PrototypeSwitch's model is `blocks/portLanePrototype.ts`: `PORT_EDITOR_MODES = ['one-line','lanes','lanes-ragged']` / `PortEditorMode` (`:35-36`), backed by `PortEditorPreference { portEditor: 'multi-line'|'single-line'; laneStyle: 'solid'|'ragged' }` (`:19-32`) persisted under `systemsketch.portEditor.v1` and exposed through a `useSyncExternalStore` hook.

engineCoupling.what: `SystemSketchNavigationPanel` imports and calls tldraw directly: `useEditor()`, `useActions()`, `useDialogs()`, `useValue()`, and renders `TldrawUiToolbar`, `TldrawUiToolbarButton`, `TldrawUiButtonIcon`. The whole status cluster is built out of tldraw UI primitives — none of it can cross the core boundary as-is.

`<DefaultZoomMenu />` IS the '45%' / '253%' readout. tldraw owns the number, the menu contents and the button; the app only restyles it via `.tlui-zoom-menu__button`. The zoom segment has no portable implementation at all — it must become a `zoomPercent` value plus a `renderZoom`/children slot.
Zoom in/out call `actions['zoom-in'|'zoom-out'].onSelect('navigation-zone')` — tldraw's action registry, addressed by string id and by tldraw's own source-zone enum.

The '99+' badge count is `useBoardDiagnosticsModel(editor).counts.total`, which subscribes to `editor.store.listen(..., { scope: 'document' })` and re-derives the whole diagnostics model. The badge must arrive as a plain number prop.

Side effects reach through the editor: `loadPreviewCloneFromCurrentUrl(editor)`, `getPortablePreviewSnapshot(editor)`, `openDragModelTuner(editor)`. These belong to the Dev panel behind the `</>` segment, not to the strip's own chrome, but they sit in the same component.

`useEditor()` + `if (editor.getEditingShapeId()) editor.complete()` before switching mode — an explicit "close any open editor first" guard. Pure interaction/host state; must become an `onBeforeChange`/`onChange` callback.

The strip and the prototype switch position themselves with `position:absolute`, `z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)` / `calc(var(--tl-layer-panels) + 1)`, and `right/bottom: var(--tl-space-2)` — tldraw's own layer and spacing custom properties. Placement and z-order are host-owned and must not travel.

Every segment rule is written against tldraw's `.tlui-button`, `.tlui-button[data-isactive]` and `.tlui-zoom-menu__button` class names. The segmented-strip look has to be re-expressed against the component's own element/data attributes.

A long WHY note choosing `--systemsketch-layer-modal` over `--tl-layer-panels` for the draft bar, because the bar renders outside `.tl-container` so `--tl-*` never resolves and a borrowed value silently falls back to 300 — which tldraw's own top-right shell also uses, and DOM order then wins it. Pure z-order/stacking reasoning: host-owned by the bbox-ui law, but the FACT that the bar's dropdowns overlap the canvas is a real constraint the port has to hand back to the host.

`themeRoot()` does `document.querySelector('.systemsketch-theme-root')` and feeds it to `Popover.Portal container=`. A live DOM query for a host-owned element — must become a `portalContainer` prop (or the popover must be host-rendered).

`getCompareSnapshots()` and `attachEditor(editor: Editor)` put a tldraw `Editor` and `TLStoreSnapshot` in the context type the bar consumes. The bar itself never touches the editor (its header comment says so), but its `onCompare`/`onMerge`/`onRebase` handlers pass snapshots around — so the port must reduce these to opaque callbacks (`onCompare()`, `onMerge()`, `onRebase()`) with no snapshot types in the signature.

`parseDraftState` / `saveDraftState` / `readDraftSnapshot` / `writeDraftSnapshot` / `deleteDraftSnapshot` all default to `window.localStorage`. Storage is already an INJECTED parameter (`storage: DraftStorage = window.localStorage`) — so the model is portable; only the default binding is host-y.

PrototypeSwitch's value is a module-level singleton over `window.localStorage` under `systemsketch.portEditor.v1`, exposed via `useSyncExternalStore`. A ported select must be controlled (`value` + `onChange`), with persistence host-owned.

`useOutsideDismiss` attaches `window.addEventListener('pointerdown', …, true)` and a `keydown` Escape listener. Global pointer/keyboard listeners for dismissal — a component concern, but it reaches `window` directly and must be swappable (or replaced by the popover primitive the host already uses).

Two more global-listener effects: outside-pointerdown + Escape to close the Dev/Help panels, and a second one that disarms the Make Stable confirm after `MAKE_STABLE_ARM_MS = 6000` or on outside click, detected with `target.closest('[data-make-stable]')` — a DOM attribute lookup.

The rename-mousedown guard reads `performance.now()` at input mount and again on `mousedown`, and calls `inputRef.current.focus()/.select()` plus `window.requestAnimationFrame` for focus restoration. Not engine coupling, but it is imperative DOM/timing behavior that has to be preserved verbatim inside the ported component (see the WHY quotes).

Every launcher segment toggles a global chrome store (`toggleRight('board-overview')`, `toggleRight('diagnostics')`), and the button's `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` are derived from `rightSurface`. Panel-open state must become `activeId` + `onToggle` props.
`showZoomButtons` comes from a global appearance-preferences store rather than a prop.

`useCompare()` may return null, and the bar's Compare button is disabled on `!compare`. The whole review-and-apply orchestration (opening the dialog with `{beforeLabel, before, afterLabel, after}` plus a `CompareAction`) lives in the presentational component. That orchestration is app logic, not component logic.

`.systemsketch-app:has(.systemsketch-popout--right[data-surface='inspector']) .systemsketch-prototype-switch { right: calc(280px + …) }` — a selector that reaches up to an app-level ancestor and a sibling panel's data attribute to dodge the docked inspector. Pure host placement.
`BuildProgress` runs a `window.setInterval` against `performance.now()` to animate an estimated progress bar. Only reachable from the Dev panel, not the strip itself.

The screenshot's actual draft chip is a shadcn `Button` inside Base UI `Toolbar.Button`/`BreadcrumbItem` — so the render-prop seam already proves this control can be re-skinned. But it is wired through SystemSketch's own TitleBar and carries Tailwind classes plus `title-bar.css` tokens.

reusableAsIs: drafts/draftModel.ts:194-201 — `snapshotDigest`: a length + djb2 fingerprint of a serialized board. Pure string → string, no React, no tldraw, storage-free. Carries its own WHY about not being cryptographic.
drafts/draftModel.ts:211-216 — `nextDraftName(state)`: 'Draft 1', 'Draft 2', … reusing a name a discarded/merged draft freed. Pure over `DocumentDraftState`.
drafts/draftModel.ts:230-235 — `currentVersionLabel(state)`: the v0.1…v0.9 / v1.0… ladder, with a long WHY on why the first row is 9-wide and split out. Pure arithmetic over a count.

drafts/draftModel.ts:237-325 — `createDraft`, `activateDraft`, `renameDraft`, `rebaseDraft`, `discardDraft`, `pinVersion`, `mergeDraft`: all pure state→state reducers over `DocumentDraftState`. The module header (`:1-30`) states outright it is 'pure data model, no React or tldraw'.

drafts/draftModel.ts:83-136 — `isRecord`/`isDraftRecord`/`isVersionRecord`/`parseDraftState`: defensive parsing that drops a malformed individual record rather than the whole list. Pure once `storage` is passed in — storage is already an injected `DraftStorage` parameter, never a bare global reference inside the function bodies.
drafts/draftModel.ts:70-81 — `draftStateKey`, `draftSnapshotKey`, `draftBaseSlot`: pure key-namespacing helpers (only meaningful if a host chooses the same storage layout).

history/historyModel.ts:75-97 — `relativeTime(timestamp, now = Date.now())`: 'just now' / N minutes / hours / days / locale date. Already takes `now` as a parameter, so it is a pure function with a defaulted clock; used for a draft row's 'based on Main · 3 hours ago' secondary label. Carries a WHY about clock skew never reading 'in 3 seconds'.

drafts/DraftModeBar.tsx:267 — `plural(count)` and :270-273 `mergeRefusal(result)`: trivial pure label formatters, but they encode the exact refusal wording ('Merge blocked — Main has N changes this draft doesn't have yet. Rebase first.') that should survive.
SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:689 — the badge clamp `problemCount > 99 ? '99+' : problemCount`: a one-line pure rule, and the thing the screenshot's red badge literally shows.
blocks/portLanePrototype.ts:42-52 — `parseStoredPortEditorPreference`: pure unknown → `PortEditorPreference` validation with per-field fallback to the frozen default.
SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:63-71 — `formatTime`: pure `Intl.DateTimeFormat` wrapper with a 'Not recorded' / raw-value fallback (Dev panel only).

drafts/DraftModeBar.tsx:26 and :33; drafts/DraftsControl.tsx:29 — the two tuned constants `STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000` and `RENAME_MOUSEDOWN_GUARD_MS = 400` (duplicated at both rename sites on purpose). Values, not code, but they are load-bearing and must port together with the guard.
mustBeReExpressed: `useDrafts()` must disappear from the bar entirely. `DraftModeBar` currently destructures nine context fields at `drafts/DraftModeBar.tsx:183-186`; every one becomes a prop: `draftName: string`, `changeCount: number`, `hasConflict: boolean`, `canMerge: boolean`, and callbacks `onExit()`, `onRename(next: string)`, `onDiscard()`, `onCompare()`, `onMerge()`, `onRebase()`.

`useCompare()` and the whole Compare/Merge/Rebase orchestration (`drafts/DraftModeBar.tsx:252-379`, ~130 lines) must move OUT of the component. The component only fires `onCompare` / `onMerge` / `onRebase`; the host decides what dialog opens, builds `CompareExplicitSource` and `CompareAction`, and hands back status text. `TLStoreSnapshot` must not appear anywhere in the ported signature.

The transient status line must become a controlled `status?: string | null` prop (plus optional `onStatusExpire`), not self-owned state with a `window.setTimeout` (`drafts/DraftModeBar.tsx:191, 206-210`). The 5s expiry is a policy the host may want to own; the component should at most accept a `statusTimeoutMs`.

Rename must be offered both controlled and uncontrolled. Today the bar owns `renaming`/`renameDraftValue`/`renameError` (`:188-192`) and validates emptiness itself (`:238-244`). The empty-name message and the Enter/Escape/blur contract are behavior that must survive; the *validation policy* (what counts as a bad name) should be a `validateName?: (next: string) => string | null` prop so a host with different rules is not forced to fork.

The `···` overflow menu and the Merge▾ split menu must become slot/items props rather than hard-coded single items. Today `OverflowMenu` renders exactly one Discard item (`:63-99`) and the split chevron renders exactly one Rebase item (`:165-177`). A modular kit needs `MenuBar.Item` composition; but the two-step 'Click again to discard' confirm and the split button's three-state look (`disabled` / `blocked` / normal) must be expressible in the new API.

`useOutsideDismiss` (`:35-53`) must not ship as raw `window` listeners in a core component. Either the kit takes a headless popover primitive (the way `DraftsControl` already uses Radix) or dismissal becomes `open` + `onOpenChange` props the host drives.

`DraftsControl`'s `Popover.Portal container={themeRoot()}` (`drafts/DraftsControl.tsx:261`) must become a `portalContainer?: HTMLElement` prop — the DOM query cannot travel. The `renderTrigger` render prop (`:225-236`) is already the right shape and should be preserved, because `chrome/TitleBar.tsx:463-499` proves it supports a completely different trigger skin without forking the popover.

The whole bottom-right cluster must be re-expressed as a generic segmented toggle-bar: `StatusBar` with `StatusBar.Item { id, icon, label, badge?, indicator?, active?, onSelect }`. Today each segment is a bespoke `TldrawUiToolbarButton` whose active state is `rightSurface === '<literal>'` (`SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:209-210, 667-734`). `active` becomes a prop; `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` become derived from it.

The badge and the indicator dot are two distinct decorations that must become first-class item props, not ad-hoc spans: `badge?: string | number` (the red `99+` count, `SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:687-691`) and `indicator?: 'success' | …` (the green preview dot, `:723`). Both are absolutely positioned inside the segment and require `overflow: visible` on the button (`systemsketch-utilities.css:87-91`) — that detail must move into the component's own CSS.

The zoom readout has to become a slot. There is no portable implementation to port — `<DefaultZoomMenu />` is tldraw's. The kit should expose `StatusBar.Readout` (or accept arbitrary children in a segment) so a host can drop in its own zoom control and still get the segmented hairline/rounding treatment.

The `−` / `+` zoom segments are conditional on a global preference (`showZoomButtons`, `SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:181, 693, 704`). In a kit that is simply which items the host passes — the conditionality must not survive as a prop on the component.

All positioning must be stripped. `.systemsketch-utility-strip`'s `position:absolute; right/bottom: var(--tl-space-2); z-index: var(--tl-layer-panels)` (`systemsketch-utilities.css:8-11`), `.systemsketch-prototype-switch`'s `bottom: 64px` (`development/prototype-switch.css:5-7`), and `.systemsketch-draft-bar`'s `z-index: var(--systemsketch-layer-modal)` (`drafts/drafts.css:357`) are all host placement. The components ship as in-flow blocks; the host positions them.

Every rule written against `.tlui-button` (`systemsketch-utilities.css:27-75`) must be re-expressed against the component's own markup — the 45×42 segment box, the 1px `border-left` hairline, first/last-child rounding, and the `--ss-accent-soft` active tint are the real design and must survive the class rename.

The `--ss-*` token vocabulary (`--ss-surface-raised`, `--ss-surface-hover`, `--ss-surface-sunken`, `--ss-surface-active`, `--ss-border`, `--ss-border-strong`, `--ss-text`, `--ss-text-muted`, `--ss-text-faint`, `--ss-text-inverse`, `--ss-accent`, `--ss-accent-soft`, `--ss-accent-text`, `--ss-danger`, `--ss-danger-soft`, `--ss-warning`, `--ss-warning-soft`, `--ss-success`, `--ss-success-soft`, `--ss-shadow-1`, `--ss-shadow-2`) and the layout tokens `--systemsketch-top-height` / `--systemsketch-chrome-inset` must map to whatever the trunk's token layer is. `drafts.css:1-3` states the invariant explicitly: 'Every colour is a `--ss-*` token … nothing here names a value directly.' That invariant is worth keeping.

The `PrototypeSwitch` must become a fully controlled `<Select>` — `value`, `options: {value,label}[]`, `onChange` — with the `editor.complete()` guard lifted into an `onBeforeChange` the host supplies (`development/PrototypeSwitch.tsx:34-36`). Its localStorage singleton stays in the host.

The three accessibility contracts on the drafts popover rows must be re-expressed as props, because they exist to fix real computed-name bugs: the explicit `aria-label={`${draft.name}, ${secondaryLabel}`}` (`drafts/DraftsControl.tsx:174-176`), the `aria-describedby` + `aria-invalid` on both rename inputs, and the discard button's confirming-vs-idle label swap (`:199`).

The conflict banner's truncation contract (`min-width: 0` on the flex child + an ellipsis span) must be part of the ported component, not left to the host — `drafts.css:505-515` records that without it the bar's minimum content width exceeded a ~760px viewport and pushed the Merge chevron off-screen.
openQuestions: The bottom-right cluster spans two very different things in ONE component: a ~75-line segmented status bar (`SystemSketchUtilities.tsx:661-735`) and ~470 lines of Dev/Help/Preview panel bodies (`:405-657`) that only happen to be anchored to it. Is the port scoped to the strip alone (the toggle-bar + badges + indicator + readout slot), with the panels treated as host content? Nothing in the current code separates them.

Does the trunk get a shared `SplitButton` primitive, or is `MergeSplitButton` ported as a one-off? Its three-state look (`data-disabled` / `data-blocked` / normal, `drafts.css:632-655`) is genuinely specific to merge semantics, but the GitHub split shape itself is generic.

`drafts/DraftModeBar.tsx:56-62` records a deliberate split: the one-item `···` menu is hand-rolled while the Merge▾ menu uses Radix, 'because a one-item menu does not need that machinery twice'. If the trunk standardizes on one menu primitive (shadcn `dropdown-menu` is already vendored in `apps/storybook-basics`), that reasoning is voided — is that an accepted loss, or should the ported kit keep two tiers?

`drafts/DraftsControl.tsx:213-224` says the shipped pill's markup must come out 'byte-identical when nothing is passed' so `chrome/TitleBar.tsx`'s shadcn prototype can sit beside it for comparison. Is that comparison still live? If SystemSketch has since settled on the TitleBar form, the port should take THAT trigger as the spec and drop the legacy pill — but that is a product decision, not a survey finding.

The draft bar and the drafts popover each carry their own copy of the rename editor (bar: `DraftModeBar.tsx:394-423`; row: `DraftsControl.tsx:46-115`) with the same 400ms mousedown guard duplicated by policy ('this app's house rule is to fix a bug at every sibling site', `DraftsControl.tsx:22-28`). Should the port collapse them into one `InlineRename` component — which would make that duplication-by-policy unnecessary — or preserve two scaled variants?

The `Compare N Changes` count and the Merge button's enablement come from two DIFFERENT sources on purpose: `changes.total` for the label, `hasUnpromotedEdits` for enablement, because `compareBoards` structurally cannot see a shape that only moved (`DraftProvider.tsx:125-134`, `DraftModeBar.tsx:366-368`). A ported component with a single `changeCount` prop would silently re-merge those. Does the kit expose both (`changeCount` AND `canMerge`), or is the host expected to know?

Whether `draftModel.ts` ports at all. It is genuinely pure and well-tested, but it is bookkeeping for SystemSketch's specific localStorage branching scheme — a bbox-ui host may have git, a server, or nothing. Does the trunk want the model, or only the components plus the `DraftRecord` shape as a prop type?

`SystemSketchNavigationPanel` is mounted as tldraw's `NavigationPanel` slot (`App.tsx:138`), and `SystemSketchHelperButtons` wraps `DefaultHelperButtons` separately (`settings/GestureTuningPanel.tsx:21-24`). A ported status bar is host-placed in-flow — is there a known non-tldraw host (React Flow adapter, plain DOM) that needs an equivalent anchor, or does the port ship placement-free and unproven?

The draft bar's z-index WHY (`drafts.css:340-357`) says its dropdowns open DOWNWARD into the canvas's top edge and a mis-chosen stacking context made a 'Rebase' click land on a tldraw shell icon. If the ported bar is placement-free, who owns that collision — and does the kit need to expose the menu's portal target so a host can solve it the way SystemSketch did?

Six smoke tests (`tests/draft_ux_polish_smoke.mjs`, `draft_merge_review_smoke.mjs`, `draft_merge_guard_smoke.mjs`, `draft_rebase_smoke.mjs`, `draft_branching_adhoc_check.mjs`, `zoom_controls_preference_smoke.mjs`) assert against `data-testid` values like `systemsketch-draft-bar-merge-chevron` and `systemsketch-drafts-row-${id}`. Do the ported components keep a configurable test-id contract, or are the SystemSketch tests expected to stay pointed at the vendored original?

libraries.howItStructures: Popups are a fixed four-layer stack: `Root` (state, renders no DOM) → `Portal` → `Positioner` (the Floating-UI-driven placement div) → `Popup` (the painted surface). Every part takes `BaseUIComponentProps` (internals/types.d.ts): `className` may be a `(state) => string` function, `style` may be a `(state) => CSSProperties` function, and `render` accepts a ReactElement or render-fn to swap the underlying element. State reaches CSS as `data-*` attributes (`data-open`, `data-closed`, `data-highlighted`, `data-pressed`, `data-side`, `data-inset`) plus CSS vars `--anchor-width`, `--available-height`, `--transform-origin`.
libraries.extensibilityStory: Three independent seams, none requiring a fork: (1) `render={<MyThing/>}` on any part re-hosts its behavior onto your element — `Toolbar.Button render={<Toggle/>}` and `Toolbar.Button render={<Select.Trigger/>}` are the library's own documented examples; (2) `Menu.createHandle<Payload>()` detaches triggers from the Root entirely, so a canvas can scatter triggers and keep one popup near the document root; (3) `Positioner.anchor` accepts `Element | RefObject | VirtualElement | (() => …)`, so the anchor need not be a DOM node at all.

libraries.whatItGives: Not a direct dependency — it arrives under `@base-ui/react`'s own deps and is what `Positioner` wraps.
