libraries.howItStructures: Base UI re-exports `VirtualElement`, `Side`, `Align`, `Boundary`, `Padding`, `Middleware` etc. through `@base-ui/react/floating-ui-react`. `UseAnchorPositioningSharedParameters` (internals/useAnchorPositioning.d.ts) is the prop set every Positioner inherits: `anchor`, `positionMethod: 'absolute'|'fixed'`, `side: 'top'|'bottom'|'left'|'right'|'inline-start'|'inline-end'`, `sideOffset: number | OffsetFunction`, `align: 'start'|'center'|'end'`, `alignOffset`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `sticky`, `arrowPadding`.
libraries.extensibilityStory: This is the one seam that makes bbox-ui's canvas case work without any custom positioning math. A selection bbox in canvas space is not a DOM element — but `{ getBoundingClientRect: () => selectionRectInScreenSpace }` is a legal `VirtualElement`, so the SAME `Menu`/`Popover` components that anchor to a button anchor to a selection, with flip/shift collision handling for free. Nothing about it is canvas-engine-specific, which keeps the core's "no engine imports" rule intact.

structuralPatterns.pattern: The four-layer popup stack is the unit of reuse — and shadcn deliberately collapses it to two
structuralPatterns.exemplar: Base UI `Menu.Root/Portal/Positioner/Popup` (menu/index.parts.d.ts) vs. bbox-ui's own `DropdownMenuContent` (apps/storybook-basics/src/components/dropdown-menu.tsx:27-58)
structuralPatterns.apiShape:
// Base UI: four layers, every one addressable
<Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Trigger />
  <Menu.Portal>
    <Menu.Positioner side="bottom" align="start" sideOffset={4} anchor={virtualEl}>
      <Menu.Popup>{/* items */}</Menu.Popup>

// shadcn: Portal+Positioner+Popup fused, 4 props re-exposed
function DropdownMenuContent(props: MenuPrimitive.Popup.Props &
  Pick<MenuPrimitive.Positioner.Props, "align"|"alignOffset"|"side"|"sideOffset">)
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: The fusion is why `<DropdownMenuContent>` reads as one line instead of four — and why it cannot currently be anchored to a canvas rect. Widening the `Pick` to include `"anchor"` buys the canvas case back for free; widening it to the whole `Positioner.Props` gives up the simplicity that made shadcn's version worth copying.

structuralPatterns.pattern: `render` replaces `asChild` — a toolbar slot hosts any control without knowing what it is
structuralPatterns.exemplar: Base UI `Toolbar.Button` + `BaseUIComponentProps.render` (internals/types.d.ts:22-37; docs/react/components/toolbar.md:29-41)
structuralPatterns.apiShape:
// roving focus, disabled + focusableWhenDisabled stay with Toolbar.Button;
// appearance and pressed-state come from whatever you render into it
<Toolbar.Root orientation="horizontal" loopFocus>
  <ToggleGroup>
    <Toolbar.Button render={<Toggle />} value="align-left" aria-label="Align left" />
  </ToggleGroup>
  <Toolbar.Separator />
  <Select.Root defaultValue="Helvetica">
    <Toolbar.Button render={<Select.Trigger />}><Select.Value /></Toolbar.Button>
  </Select.Root>
</Toolbar.Root>
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: A toolbar built this way accepts controls it was never written for — which is exactly the "usable in any host" requirement. Cost: the composition is invisible in the type of the toolbar, so nothing stops a host putting a non-focusable div in a slot; `nativeButton={false}` has to be set by hand when the rendered element isn't a real `<button>`.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Detached triggers + typed payload = one popup definition, N scattered triggers (the canvas pattern)
structuralPatterns.exemplar: `Menu.createHandle<Payload>()` / `Menu.Handle` (menu/store/MenuHandle.d.ts) + `Menu.Trigger` `handle`/`payload` props (menu/trigger/MenuTrigger.d.ts:20-30) + `PayloadChildRenderFunction` on `Menu.Root`; documented at docs/react/components/menu.md:2250 and :2661
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Removes every reason to re-mount menu markup per shape — the single biggest win for a canvas host, and it is upstream-supported rather than something bbox-ui would invent. Constraints straight from the docs: only TOP-LEVEL menus can have detached triggers (submenu triggers must live inside their `SubmenuRoot`), and imperative `handle.open(triggerId)` / `.close()` are no-ops while no Root is mounted — calls are dropped, never replayed. `Menu.Viewport` / `Popover.Viewport` exist solely to animate the content swap when the trigger changes.

structuralPatterns.pattern: `anchor` takes a VirtualElement, so a popup can hang off geometry instead of DOM
structuralPatterns.exemplar: `UseAnchorPositioningSharedParameters.anchor` (internals/useAnchorPositioning.d.ts:76-80) + `VirtualElement` (@floating-ui/dom floating-ui.dom.d.ts:356-360)
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: The whole selection-anchored floating toolbar becomes stock positioning with stock collision handling. But the anchor object must be memoized and re-created when the rect moves — a fresh object every render re-triggers positioning, and a stale one pins the toolbar to a rect that no longer exists. `sticky` and `trackAnchor` are the knobs for pan/zoom behavior.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Higher-level menus are assembled from the COPIED lower-level file, never from the primitive again
structuralPatterns.exemplar: shadcn base-nova `menubar.tsx` — `registryDependencies: ["dropdown-menu"]`, and every part is `function MenubarItem(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof DropdownMenuItem>)`
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: One styling decision, inherited everywhere — restyle `DropdownMenuItem` and the menubar, the block context menu and the file menu all move together. It also means bbox-ui already owns ~90% of a Menubar: the net new code is the `Menubar` container plus `data-slot` renames and different offsets (`alignOffset: -4`, `sideOffset: 8`). Cost: a menubar item can no longer diverge from a dropdown item without a prop, by construction.

structuralPatterns.pattern: `useRender` + `mergeProps` — give your OWN component the `render` seam the primitives have
structuralPatterns.exemplar: shadcn `ButtonGroupText` (apps/docs/src/registry/new-york-v4/ui/button-group.tsx:41-63), and `SidebarMenuButton` in sidebar.tsx
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: This is how a bbox-authored part (a `Bar` slot, a breadcrumb segment) becomes swappable by a host without a `component=` prop or a fork. Worth reaching for only where a host plausibly needs to re-host the element — `ButtonGroup` itself is a plain `<div>` and doesn't bother.

structuralPatterns.pattern: `data-slot` on every element is the styling contract a copy-paste registry ships instead of a theme API
structuralPatterns.exemplar: Every file read: `data-slot="dropdown-menu-item"`, `data-slot="bar-left"`, `data-slot="button-group-separator"`, `data-slot="toggle-group-item"`
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: The slot names become de-facto public API — `ButtonGroup` already keys its rounded-corner logic off `[data-slot]` on arbitrary children, so renaming a slot in one file silently breaks layout in another. Worth the cost: it is what lets a host style a menu it did not author, which npm-dependency libraries usually solve with a theme object.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Self-contained registry items with `target:` remapping — bbox-ui's chosen distribution contract
structuralPatterns.exemplar: ui.shadcn.com/schema/registry-item.json, and /home/bam/bbox-ui/registry.json (22 items, all `registry:component` or `registry:lib`)
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: `type` enum is `registry:lib|block|component|ui|hook|theme|page|file|style|base|font|item`; items may carry `dependencies` (npm), `devDependencies`, `registryDependencies`, `cssVars`, `css`, `docs`, `categories`, `meta`, `envVars`. bbox-ui's existing 22 items deliberately use NO `registryDependencies` between bbox items — a shared file is simply re-listed with its own `target` by each item that needs it. Every menu library named here passes the repo's npm test (`@base-ui/react`, `class-variance-authority`, `lucide-react`, `cmdk`, `cn` are all public); `@bbox-ui/core` and `@bbox-ui/glyph-content` are the only blockers, and no menu work needs them. Keep the trunk's up-and-over `../lib/utils` rule in mind: `lib/utils.ts` targets `components/lib/utils.ts`, NOT `components/bbox/lib/utils.ts`.

refs.recommendation:
Build nothing that Base UI already ships, and get the menubar almost free from the file bbox-ui already owns.

1. **Floating toolbar (the flagship)** — `Toolbar.Root` from `@base-ui/react/toolbar` is the ONLY genuinely missing wrapper. shadcn has no `toolbar` item in any style (both `base-nova` and `new-york-v4` return 404; the 74-component docs index omits it), and nothing in bbox-ui imports `@base-ui/react/toolbar`. Write one ~60-line `toolbar.tsx` in the trunk exposing `Toolbar ToolbarGroup ToolbarButton ToolbarSeparator ToolbarLink` with the same cva/data-slot/BarSize-cascade shape as `button.tsx`, and let slots be filled by `render={<Button/>}` / `render={<Toggle/>}` / `render={<DropdownMenuTrigger/>}`. Do NOT add a `variant` prop per control type — the render seam is the extension point.

2. **Anchor it with a VirtualElement, not custom math.** Add `"anchor"` to the `Pick<MenuPrimitive.Positioner.Props, …>` in `dropdown-menu.tsx:34` (and the mirror in `tooltip.tsx:32`) — a one-word change that today is the only thing blocking a canvas-anchored popout. The toolbar itself takes an `anchor?: Element | VirtualElement` prop and hands it straight through. This keeps the core free of canvas imports: the host supplies `getBoundingClientRect`, bbox-ui supplies no geometry.

3. **Popouts: one Root, many triggers.** Use `Menu.createHandle<Payload>()` + `payload` on each trigger + a function-child `Menu.Root` + `Menu.Viewport`. One popup mounts near the document root; every block/port/edge trigger is detached. Remember the two documented limits: submenu triggers must stay inside their `SubmenuRoot`, and handle methods are dropped while no Root is mounted.

4. **Menubar / burger file menu: copy shadcn base-nova's composition, not its file.** Its `menubar` declares `registryDependencies: ["dropdown-menu"]` and defines every part as `React.ComponentProps<typeof DropdownMenu*>` — so bbox-ui's own 261-line `dropdown-menu.tsx` supplies all of it. Net new: the `Menubar` container from `@base-ui/react/menubar` (a single non-namespaced export) plus `data-slot` renames. When copying: strip the `import { cn } from "cn"` (use `../lib/utils`) and the `@/app/(create)/components/icon-placeholder` import, which resolves in no consumer project.

5. **Bottom toolbar / top-left cluster: compose, don't invent.** `ToggleGroup` for the tool selector (port `packages/inspector/src/components/ui/toggle-group.tsx` — already Base UI, adds a `spacing` prop; repoint its `cn`), `ButtonGroup`/`ButtonGroupSeparator` for the forward/back pair, `DropdownMenu` for the draft selector, and the trunk's existing three-slot `Bar` as the strip itself. Feed everything the ambient `BarSizeProvider`/`useBarSize` cascade so one `size` prop drives the whole bar.

6. **Panels (Frames / Problems / Compare changes): `Collapsible` + `ScrollArea` + `Tabs`, not `Sidebar`.** shadcn's `sidebar.tsx` is 723 lines and hard-wires `document.cookie`, a Cmd+B shortcut, `useIsMobile`, and a `Sheet` — all host policy that violates bbox-ui's core rule. Take only its shape: a `Provider + use*()` state contract (the repo already has exactly this in `barSize.tsx`), controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange` with an uncontrolled fallback, and `data-state="expanded|collapsed"` for styling.

7. **Pin the style.** `apps/docs/components.json` already says `"style": "base-nova"`; add the same to any trunk `components.json`. A bare `npx shadcn add menubar` from the trunk pulls the `new-york-v4` Radix build (`dependencies: ["cn","radix-ui"]`, `import { Menubar } from "radix-ui"`) and would put a second popup engine beside `@base-ui/react`.

refs.area: Canvas-app menu systems — tldraw 5.3.2 (read on disk), Excalidraw (fetched from GitHub master), @xyflow/react 12.11.6 (read on disk), @base-ui/react 1.8.0 (read on disk)

libraries.name: tldraw 5.3.2 (`tldraw` + `@tldraw/editor`)
libraries.license: NOT MIT — package.json says `"license": "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md"` (the tldraw SDK licence: watermark + render cutoff, production use gated). Source is on disk under node_modules/tldraw/src but is NOT copy-pasteable into bbox-ui under bbox-ui's own terms.
libraries.whatItGives: Item primitives: `TldrawUiMenuItem` (+`TLUiMenuItemProps`), `TldrawUiMenuGroup` (+`TLUiMenuGroupProps`), `TldrawUiMenuSubmenu`, `TldrawUiMenuCheckboxItem`, `TldrawUiMenuActionItem`, `TldrawUiMenuToolItem`, `TldrawUiMenuContextProvider` (+`TLUiMenuContextType`, `useTldrawUiMenuContext`). Containers: `DefaultToolbar` (+`DefaultToolbarProps`), `DefaultToolbarContent`, `ToolbarItem` (props `{tool: string}`), `OverflowingToolbar` (+`OverflowingToolbarProps`), `DefaultContextMenu` (+`TLUiContextMenuProps`), `DefaultContextMenuContent`, `DefaultStylePanel`/`DefaultStylePanelContent`, `DefaultMenuPanel`, `TldrawUiContextualToolbar` (+`TLUiContextualToolbarProps`). Registries: `useTools` / `TLUiToolItem` / `TLUiToolsContextType`, `useActions` / `TLUiActionItem` / `TLUiActionsContextType`, `TLUiOverrides`, `TLUiComponents` / `useTldrawUiComponents`. NOTE: `TLUiToolbarItem` (named in the brief) does NOT exist — grep of `src/` and `dist-cjs/index.d.ts` returns zero hits. The real names are `TLUiToolItem` and `ToolbarItem`.
libraries.howItStructures:
THREE independent axes, which is the whole trick. (1) A flat id→item registry per kind: `TLUiToolsContextType = Record` and `TLUiActionsContextType = Record` (useTools.tsx:48, actions.tsx:~62). (2) A menu-TYPE context: `TldrawUiMenuContextProvider type="toolbar"|"menu"|"context-menu"|"icons"|"small-icons"|"keyboard-shortcuts"|"helper-buttons"|"toolbar-overflow"`; `TldrawUiMenuItem` reads it and `switch (menuType)` over all eight, emitting a toolbar button, a dropdown row, a Radix `ContextMenu.Item`, or a shortcuts-dialog key-pair from ONE declaration. (3) A slot map: `TLUiComponents` is 31 optional keys (`ContextMenu`, `Toolbar`, `MainMenu`, `PageMenu`, `StylePanel`, `QuickActions`, `ActionsMenu`, `TopPanel`, `SharePanel`, …) each `ComponentType

| null`, spread over defaults in `TldrawUiComponentsProvider`. `DefaultMenuPanel` then composes four of those slots — the exact analog of a top-left bar with burger + breadcrumb + nav + quick actions.
libraries.extensibilityStory: ADD ONE ITEM: `overrides={{ tools: (editor, tools) => ({...tools, mine: {id:'mine', label:'…', icon:'…', onSelect(){}}}) }}` — a pure function over the record, no source touched. But the DEFAULT TOOLBAR WILL NOT SHOW IT: `DefaultToolbarContent` is a hardcoded JSX list of 28 `<XToolbarItem/>` elements. To place it you must pass `children` to `DefaultToolbar` — and `DefaultToolbar`'s children DEFAULT to `<DefaultToolbarContent/>`, so you write `<DefaultToolbar><DefaultToolbarContent/><ToolbarItem tool="mine"/></DefaultToolbar>` and wire it in via `components={{ Toolbar: MyToolbar }}`. REORDER: only by re-authoring that children list (cheap — each item is a one-line component). SWAP ONE RENDERER: `components={{ StylePanel: MyPanel }}`; DELETE a zone: `components={{ PageMenu: null }}`. COST: the whole thing is `@tldraw/editor`-coupled — every primitive calls `useEditor()`, `useTranslation()`, `useReadonly()`, `useBreakpoint()`, and item labels are i18n KEYS, not strings. You cannot lift `TldrawUiMenuItem` out; you can only copy the idea.

libraries.name: Excalidraw (`@excalidraw/excalidraw`, GitHub master)
libraries.license: MIT
libraries.whatItGives: PUBLICLY EXPORTED from packages/excalidraw/index.tsx: `MainMenu` (with `.Trigger`, `.Item`, `.ItemLink`, `.ItemCustom`, `.Group`, `.Separator`, `.Sub`, `.DefaultItems`), `WelcomeScreen`, `Footer`, `Sidebar`, `DefaultSidebar`, `Stats`, `Button`, `LiveCollaborationTrigger`, `CommandPalette`, `TTDDialog`, `TTDDialogTrigger`, `Ellipsify`. NOT EXPORTED (verified against the export list): `Island`, `ActionManager`, `DropdownMenu`, `Actions`/`SelectedShapeActions`. Internal types: `Action` (`{name, label, keywords?, icon?, PanelComponent?, perform, keyPriority?, keyTest?, predicate?, checked?, trackEvent, viewMode?, navigation?}`), `PanelComponentProps`, `ActionName`, `UIOptions`, `CanvasActions`, `ViewportUIDock`, `ViewportUIName`.
libraries.howItStructures: An `ActionManager` holding `actions = {} as Record<ActionName, Action>` with `registerAction(action) { this.actions[action.name] = action }` and `registerAll(actions)`. One `Action` object carries BOTH the behaviour (`perform`) AND its renderer (`PanelComponent?: React.FC<PanelComponentProps>`) AND its keybinding (`keyTest`) AND its availability (`predicate`) — behaviour, chrome, and shortcut are one record, which is the opposite of tldraw's split. Panels then call `renderAction("changeStrokeColor")` by name; `PanelComponentProps` even passes `renderAction` back down so a panel can nest others. Public composition is a compound namespace: `MainMenu = Object.assign(withInternalFallback("MainMenu", …), { Trigger: DropdownMenu.Trigger, Item: DropdownMenu.Item, ItemLink, ItemCustom, Group, Separator, Sub, DefaultItems })`. `Island` is a 25-line forwardRef `<div className="Island">` with `padding`, `data-viewport-ui` and `data-viewport-ui-name` — the floating-surface shell, nothing more.
libraries.extensibilityStory: ADD ONE ITEM + REORDER (main menu only, and it's genuinely good): the host renders `<Excalidraw><MainMenu><MainMenu.DefaultItems.LoadScene/><MainMenu.Item onSelect={…}>Mine</MainMenu.Item></MainMenu></Excalidraw>` — the host writes the literal order, and `DefaultItems` are individually opt-in, so both adding and reordering are free. `withInternalFallback` is what makes it work: a `renderAtom` counter increments in `useLayoutEffect` per mounted instance, and the library's own fallback skips rendering once it sees a host instance mounted — so the host "overrides" a slot just by rendering the component anywhere in the subtree, no props threading. SWAP ONE RENDERER: `registerAction` overwrites by name, so replacing one `PanelComponent` is one call — except ActionManager is not exported, so a host cannot do it. REORDER THE SHAPE-ACTIONS PANEL: impossible without forking — `SelectedShapeActions` is hardcoded JSX (`{predicates.strokeColor && renderAction("changeStrokeColor")}` …). Remaining public knobs are coarse booleans: `UIOptions.canvasActions = {changeViewBackgroundColor, clearCanvas, export, loadScene, saveToActiveFile, toggleTheme, saveAsImage}` plus escape hatches `renderTopRightUI(isMobile, appState)` and `renderCustomStats`. COST: MIT means bbox-ui MAY copy `Island`, `DropdownMenu` and the `Action` shape verbatim with attribution — which is the realistic route, since none of them are importable.

libraries.name: @xyflow/react 12.11.6
libraries.license: MIT
libraries.whatItGives: `Panel` (`PanelProps = HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { position?: PanelPosition }`, a `ForwardRefExoticComponent`), `NodeToolbar` (`NodeToolbarProps = HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> & { nodeId?: string | string[]; isVisible?: boolean; position?: Position; offset?: number; align?: Align }`), `NodeToolbarPortal`, `Controls` (`ControlProps` with `showZoom`/`showFitView`/`showInteractive`/`fitViewOptions`/`onZoomIn`/`onZoomOut`/`onFitView`/`onInteractiveChange`/`position`/`orientation`/`children`), `ControlButton` (`ControlButtonProps = ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>` — literally nothing more).
libraries.howItStructures: It does not have a menu system. `Panel` is a positioned div (`top-left`…`bottom-right`) and nothing else — the docstring says it is what `<MiniMap/>` and `<Controls/>` are built on. `NodeToolbar` is the one real idea: it portals out of the node, does not scale with the viewport, positions itself against `nodeId` (or an array of node ids, for a shared toolbar over a multi-selection), and auto-hides unless the node is selected or `isVisible` is forced. `Controls` is a fixed built-in set behind three booleans plus a `children` append slot.
libraries.extensibilityStory: ADD ONE ITEM: `<Controls><ControlButton onClick={…}><Icon/></ControlButton></Controls>` — appends only, always after the built-ins. REORDER: not possible; the built-ins are hardcoded and the only lever is turning each off with `showZoom`/`showFitView`/`showInteractive` and re-adding your own `ControlButton`s in order — i.e. reorder by full replacement. SWAP ONE RENDERER: not possible; there is no slot map and no item registry. COST is inverted from tldraw's: near-zero coupling (`Panel` and `NodeToolbar` are pure positioning, importable today, already a peer in bbox-ui) but near-zero structure — it gives you the WHERE, never the WHAT.

libraries.name: @base-ui/react 1.8.0
libraries.license: MIT
libraries.whatItGives: Publicly installable primitives already on disk in bbox-ui: `Menu` (Root/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Item/CheckboxItem/CheckboxItemIndicator/RadioGroup/RadioItem/Group/GroupLabel/Separator/SubmenuRoot/SubmenuTrigger/Arrow), `ContextMenu` (same part set, re-exported with ContextMenu* type aliases), `Menubar`, `Toolbar` (`Toolbar.Root` with `orientation`/`loopFocus`/`disabled`, `Toolbar.Group`, `Toolbar.Button`, `Toolbar.Link`, `Toolbar.Input`, `Toolbar.Separator`), `Popover`, `Tooltip`, `Toggle`, `ToggleGroup`, `useRender` (+`UseRenderRenderProp`, `ComponentRenderFn`).
libraries.howItStructures: Every part is `BaseUIComponentProps<'div', State>`, which means every part accepts `render?: React.ReactElement | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, State>` and `className?: string | ((state) => string)`. Component state is automatically projected to `data-*` attributes (`stateAttributesMapping`), so a consumer restyles or re-elements any part without a wrapper component. `Toolbar.Root` supplies the roving-tabindex/arrow-key behaviour that tldraw hand-rolls in `TldrawUiToolbar` + `OverflowingToolbar`'s numbered-shortcut `keydown` handler.
libraries.extensibilityStory: This is the only one of the four that clears bbox-ui's npm gate AND is already a dependency — `apps/storybook-basics/src/components/dropdown-menu.tsx` is the stock shadcn `new-york` DropdownMenu over `@base-ui/react/menu`, per its own header comment. ADD/REORDER: it is raw JSX, so both are free and unconstrained — but it gives you NO item model, no registry, no overflow, no slot map. SWAP ONE RENDERER: `render={<MyThing/>}` on any part, no fork. COST: it is a primitive layer, not a menu system; every pattern below still has to be written on top of it.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Context-typed item primitive — one item declaration, N chromes. The single most transferable idea here: the item does not know whether it is a toolbar button, a dropdown row, or a context-menu row. The CONTAINER declares the menu type via context; the item switches on it.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: tldraw — `TldrawUiMenuContextProvider` + `TldrawUiMenuItem` (/home/bam/systemsketch/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/primitives/menus/TldrawUiMenuContext.tsx and TldrawUiMenuItem.tsx). Eight types: 'menu' | 'small-icons' | 'context-menu' | 'icons' | 'keyboard-shortcuts' | 'helper-buttons' | 'toolbar' | 'toolbar-overflow'.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: One giant switch is a real smell, and `exhaustiveSwitchError` means adding a ninth chrome edits every primitive (`TldrawUiMenuItem`, `TldrawUiMenuGroup`, `TldrawUiMenuSubmenu` all switch on the same enum). In exchange, the SAME `<FitToContent/>` element appears in the floating toolbar, the right-click menu, the burger menu and the shortcuts dialog with zero duplication — which is exactly the problem a multi-surface editor kit has. Note `TldrawUiMenuGroup`/`Submenu` return bare `children` for unhandled types, so a new chrome degrades rather than crashes there.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Nullable slot map — one flat object of ComponentType|null, spread over defaults. A host swaps, wraps, or DELETES any region of chrome without the library knowing the region exists.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: tldraw — `TLUiComponents` / `TldrawUiComponentsProvider` / `useTldrawUiComponents` (/home/bam/systemsketch/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/context/components.tsx); consumed zone-wise in `DefaultMenuPanel.tsx`.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: `null` as "delete this" (vs `undefined` as "use default") is a genuinely load-bearing distinction that reads as a footgun until you need it. The map is flat and untyped-by-position, so nothing stops a host swapping `Toolbar` for something that breaks `OverflowingToolbar`'s DOM contract. But it is one object, it is serialisable-ish, and it is the reason a tldraw host never forks the UI package.

structuralPatterns.pattern: `children ?? <DefaultXContent/>` — the wrap-don't-fork default. Every container's children default to its own default content component, which is ALSO exported. Adding one item is therefore `<Container><DefaultContent/><Mine/></Container>`, never a fork.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: tldraw — `DefaultToolbar`/`DefaultToolbarContent` (Toolbar/DefaultToolbar.tsx line ~`{children ?? <DefaultToolbarContent />}`) and `DefaultContextMenu`/`DefaultContextMenuContent` (`const content = children ?? <DefaultContextMenuContent />`). Excalidraw reaches the same place with `MainMenu.DefaultItems`.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Reordering means re-authoring the whole list — you inherit no future default items, and tldraw's list is 28 entries (`DefaultToolbarContent` exports all 28 individually: `SelectToolbarItem`, `FrameToolbarItem`, …, so re-authoring is mechanical, not painful). The alternative — a declarative `order: string[]` — is more ergonomic for one reorder and far worse for conditional/nested items. tldraw chose JSX and exported the atoms; that combination is what makes it work.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Flat id→item registry with a pure override FUNCTION (not an array of patches). Behaviour lives in a record keyed by id; the host receives the record and returns a new one.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: tldraw — `TLUiOverrides.tools/actions` over `TLUiToolsContextType = Record<string, TLUiToolItem>` (overrides.ts, useTools.tsx:26-53, actions.tsx:46-62). Excalidraw's `ActionManager.registerAction(action) { this.actions[action.name] = action }` is the imperative twin.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: tldraw SPLITS behaviour (registry) from placement (JSX), so registering an item shows nothing until you also place it — a real papercut, and the `meta?: Record<string, any>` escape hatch (used for `meta.geo`) is the seam where type safety gives out. Excalidraw FUSES them (`Action.PanelComponent` sits next to `Action.perform` and `Action.keyTest`), which makes one action self-contained and makes the order unownable by anyone but the library. For a copy-paste kit the split wins: bbox-ui consumers own the placement file anyway.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Compound-component namespace with opt-in defaults — `Menu.Item`, `Menu.Group`, `Menu.DefaultItems.*` on one import. This is the shadcn-native ergonomic and costs nothing architecturally.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: Excalidraw — `MainMenu = Object.assign(withInternalFallback("MainMenu", …), { Trigger, Item, ItemLink, ItemCustom, Group, Separator, Sub, DefaultItems })` (packages/excalidraw/components/main-menu/MainMenu.tsx), delegating to `DropdownMenu.Trigger/.Content/.Item/.ItemCheckbox/.ItemLink/.ItemCustom/.Group/.Separator/.Sub`.
structuralPatterns.apiShape:
<MainMenu>
  <MainMenu.DefaultItems.LoadScene />
  <MainMenu.DefaultItems.SaveAsImage />
  <MainMenu.Separator />
  <MainMenu.Item onSelect={() => openMine()} icon={<Mine/>}>My action</MainMenu.Item>
  <MainMenu.Group title="Danger"><MainMenu.Item …/></MainMenu.Group>
</MainMenu>
// the whole surface arrives on one import; DefaultItems are individually opt-in,
// so ADD and REORDER are the same gesture and neither touches library source.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: `Object.assign` on a function defeats some tree-shaking and confuses `React.lazy`/RSC boundaries (Excalidraw marks the dropdown `"use client"`-equivalent). Worth it: one import, discoverable by autocomplete, and it is the idiom shadcn consumers already have in their fingers — bbox-ui's own vendored `dropdown-menu.tsx` is the same shape without the `.DefaultItems` half, which is the half worth adding.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Component-identity slot with an internal fallback — the host overrides a region by RENDERING the component anywhere in the subtree, with no props threading and no slot name. The library counts mounted instances and stands down.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: Excalidraw — `withInternalFallback("MainMenu", Component)` (packages/excalidraw/components/hoc/withInternalFallback.tsx): a `renderAtom` counter incremented in `useLayoutEffect`, plus a `preferHost` flag set when a non-fallback instance renders; the fallback skips when the counter exceeds 1.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Genuinely elegant for app authors (no `components={{…}}` prop to discover), genuinely fragile underneath: it is a global mounted-instance counter, so it breaks on two editor instances on one page, and its own comment admits the goal is only to "ensure we don't render fallback and host components at the same time". It also cannot express DELETE (there is no `null`), only REPLACE. For bbox-ui — a copy-paste kit with no single host — the explicit `TLUiComponents`-style map is the safer of the two; note this one only as the ergonomic ceiling.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Overflow by DOM measurement with children rendered TWICE — and an explicit warning, because the brief's framing of this is wrong.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: tldraw — `OverflowingToolbar` (/home/bam/systemsketch/node_modules/tldraw/src/lib/ui/components/Toolbar/OverflowingToolbar.tsx).
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF: tldraw 5.3.2 does NOT inspect a React menu tree. `TldrawUiMenuItem` renders immediately; the only "inspection" is `collectItems(HTMLCollection)` walking real DOM children and `assert(mainItems.length === overflowItems.length)` pairing the two renders positionally. The schema-inspection approach existed in tldraw v2 alphas (`menuSchema`) and is gone. The cost of the DOM route is spelled out in the source's own comments: a too-broad `attributeFilter` caused ResizeObserver loop warnings (#8528) and a too-narrow one broke active-tool tracking (#8689). The benefit is that arbitrary host children overflow correctly without declaring a width — which a schema could never do.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Positioning shell separated from content — the floating/contextual toolbar is a pure placement machine that takes children and a bounds getter.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: tldraw `TldrawUiContextualToolbar` (primitives/TldrawUiContextualToolbar.tsx, doc comment: "A generic floating toolbar that can be used for things like rich text editing, image toolbars") and @xyflow/react `NodeToolbar` / `Panel`.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: tldraw's version carries real hard-won behaviour the brief's screenshots imply is wanted — MOVE_TIMEOUT/SHOW+HIDE_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT debouncing, MIN_DISTANCE_TO_REPOSITION_SQUARED hysteresis, SCREEN_MARGIN clamping, a ResizeObserver on its own content, and re-position on `editor.getCamera()` — all of which is editor-coupled and ~400 lines. xyflow's is ~40 lines of pure placement and rides the viewport transform. For bbox-ui the shell must be editor-agnostic: take `getAnchorBounds(): {x,y,w,h} | undefined` as a prop (tldraw's `getSelectionBounds` shape, minus `Box`) so the HOST owns the camera, which is exactly bbox-ui's core-imports-no-engine rule.

structuralPatterns.pattern: `render` prop on every part — swap a renderer without a wrapper component, and get component state as data-* attributes for free.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: @base-ui/react 1.8.0 — `useRender` / `BaseUIComponentProps<'div', State>`; every Menu/Toolbar/ContextMenu part accepts it.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Base UI's `render` is strictly more flexible than a slot map for ONE element, and strictly weaker for a REGION (it cannot delete a zone, reorder siblings, or replace a whole panel). The two compose rather than compete: use `render` inside a component, use a `TLUiComponents`-style map between components. This is the only pattern on this list that bbox-ui can adopt by `npm install` rather than by writing it.

refs.recommendation:
Take the ARCHITECTURE from tldraw, the ERGONOMICS from Excalidraw, and the only actual DEPENDENCY from Base UI — which bbox-ui already has.

**What passes the npm-installability gate.** Exactly one library: `@base-ui/react` (MIT, 1.8.0, already on disk and already depended on — `apps/storybook-basics/src/components/dropdown-menu.tsx` is stock shadcn `new-york` over `@base-ui/react/menu`, per its own header). `@xyflow/react` (MIT) also passes but has no menu system to give. tldraw fails twice: non-MIT licence, and every primitive calls `useEditor()`. Excalidraw is MIT but exports neither `Island` nor `ActionManager` nor `DropdownMenu` — so it is a COPY source (which is fine, and is precisely bbox-ui's distribution model) and never an import.

**The stock-part floor, per element.** Floating toolbar and bottom toolbar → `Toolbar.Root`/`Toolbar.Group`/`Toolbar.Button`/`Toolbar.Separator` (gives roving tabindex, `orientation`, `loopFocus` — all of which tldraw hand-rolls). Popout menus → the already-vendored `dropdown-menu.tsx` over `Menu.*`. Right-click → `ContextMenu.*` (same part names, aliased types). Top-left burger/breadcrumb bar → `Menubar` + `Toolbar.Root`. Toggle clusters in a `Bar` → `Toggle`/`ToggleGroup`. Do not write any of these.

**The four things bbox-ui must write itself, in this order.**
1. **`MenuSurfaceProvider` + one `<BboxMenuItem>`** — tldraw's `TldrawUiMenuContextProvider`/`TldrawUiMenuItem` pattern, but with a SMALL enum (start at `'toolbar' | 'dropdown' | 'context-menu'`; tldraw's eight is what an exhaustive switch costs at scale) and with plain `label: string` instead of i18n keys. This is the pattern that makes one `<FitToContent/>` declaration serve the floating toolbar, the right-click menu and the burger menu — the reason the systemsketch menus are worth porting as a kit at all.
2. **A `BboxUiComponents`-style nullable slot map** for the panel-shaped surfaces (frames panel, problems panel, compare-changes panel, draft title bar, top-left bar). Copy the `undefined = default / null = delete / Component = replace` semantics verbatim from `context/components.tsx`, and copy `DefaultMenuPanel`'s zone-of-slots composition for the top-left bar (burger, breadcrumb, draft selector, back/forward are four independently nullable slots, not one component).
3. **`children ?? <DefaultXContent/>` on every container, with every atom exported** — `DefaultToolbar`/`DefaultToolbarContent` + 28 individually exported `*ToolbarItem`s is the shape to copy. In a copy-paste registry this matters more than upstream, because a consumer who reorders owns the file anyway; the atoms are what make that cheap.
4. **An anchored-surface shell** for the floating toolbar, taking `getAnchorBounds(): {x,y,w,h} | undefined` — tldraw's `TldrawUiContextualToolbar.getSelectionBounds` signature with `Box` replaced by a plain rect, so the HOST owns the camera. This is the single place where bbox-ui's "core imports no canvas engine" rule and tldraw's design actually conflict, and the prop boundary is the resolution.

**Explicitly do not port.** tldraw's `OverflowingToolbar` — two full renders of `children` paired positionally, driven by a ResizeObserver plus a MutationObserver whose `attributeFilter` the source comments show has broken twice (#8528, #8689). It is the highest-complexity, lowest-certainty piece; ship a fixed toolbar first and revisit overflow only when a real surface overflows. Also do not port the i18n key indirection or `readonlyOk`/`useReadonly` gating; they are host policy, not component structure.

**Add one Excalidraw idea as pure sugar:** the compound namespace (`Toolbar.Item`, `Toolbar.Group`, `Toolbar.DefaultItems.Select`). One import, autocomplete-discoverable, and it is the shadcn idiom the receiving repo already speaks. Skip `withInternalFallback` — a global mounted-instance counter cannot express "delete this zone" and breaks on two editors per page.

**One correction to carry forward:** the brief's `TLUiToolbarItem` does not exist in tldraw 5.3.2 (zero hits in `src/` and `dist-cjs/index.d.ts`); the real names are `TLUiToolItem` and `ToolbarItem`. And tldraw's menu items are NOT a React tree that is inspected rather than rendered — that was the v2-alpha `menuSchema`, since removed. In 5.3.2 items render immediately and the only inspection is `collectItems()` walking real DOM children. Any design doc built on the schema framing would be building toward something upstream already abandoned.

refs.area: Headless menu/toolbar primitives and their composition + a11y contracts

libraries.name: @base-ui/react (v1.8.0) — ALREADY A DEPENDENCY
libraries.license: MIT — verified on disk, node_modules/.pnpm/@base-ui+react@1.8.0.../package.json line "license": "MIT". Runtime deps (same file): @babel/runtime, @floating-ui/react-dom ^2.1.9, @floating-ui/utils ^0.2.12, use-sync-external-store ^1.6.0, @base-ui/utils 0.4.0. Public on npm.
libraries.whatItGives: Verified by listing the installed package directory: menu/, menubar/, toolbar/, toggle-group/, popover/, context-menu/, navigation-menu/, tooltip/, use-render/, merge-props/, plus a VENDORED floating-ui-react/. Menu parts (menu/index.parts.d.ts, exact export aliases): Root, Trigger, Portal, Backdrop, Positioner, Popup, Arrow, Item, LinkItem, Group, GroupLabel, CheckboxItem, CheckboxItemIndicator, RadioGroup, RadioItem, RadioItemIndicator, SubmenuRoot, SubmenuTrigger, Separator, Viewport, Handle, createHandle. Toolbar parts (toolbar/index.d.ts): ToolbarRoot, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarButton, ToolbarLink, ToolbarInput, ToolbarSeparator. Also `Menubar`, `ToggleGroup`, `useRender`, `mergeProps`.
libraries.howItStructures: Compound components, children-as-elements. Every part's props extend `BaseUIComponentProps<'div', State>` (internals/types.d.ts:21), which supplies `render?: React.ReactElement | ComponentRenderFn<RenderFunctionProps, State>` — Base UI's replacement for Radix `asChild`, and strictly more capable because the function form receives the part's State. `className` and `style` also accept `(state) => …`. State is auto-projected to `data-*` attributes. Submenus nest as `Menu.SubmenuRoot` wrapping `Menu.SubmenuTrigger` + a nested Portal/Positioner/Popup. `MenuItem.label?: string` explicitly "Overrides the text label to use when the item is matched during keyboard text navigation" — typeahead is built in. `ToolbarRoot` is roving-tabindex with `orientation` and `loopFocus` (default true).
libraries.extensibilityStory: Three independent escape hatches, all verified on disk. (1) `render` on every part — swap the tag or compose with another component without a wrapper div; the docs' own Toolbar example is `<Toolbar.Button render={<Menu.Trigger />} />`. (2) `useRender` + `mergeProps` (use-render/useRender.d.ts, merge-props/) — the PUBLIC hook for authoring your own Base-UI-shaped part with the same render/state/data-attr contract; this repo already uses it in packages/inspector/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx and button-group.tsx. (3) `Menu.createHandle<Payload>()` — detached triggers, see structural patterns.

libraries.name: Radix UI / radix-ui
libraries.license: MIT — verified on disk: node_modules/.pnpm/radix-ui@1.6.7.../package.json. NOT a first-party dependency here; it arrives only transitively, under tldraw@5.3.2's node_modules and one hoisted copy (verified by grepping node_modules for dependents of @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu).
libraries.whatItGives: DropdownMenu parts (fetched from radix-ui.com): Root, Trigger, Portal, Content, Label, Item, Group, CheckboxItem, RadioGroup, RadioItem, ItemIndicator, Separator, Arrow, Sub, SubTrigger, SubContent. Toolbar parts: Root, Button, Separator, Link, ToggleGroup, ToggleItem. Single-package install `npm install radix-ui`, imported `import { DropdownMenu } from "radix-ui"`.
libraries.howItStructures: Compound components, children-as-elements — the same shape as Base UI. Composition via `asChild` (boolean, default false), backed by `@radix-ui/react-slot`. Submenus: `DropdownMenu.Sub` > `SubTrigger` + `Portal` > `SubContent`. Toolbar Root takes `orientation` ('horizontal' default) and `loop` (default true), roving tabindex. Documented "Full keyboard navigation" and "Typeahead support".
libraries.extensibilityStory: `asChild` merges props onto the single child element — good, but boolean-only: the child never receives the part's state, so a consumer who wants to restyle on `highlighted`/`open` must read `data-*` in CSS rather than branch in JS. Radix is the safe, boring choice and its part vocabulary is the de-facto standard — but adopting it here means a SECOND popover/positioning runtime sitting beside Base UI, with duplicated dismissable-layer and focus-scope logic.

libraries.name: react-aria-components (Adobe)
libraries.license: NOT VERIFIED — I did not fetch a licence file or find the package installed first-party. (Note: the fetch summary for react-aria.adobe.com/Menu asserted it is "Anthropic's React Aria library" — that is a summarizer error; React Aria is Adobe's, hosted on react-spectrum.adobe.com / react-aria.adobe.com.) It appears in this tree only inside storybook@10.6.0's own bundled package.json (as a yarn-patched dep), never as a workspace dependency.
libraries.whatItGives: Fetched from react-aria.adobe.com/Menu: `MenuTrigger`, `Menu`, `MenuItem`, `MenuSection`, `SubmenuTrigger`, `Separator`, `Header`, `Keyboard`, `Text`, `MenuLoadMoreItem`. Toolbar and `useMenuTriggerState` exist in the wider react-aria/react-stately surface but I did NOT fetch their pages — do not cite their APIs from this report.
libraries.howItStructures: The one genuinely different structure in this comparison: a COLLECTION API that accepts items-as-data plus a render function, not only children-as-elements. Verbatim from the docs: `<Menu items={items}>{(item) => <MenuItem>{item.name}</MenuItem>}</Menu>`. Submenus wrap a MenuItem: `<SubmenuTrigger><MenuItem>Share</MenuItem><Menu>…</Menu></SubmenuTrigger>`, nestable multiple levels. Typeahead documented; long-press trigger via Alt+ArrowDown.
libraries.extensibilityStory: Data-driven extension is the strongest here — a host adds a menu entry by pushing an object into an array, with no JSX surgery, which is exactly what a plugin-style host wants. The cost is that react-aria-components is a large single package and its styling model (render props returning className) is a different idiom from the `data-*` + Tailwind idiom this repo already committed to in dropdown-menu.tsx. Adopting it is a re-platform, not an addition.

libraries.name: Ariakit (@ariakit/react)
libraries.license: NOT VERIFIED — not installed in this tree; I did not fetch a licence file. (Widely MIT, but that is memory, not evidence.)
libraries.whatItGives: Fetched from ariakit.com/components/menu: components `MenuProvider`, `MenuButton`, `MenuButtonArrow`, `Menu`, `MenuItem`, `MenuItemCheckbox`, `MenuItemRadio`, `MenuItemCheck`, `MenuSeparator`, `MenuGroup`, `MenuGroupLabel`, `MenuHeading`, `MenuDescription`, `MenuDismiss`, `MenuArrow`, `MenuList`; hooks `useMenuStore()`, `useMenuContext()`. Imported as `import * as Ariakit from "@ariakit/react"`.
libraries.howItStructures: Children-as-elements, but state lives in an EXTERNAL STORE rather than in React context alone: `useMenuStore()` creates the store and `MenuProvider` distributes it, with `values`/`setValues` for checkbox/radio items. Submenus are nested `Menu` components that open on hover over the parent item. `<Menu gutter={8}>` for spacing.
libraries.extensibilityStory: The store is the selling point: a host can read or drive menu state from outside the React subtree, which is what a canvas app usually wants. But Base UI already gives that specific capability via `Menu.createHandle()` without a new package, so Ariakit's differentiator is largely neutralised here. Adding it means a third popover runtime.

libraries.name: Headless UI (@headlessui/react)
libraries.license: NOT VERIFIED — not installed in this tree.
libraries.whatItGives: Fetched from headlessui.com/react/menu: `Menu`, `MenuButton`, `MenuItems`, `MenuItem`, `MenuSection`, `MenuHeading`, `MenuSeparator`.
libraries.howItStructures: Children-as-elements with an `as` prop for tag/component swap (`MenuButton` defaults to `button`, `MenuItems` to `div`, `Menu` and `MenuItem` to `Fragment`). Positioning is a first-class prop rather than a separate part: `anchor` on `MenuItems` takes `"bottom"` / `"top start"` / `"bottom end"` or `{ to, gap, offset, padding }`. State surfaces both as `data-open` / `data-focus` / `data-disabled` and as render props (`open`, `focus`, `close`).
libraries.extensibilityStory: DISQUALIFYING for this brief: the docs contain no nested-menu/submenu API. bbox-ui's floating toolbar popouts and file/burger menu need submenus. The `anchor` prop is also a closed abstraction — there is no exposed positioner part to hand a virtual element, which is precisely what a canvas host needs.

libraries.name: cmdk
libraries.license: MIT — per the GitHub README fetched at github.com/pacocoursey/cmdk (README text, not a LICENSE file I opened).
libraries.whatItGives: `Command`, `Command.Input`, `Command.List`, `Command.Item`, `Command.Group`, `Command.Separator`, `Command.Empty`, `Command.Loading`, `Command.Dialog`.
libraries.howItStructures: Children-as-elements, but with an inverted control flow: "You render items, it filters and sorts them automatically." A custom `filter(value, search, keywords)` returns a numeric rank; `keywords` act as aliases affecting ranking. `value` controls selection and is always `trim()`ed.
libraries.extensibilityStory: Not a menu library and not a competitor to the others — it is a command-palette/filterable-list engine. It solves a problem bbox-ui may want LATER (a searchable action palette over the same action list), and it composes rather than conflicts: cmdk inside a Base UI `Menu.Popup` or `Popover.Popup` is a normal pattern. Note apps/docs/src/registry/new-york-v4/ui/command.tsx currently builds its command surface on Base UI's Dialog, not on cmdk.

libraries.name: Floating UI (@floating-ui/react-dom, @floating-ui/dom)
libraries.license: MIT — verified on disk for both @floating-ui/dom@1.8.0 and @floating-ui/react-dom@2.1.9 package.json files. Already installed transitively AS A DEPENDENCY OF @base-ui/react.
libraries.whatItGives: Fetched from floating-ui.com/docs/useFloating: `useFloating` returns `refs` (`reference`, `floating`, `setReference()`, `setFloating()`), `floatingStyles`, `placement` (the FINAL placement after middleware), `x`, `y`, `context`, `middlewareData`, `isPositioned`, `update()`. Option `whileElementsMounted` takes `autoUpdate`. Middleware: `offset`, `inline`, `shift`, `flip`, `autoPlacement`, `size`, `arrow`, `hide`.
libraries.howItStructures: Not a component library — a positioning engine every one of the above sits on. Virtual elements (floating-ui.com/docs/virtual-elements) require only a `getBoundingClientRect()` returning `{x, y, top, left, bottom, right, width, height}`, with optional `contextElement` for clipping and `getClientRects` for ranges. Documented uses: cursor coordinates, context menus, custom reference areas.
libraries.extensibilityStory: Using it DIRECTLY is the escape hatch of last resort — full control, but you then own dismissal, focus trapping, roving tabindex, typeahead and ARIA wiring, which is the bulk of the work. The right move is to reach for it only through Base UI's already-exposed positioner props, which forward the same concepts (`anchor`, `sideOffset` as a function, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `sticky`, `positionMethod`).

structuralPatterns.pattern: Slot/render composition — the kit's styled component BECOMES the primitive's part instead of wrapping it. This is what makes a copy-paste component extensible without forking: a consumer swaps the element, or composes two primitives on one DOM node, with zero wrapper divs polluting the canvas layout.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: @base-ui/react — `BaseUIComponentProps.render` (internals/types.d.ts:21-33). Radix's equivalent is the boolean `asChild` + `@radix-ui/react-slot`.
structuralPatterns.apiShape:
// Base UI: `render` takes an element OR a function that RECEIVES state
<Menu.Item render={<MyRow icon={<Trash />} />}>Delete</Menu.Item>

<Menu.Item render={(props, state) => (
  <div {...props} className={state.highlighted ? "bg-accent" : ""} />
)} />

// The toolbar case, verbatim from base-ui.com/react/components/toolbar:
<Toolbar.Root>
  <Menu.Root>
    <Toolbar.Button render={<Menu.Trigger />} />
    <Menu.Portal>{/* … */}</Menu.Portal>
  </Menu.Root>
</Toolbar.Root>
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Base UI's function form is strictly more capable than Radix `asChild` (the child sees State, not just merged props), but it is also a bigger API surface to teach, and prop-merge order matters: per the useRender docs, event handlers merge, `className`/`style` join, and other external props OVERWRITE internal ones — so a careless consumer can clobber an ARIA attribute the primitive set.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Detached trigger via a handle object — the thing that opens the menu and the menu's content need not be in the same React subtree, and the trigger can hand the menu a typed payload. For a canvas app this is the decisive pattern: the trigger is a block on the canvas (or a floating toolbar button rendered in a portal), while the menu content lives once, at the app root, parameterised by which block opened it.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: @base-ui/react — `Menu.createHandle()` / `MenuHandle<Payload>` (menu/store/MenuHandle.d.ts), `handle` + `payload` props on `MenuTrigger` (menu/trigger/MenuTrigger.d.ts), and `children?: React.ReactNode | PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` on `MenuRoot` (menu/root/MenuRoot.d.ts). Ariakit's `useMenuStore()` is the nearest analogue; Radix and Headless UI have NO equivalent.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Buys exactly the decoupling bbox-ui's "props in, DOM out" rule wants — menu content is defined once and knows nothing about canvas coordinates. Cost: the handle is a mutable object created outside React, so it must be module-scope or memoised, and the docs are explicit that imperative `open()`/`close()` only take effect while a root is attached — calls before mount or after unmount are silently ignored, which is a real footgun in a host that mounts panels lazily.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Virtual-element anchoring — position a popup against an arbitrary screen rect rather than a DOM node. This is the seam that lets a menu follow a canvas selection, a cursor, or a block whose visual is drawn on a <canvas> and has no element to point at, WITHOUT the menu component learning anything about the canvas engine.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: @base-ui/react — `UseAnchorPositioningSharedParameters.anchor` (internals/useAnchorPositioning.d.ts:78), forwarded onto `Menu.Positioner`/`Popover.Positioner`. The underlying contract is Floating UI's VirtualElement (floating-ui.com/docs/virtual-elements).
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Keeps the canvas-engine coupling in ONE function the host supplies, which is exactly the core rule. But the anchor is pull-based: the rect is re-read on Floating UI's `autoUpdate` schedule, not on every canvas transform tick, so a menu anchored to a shape during a fast pan/zoom can visibly lag. A host that needs pixel-locked tracking has to force `update()` from its own render loop.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Items-as-data with a render function — a menu's contents are an ARRAY, and the component maps it. A host extends a menu by contributing objects to a list; it never edits JSX it does not own. This is the difference between "extensible" and "forkable" for a plugin-shaped host.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: react-aria-components — `<Menu items={…}>{(item) => …}</Menu>` (react-aria.adobe.com/Menu, quoted verbatim below). Base UI has NO collection API; its menus are always children-as-elements.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Data-driven menus are trivially mergeable, orderable and filterable by a host, and serialize — which also makes them testable without a DOM. The cost is a closed set: anything the data schema does not model (a colour swatch row, an inline slider, a nested code editor — all of which bbox-ui's floating toolbar screenshots show) needs an escape hatch back to JSX, so in practice you need BOTH doors, and maintaining both is real work.

structuralPatterns.pattern: A first-class hook for authoring your OWN part in the library's idiom — so a kit component that the library does not ship still merges props, projects state to data-attributes, and honours `render` identically to a stock part. Without this, every custom component is a second-class citizen and composition breaks at exactly the seams a design kit adds.
structuralPatterns.exemplar: @base-ui/react — `useRender` (use-render/useRender.d.ts) + `mergeProps` (merge-props/). Already in use in this repo at packages/inspector/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:2-3 and button-group.tsx:1-2, and apps/docs/src/registry/new-york-v4/ui/sidebar.tsx:3-4.
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: This is the cheapest possible adoption path — a bbox-ui component can present a Base-UI-shaped surface while importing only `use-render`/`merge-props`, two of the lightest subpaths in the package. The catch is that `useRender` returns a ReactElement, not props, so a component using it cannot ALSO spread onto something else; and it locks the kit's prop-merge semantics to Base UI's, which is a soft dependency on that library's conventions even where the runtime import is tiny.

structuralPatterns.pattern: A roving-tabindex CONTAINER that other primitives compose into, rather than a toolbar that owns a fixed list of item types. The toolbar supplies focus management and orientation; each item independently supplies its own behaviour (menu trigger, toggle, tooltip, input).
structuralPatterns.exemplar: @base-ui/react — `Toolbar.Root` (`orientation`, `loopFocus`, `ToolbarRootItemMetadata { disabled, focusableWhenDisabled }` in toolbar/root/ToolbarRoot.d.ts) + `Toolbar.Button` (`focusableWhenDisabled` default TRUE, toolbar/button/ToolbarButton.d.ts). Radix Toolbar is the same pattern with `orientation` + `loop`.
structuralPatterns.apiShape:
<Toolbar.Root orientation="horizontal" loopFocus>
  <Toolbar.Button render={<Menu.Trigger />} />        {/* popout */}
  <Toolbar.Separator />
  <ToggleGroup value={tool} onValueChange={setTool}>
    <Toolbar.Button render={<Toggle value="select" />} />
  </ToggleGroup>
  {/* tooltip inverts the nesting — see base-ui toolbar docs */}
  <Tooltip.Root><Tooltip.Trigger render={<Toolbar.Button />} /></Tooltip.Root>
</Toolbar.Root>
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: One focus model for the whole strip, and the same Toolbar serves the bottom tool bar, the top-left bread-crumb strip and the floating selection toolbar with no new component. Two sharp edges verified in the docs: the nesting direction is NOT uniform (`Toolbar.Button render={<Menu.Trigger/>}` for menus, but `Tooltip.Trigger render={<Toolbar.Button/>}` for tooltips), and horizontal arrow keys collide with text-cursor movement inside `Toolbar.Input`, which is why that part exists as its own type.

refs.recommendation:
Take Base UI, and take it because it is already here — do not add a second menu runtime.

The decisive on-disk fact: `@base-ui/react` is the ONLY menu-capable headless library that any workspace package depends on. Four package.json files declare it (`apps/storybook-basics` ^1.8.0, `apps/docs`, `packages/inspector`, `packages/glyph-picker`), and nothing else in the repo declares Radix, Ariakit, React Aria, Headless UI or cmdk. Radix reaches node_modules only under `tldraw@5.3.2`; react-aria-components only inside Storybook's own bundle. Adopting any alternative means shipping a second dismissable-layer/focus-scope/positioning stack beside one already paid for.

It also passes the copy-paste-registry test, which is the test that actually binds here. `registry.json`'s `dependencies` array is how shadcn npm-installs a component's deps into the consumer's project (`apps/docs/src/registry/registry-ui.ts:7` already does `dependencies: ["@base-ui/react"]`). `@base-ui/react` is public and MIT, so it is a legal registry dependency — unlike `@bbox-ui/core` and `@bbox-ui/glyph-content`, whose `private: true` is exactly what blocks `block-node-reactflow`, `block-shape-tldraw` and `glyph` today. A menu item built on Base UI installs and compiles for a stranger; one built on a workspace package does not.

And the trunk has already made this call once: `apps/storybook-basics/src/components/dropdown-menu.tsx` is the stock shadcn `new-york` DropdownMenu over `MenuPrimitive` from `@base-ui/react/menu`, with a header comment stating the reasoning ("this app already depends on @base-ui/react, no new package needed"). `toggle.tsx` and `tooltip.tsx` sit on the same base. The menu port extends that lineage rather than opening a new one.

Concretely, for the seven menu surfaces in the ask:
- **Bottom tool bar, top-left strip, floating toolbar chrome** → `Toolbar.Root` + `Toolbar.Button` + `Toolbar.Separator`, with `Toolbar.Button render={<Menu.Trigger />}` for every popout. One roving-tabindex model across all three. Note the trunk's existing `bar.tsx` is a pure three-slot LAYOUT strip with a deliberate computed grid template and no focus behaviour — Toolbar should compose INSIDE a `Bar` slot, not replace it; conflating them would destroy the documented `barGridTemplateColumns` rationale.
- **Floating toolbar popouts anchored to a canvas selection** → `Menu.Positioner`'s `anchor` accepting a Floating UI `VirtualElement` (`() => ({ getBoundingClientRect })`), plus `collisionBoundary` set to the canvas viewport and `positionMethod="fixed"`. This is the single API that satisfies "the core imports no canvas engine": the host passes one rect-producing function, and the menu component stays props-in/DOM-out.
- **Burger/file menu with nested settings** → `Menu.SubmenuRoot` + `Menu.SubmenuTrigger`; typeahead is built in, overridable per item via `MenuItem.label`.
- **Draft selector, breadcrumb dropdown, per-block context menus** → `Menu.createHandle<Payload>()` with `payload` on each trigger and a function child on `Menu.Root`. Define the menu ONCE, parameterise by which block/draft opened it. Radix and Headless UI cannot do this at all; Ariakit's store can, but buys nothing Base UI does not already give.
- **Frames / problems / compare-changes panels** → these are panels, not menus. Their list rows should NOT be `Menu.Item` (that pulls in menu roving-focus and close-on-click semantics they do not want). Build them on the kit's own row primitives via `useRender` + `mergeProps`, which is the pattern `packages/inspector/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx` already uses.

Steal exactly one idea from elsewhere: **react-aria-components' items-as-data collection API**. Its `<Menu items={items}>{(item) => <MenuItem/>}</Menu>` is the one structural thing Base UI genuinely lacks, and it is the thing that makes a menu extensible by a host that cannot edit the JSX. Reproduce the SHAPE, not the library — give bbox-ui's menu a `actions?: MenuAction[]` data door alongside the children-as-elements door, mapping `MenuAction` onto Base UI parts internally. That is ~40 lines, adds no dependency, and keeps the JSX door open for the rich rows (colour swatches, sliders, inline editors) visible in the floating-toolbar screenshots that no data schema will model well.

Rule out: **Headless UI** (no submenu API at all — disqualifying for the burger menu and toolbar popouts, and its closed `anchor` prop gives no positioner part to hand a virtual element). **Ariakit** and **Radix** (capable, but every differentiator is already covered, so they are a net-new runtime for zero new capability). **cmdk** is not a competitor — park it as the future filterable-action-palette engine, composed inside a Base UI popup, if that surface is ever wanted.

Do NOT reach for `@floating-ui/react` directly. It is already present as Base UI's own dependency (and Base UI even vendors a `floating-ui-react/` subpath), and Base UI forwards everything needed — `anchor`, `sideOffset` as an offset function, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`, `sticky`, `positionMethod`. Using it raw means re-owning dismissal, focus trapping, roving tabindex, typeahead and ARIA, which is the majority of the work.

Two caveats to carry into implementation. (1) `Menu.createHandle()` returns a mutable non-React object whose imperative `open()`/`close()` are documented to be **silently ignored** while no root is mounted — lazily-mounted panels will hit this. (2) Virtual-element anchoring is pull-based on Floating UI's `autoUpdate` schedule, so a menu anchored to a shape will visibly lag a fast pan/zoom unless the host calls `update()` from its own render loop; decide deliberately whether menus close on canvas transform instead.

refs.area: Schema-driven menu contribution systems — config registry (data describing menus) vs compound components (JSX describing menus), and whether bbox-ui can ship both

libraries.license: MIT — LICENSE on disk reads "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2019 Material-UI SAS"; package.json "license": "MIT", version 1.8.0

ContextMenu parts: root, trigger, positioner. `MenuItemProps { onClick?, disabled?, label?, id?, closeOnClick?: boolean }` (menu/item/MenuItem.d.ts). Public hook `useRender` exported from @base-ui/react/use-render.
libraries.howItStructures: Pure compound components — one React context per Root, parts addressed as `Menu.Root` / `Menu.Trigger` / `Menu.Portal` / `Menu.Positioner` / `Menu.Popup` / `Menu.Item` / `Menu.SubmenuRoot`. No data schema anywhere: the tree IS the JSX. bbox-ui's trunk already wraps exactly this in apps/storybook-basics/src/components/dropdown-menu.tsx, whose header comment says it is the stock shadcn new-york DropdownMenu over Base UI's Menu primitive, exporting DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuPortal, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuTrigger.
libraries.extensibilityStory: Two seams, both verified in internals/types.d.ts:21-39. (1) `BaseUIComponentProps.render?: React.ReactElement | ComponentRenderFn<RenderFunctionProps, State>` — every part accepts a replacement element or a render function, so a registry-generated item can swap the tag or compose another component without forking the part. (2) `className?: string | ((state: State) => string | undefined)` and `style` likewise take the state, so variant styling is a function of state rather than a prop matrix. `useRender({ render, ref, state, stateAttributesMapping, props, enabled, defaultTagName })` is the same machinery exported publicly, which is what lets bbox-ui build its OWN parts (a Bar item, a floating-toolbar button) that behave like Base UI parts. Crucially for this repo: @base-ui/react is a public MIT npm package, so a shadcn registry item can list it in `dependencies` and a consumer can actually install it — unlike @bbox-ui/core or @bbox-ui/glyph-content, which are private:true and are the known blocker for the two adapters and glyph.tsx.

libraries.name: VS Code — `contributes.menus` / `contributes.commands` / `contributes.submenus` (declarative) and `MenuRegistry` / `registerAction2` (runtime)
libraries.license: MIT (microsoft/vscode source), but NOT a dependency — nothing here is npm-installable outside the VS Code host. Pattern to copy, ~150 lines, not a package to add.
libraries.whatItGives: Declarative layer (code.visualstudio.com/api/references/contribution-points): `contributes.commands` keys `command`, `title`, `category`, `icon`, `enablement`, `shortTitle`; `contributes.menus` item keys `command`, `submenu`, `when`, `group`, `alt`; `contributes.submenus` entries `{ id, label }`; `contributes.keybindings` keys `command`, `key`, `mac`, `linux`, `win`, `when`. Runtime layer (src/vs/platform/actions/common/actions.ts, fetched): `interface IMenuItem { command: ICommandAction; alt?: ICommandAction; when?: ContextKeyExpression; group?: 'navigation' | string; order?: number; isHiddenByDefault?: boolean }`; `interface ISubmenuItem { title; submenu: MenuId; icon?: Icon; when?; group?; order?; isSelection?; isSplitButton? }`; `MenuId` with 200+ static instances (`MenuId.CommandPalette`, `MenuId.EditorContext`) plus `static for(identifier: string): MenuId`; `MenuRegistry.addCommand(userCommand: ICommandAction): IDisposable`, `MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem(menu: MenuId, item: IMenuItem | ISubmenuItem): IDisposable`, `MenuRegistry.getMenuItems(loc: MenuId): Array<IMenuItem | ISubmenuItem>`; `abstract class Action2 { constructor(readonly desc: Readonly<IAction2Options>); abstract run(accessor, ...args) }` and `registerAction2(ctor): IDisposable`, where `interface IAction2CommonOptions extends ICommandAction { menu?: OneOrN<{ id: MenuId; precondition?: null } & Omit<IMenuItem, 'command'>>; keybinding?: OneOrN<Omit<IKeybindingRule,'id'>> }`.
libraries.howItStructures: Three orthogonal registries naming one string id. A command declares identity + presentation + availability ONCE; a menu contribution is pure placement data `{ command|submenu, when, group, order }` that carries no body, no label, no icon. Sorting is `group@order`: groups sort lexicographically (which is why the predefined names are numbered — editor/context is `navigation`, `1_modification`, `9_cutcopypaste`, `z_commands`; explorer/context is `navigation`, `2_workspace`, `3_compare`, `4_search`, `5_cutcopypaste`, `6_copypath`, `7_modification`), and `@<number>` orders within a group. `navigation` is special-cased to sort first everywhere.
libraries.extensibilityStory: Adding an item to a menu is one JSON object or one `MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem` call and it returns an `IDisposable` — a view contributes while mounted and un-contributes on unmount, no host edit. Removing one is disposing that handle. Reordering is editing a string. The load-bearing rule, quoted from the docs page: "`when` clauses apply to menus and `enablement` clauses to commands. The `enablement` applies to all menus and even keybindings while the `when` only applies to a single menu." `registerAction2` is the sugar that lets one class declare command + N menu placements + N keybindings together — the ergonomic form of the same split, not a different model.

libraries.name: Tweakpane 4.0.5 + @tweakpane/core
libraries.license: MIT (package.json "license": "MIT"); read on disk at /home/bam/AFFiNE/node_modules/tweakpane and /home/bam/AFFiNE/node_modules/@tweakpane/core
libraries.whatItGives: `Pane` (dist/types/pane/pane.d.ts) extends `RootApi`, with `registerPlugin(bundle: TpPluginBundle)`. `ContainerApi` (@tweakpane/core/dist/blade/common/api/container.d.ts) is the whole authoring surface: `readonly children: BladeApi[]`, `addButton(params: ButtonParams): ButtonApi`, `addFolder(params: FolderParams): FolderApi`, `addTab(params: TabParams): TabApi`, `add(api: BladeApi, opt_index?: number): void`, `remove(api: BladeApi): void`, `addBinding<O extends Bindable, Key extends keyof O>(object: O, key: Key, opt_params?: BindingParams): BindingApi<unknown, O[Key]>`, `addBlade(params: BaseBladeParams): BladeApi`. Params base (@tweakpane/core/dist/common/params.d.ts): `BaseParams { disabled?, hidden?, index? }`, `BindingParams { label?, tag?, view? }`, `PickerLayout = 'inline' | 'popup'`, `ListParamsOptions<T> = ArrayStyleListOptions<T> | ObjectStyleListOptions<T>` where the array style is `{ text: string; value: T }[]`.
libraries.howItStructures: Imperative builder over a value graph, not JSX. `addBinding(object, key)` binds a control to a live property; you never say which widget. Widget selection is a chain-of-responsibility over a plugin pool: `InputBindingPlugin<In, Ex, P>` (@tweakpane/core/dist/input-binding/plugin.d.ts) has `type: 'input'` and `accept: (exValue: unknown, params: Record<string, unknown>) => Acceptance<Ex, P> | null` — documented as "A typed value if the plugin accepts the input, or null if the plugin sees them off and pass them to the next plugin." Then `binding: { reader, constraint?, equals?, writer }` and `controller: (args) => ValueController<In>`.
libraries.extensibilityStory: A new widget family is a new plugin object registered with `pane.registerPlugin()` — nothing in the host switches on a kind enum, and no existing plugin changes. `accept` returning null is the only extension point; first match wins. `view?: string` on BindingParams is the call-site override when you want a non-default widget for an accepted type. This is the cleanest verified answer to "how do I add a new control kind without editing a renderer's if-chain" — and it is exactly the problem SystemSketch's `ContextualGlyphFamily` lookup table solves by hand today.

libraries.name: leva 0.10.1
libraries.license: MIT (registry.npmjs.org/leva/latest); peerDependencies react ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0, react-dom ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0
libraries.whatItGives: packages/leva/src/index.ts exports exactly: `useControls` (from ./useControls), `Leva`, `LevaPanel` (from ./components/Leva), `useStoreContext`, `LevaStoreProvider` (from ./context), `levaStore`, `useCreateStore` (from ./store), `export * from './helpers'`, and `LevaInputs`. helpers/index.ts is exactly four lines: `export * from './folder'`, `'./button'`, `'./buttonGroup'`, `'./monitor'`. Verified signature: `export function folder<S extends Schema>(schema: S, settings?: FolderSettings): FolderInput<SchemaToValues<S>>` returning `{ type: SpecialInputs.FOLDER, schema, settings }`. Types declared under dist/declarations/src/types/{public,internal,utils}.d.ts; `useControls` is heavily overloaded across `schemaOrFolderName`, `settingsOrDepsOrSchema`, `depsOrSettingsOrFolderSettings`, `depsOrSettings`, `depsOrUndefined`.
libraries.howItStructures: One plain-object schema in, typed values out: `const { size, color } = useControls({ size: 1, color: '#f00' })`. Input kind is inferred from the VALUE (a number is a slider, a hex string is a colour picker), overridable by an options object. Nesting is data — `folder({...}, { collapsed: true })` is a value INSIDE the schema object, never a JSX wrapper. `button` / `buttonGroup` / `monitor` are the same trick for non-bound entries. The panel component (`LevaPanel`) is decoupled from the schema via a store (`useCreateStore`, `LevaStoreProvider`), so one schema can be rendered by a panel mounted anywhere in the tree.
libraries.extensibilityStory: `createPlugin` (dist/declarations/src/plugin.d.ts) + the `leva/plugin` entry point; leva's own nine input types (Number, Select, Color, String, Boolean, Vector3d, Vector2d, Image, Interval) are registered through the same `register` call in index.ts that a third-party plugin uses. The store/panel split is the strongest idea for bbox-ui: the schema can live in a host-agnostic module while the surface that draws it is chosen per host. The weakness for this brief: leva is a property panel, not a menu — no `when`, no groups-with-order, no command ids, and its styling is stitches-based and not Tailwind, so copying its code is not on the table.

libraries.name: kbar 1.0.0
libraries.license: MIT (registry.npmjs.org/kbar/latest); peer react ^17||^18||^19; deps fuse.js ^7.5.0, fast-equals ^2.0.3, tiny-invariant ^1.2.0, @radix-ui/react-portal ^1.1.17, @tanstack/react-virtual ^3.14.9
libraries.whatItGives: src/types.ts exports `ActionId`, `Priority`, `ActionSection`, `Action`, `ActionStore`, `ActionTree`, `ActionGroup`, `KBarOptions`, `KBarProviderProps`, `KBarState`, `KBarQuery`, `IKBarContext`, `VisualState` (enum), `HistoryItem`, `History`. The core type verbatim: `export type Action = { id: ActionId; name: string; shortcut?: string[]; keywords?: string; section?: ActionSection; icon?: string | React.ReactElement | React.ReactNode; subtitle?: string; perform?: (currentActionImpl: ActionImpl) => any; parent?: ActionId; priority?: Priority }`.
libraries.howItStructures: A flat array of Actions is the whole model; the command tree is reconstructed from `parent: ActionId` back-references, grouping from `section`, ordering from `priority`. `perform` is the body and lives on the action, once. This is the closest verified npm package to "a config registry for commands" in React.
libraries.extensibilityStory: Actions are registered from anywhere in the tree and un-register on unmount — the same disposable-contribution shape as `MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem`. But note what is missing against VS Code: there is no `when` / `enablement` predicate at all (availability has to be done by adding/removing actions), and no `group@order` string — `priority` is a number on the action, not on the placement, so one action cannot sit in two surfaces at two positions. That single gap is why kbar is a good palette and a poor contextual-menu engine, and it is the reason I would copy VS Code's IMenuItem shape rather than kbar's Action shape.

libraries.name: @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu 2.1.20 (the alternative primitive family — recommended AGAINST here)
libraries.license: MIT; read on disk at /home/bam/Agentero/node_modules/.pnpm/@radix-ui+react-dropdown-menu@2.1.20_.../node_modules/@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu/dist/index.d.ts
libraries.whatItGives: Declared exports: `createDropdownMenuScope`, `DropdownMenu`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `DropdownMenuPortal`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuGroup`, `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`, `DropdownMenuItemIndicator`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`, `DropdownMenuArrow`, `DropdownMenuSub`, `DropdownMenuSubTrigger`, `DropdownMenuSubContent`, plus the short aliases `Root`, `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Content`, `Group`, `Label`, `Item`, `CheckboxItem`, `RadioGroup`, `RadioItem`, `ItemIndicator`, `Separator`, `Arrow`, `Sub`, `SubTrigger`, `SubContent`.
