libraries.extensibilityStory: Functionally equivalent to Base UI for this job. The reason to say no: bbox-ui's trunk already standardised on @base-ui/react for dropdown-menu.tsx, toggle.tsx, tooltip.tsx and collapsible.tsx, and SystemSketch's own popovers are Radix. Porting the menus into bbox-ui with Radix would leave the kit shipping two primitive families with two different composition escape hatches (`asChild` vs `render`), which is the same class of mistake as the pre-existing `port` / `port-v2` split. Pick Base UI, because it is already the trunk's dependency and is already what the stock file installs.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Declare the verb once, reference it by id from every surface — a menu entry is placement data with no body, no label and no icon
structuralPatterns.exemplar: VS Code — `MenuRegistry.addCommand(ICommandAction)` + `MenuRegistry.appendMenuItem(MenuId, IMenuItem)`; declarative twin `contributes.commands` + `contributes.menus`
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: You give up the ability to read a menu's contents by reading one file — the entries are scattered across every module that contributes. VS Code pays for this with a MenuId enum of 200+ statics and a `getMenuItems` you must call to know what is actually there. For a component kit that is the right trade only if hosts genuinely need to contribute; for a menu whose items are fixed forever, the JSX is shorter and more legible.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Sorting and grouping are a string, not an array position — `group@order` with numbered group names
structuralPatterns.exemplar: VS Code `IMenuItem.group?: 'navigation' | string` + `order?: number`; predefined names `navigation`, `1_modification`, `9_cutcopypaste`, `z_commands`
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Numbered prefixes are load-bearing but invisible to the type system — a typo in a group name silently creates a new group with its own separator rather than failing. SystemSketch's `ContextualControlRecipe.groups[].items[]` uses array position instead, which is typo-proof (the kind is a union) but means a third-party contribution cannot land between two existing items without rewriting the recipe.

structuralPatterns.pattern: The availability predicate belongs to the verb, not to the widget — and it must be answerable WITHOUT running the verb
structuralPatterns.exemplar: VS Code `enablement` on the command vs `when` on the menu item (docs: "The `enablement` applies to all menus and even keybindings while the `when` only applies to a single menu"); `IAction2CommonOptions.menu.precondition?: null` is the per-placement opt-out
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Two predicates that look identical and differ only in scope is a genuine footgun — and the vault has already paid for a related one: `Commands vs UI Triggers (2026-07-25)` records that in a when clause a bare word is a context-key lookup, not a string, so `selectedBlockKind == call` silently compares against an unset key and is always false. If bbox-ui adopts when-expressions it must ship the unit check that catches the unquoted-literal form, not just the evaluator.

structuralPatterns.pattern: The widget is chosen from what the item is BOUND to, never restated at the call site — and new widget kinds arrive as accept-or-pass plugins rather than a renderer if-chain
structuralPatterns.exemplar: Blender `UILayout.prop()`; Tweakpane `InputBindingPlugin.accept`
structuralPatterns.apiShape:
# Blender: 'Exposes an RNA item and places it into the layout' — no widget named
prop(data, property, text='', icon='NONE', expand=False, slider=False,
     toggle=-1, icon_only=False, emboss=True, index=-1, invert_checkbox=False)
// Tweakpane: same idea, as a chain of responsibility
accept: (exValue: unknown, params: Record<string, unknown>) =>
  Acceptance<Ex, P> | null   // null ⇒ pass to the next plugin
pane.addBinding(shape, 'strokeWidth', { min: 1, max: 8 })  // slider, unasked
pane.registerPlugin(myBundle)  // new kind, zero host edits
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Inference is delightful until it is wrong, and then the override syntax is where all the complexity goes — Blender's prop() carries fifteen keyword arguments that exist only to un-choose the inferred widget (`expand`, `slider`, `toggle`, `icon_only`, `emboss`), and Tweakpane needs `view?: string` for the same reason. Inference also cannot express "this string is a colour" without a params hint, which is precisely why SystemSketch's registry names a `glyph` family explicitly instead of inferring.

structuralPatterns.pattern: Nesting lives in the data, not in a JSX wrapper — a submenu/folder is a VALUE inside the schema
structuralPatterns.exemplar: leva `folder(schema, settings)`; Tweakpane `ContainerApi.addFolder(params)` / `addBlade(params)`; VS Code `ISubmenuItem { submenu: MenuId }`
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: leva's inline-object nesting keeps the whole panel readable in one place but makes the child un-contributable from elsewhere; VS Code's id-reference nesting is the opposite — a host can fill a submenu it did not declare, at the cost that no single file tells you what is in it. These are the same trade as pattern 1, one level down, and a kit can legitimately choose differently for the two cases (inline for an inspector panel, id-reference for a context menu).

structuralPatterns.pattern: The render prop is the seam that lets a config registry emit stock JSX without the registry knowing about React — so a kit can ship BOTH layers over one primitive
structuralPatterns.exemplar: Base UI `BaseUIComponentProps.render?: React.ReactElement | ComponentRenderFn<RenderFunctionProps, State>` and the public `useRender({ render, state, props, defaultTagName, stateAttributesMapping, enabled })`
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: Two layers means two ways to do the same thing, and a codebase will drift toward whichever is nearer to hand — which is exactly the six-parallel-lists failure the vault already measured in workbench. The mitigation that VS Code uses and a kit should copy: the JSX layer is the PRIMITIVE and has no opinions, the registry is the only place a real product verb may be declared, and the renderer is small enough (~40 lines) that nobody is tempted to hand-roll a second one.

structuralPatterns.pattern: A flat array plus a parent id is the cheapest command tree — but it cannot express one verb in two places at two positions
structuralPatterns.exemplar: kbar `Action { id; name; shortcut?; keywords?; section?; icon?; subtitle?; perform?; parent?: ActionId; priority?: Priority }`
structuralPatterns.apiShape:
const actions: Action[] = [
  { id: 'turn-into', name: 'Turn into', section: 'Structure' },
  { id: 'turn-into-block', name: 'Block', parent: 'turn-into',
    perform: () => editor.turnInto('block') },
  { id: 'detach', name: 'Detach to primitive', shortcut: ['d'],
    keywords: 'explode ungroup', priority: Priority.HIGH,
    perform: () => editor.detach() },
]
structuralPatterns.tradeoff: `priority` sits on the action, not on the placement, and there is no `when` at all — so availability is expressed by adding and removing actions from the array, and a verb that should be item 2 in the context menu and item 7 in the toolbar cannot say so. Good enough for a palette (where there is only one surface), structurally wrong for the floating toolbar + right-click menu + burger menu trio bbox-ui actually has.

refs.recommendation:
**Take the compound-component layer entirely off the shelf, write the registry ourselves (~150 lines, copied from VS Code's shape), and — most important — stop treating the floating appearance toolbar as a menu at all. It is a property panel, and every library says so.**

Concretely:

**1. The JSX layer is already stock and already installed — do not rebuild it.** `@base-ui/react@1.8.0` (MIT, verified on disk in bbox-ui's node_modules) ships `Menu` (21 parts incl. `submenu-root`, `submenu-trigger`, `checkbox-item`, `radio-item`, `group-label`), `ContextMenu` (root/trigger/positioner), `Menubar`, and `Toolbar` (`Root`/`Group`/`Button`/`Link`/`Input`/`Separator`, with `orientation` and `loopFocus`). The trunk's `apps/storybook-basics/src/components/dropdown-menu.tsx` already wraps it with the 15 stock shadcn exports. **`Toolbar.Root` is the part the bottom toolbar and the floating toolbar both want** and nothing in the kit has to own roving-focus or keyboard wrap. Missing pieces the port genuinely owns: the **placement policy** (FigJam's flip-not-clamp, gap 16 / margin 20 / height 40, and removal from the DOM during a drag — all already measured in `/home/bam/systemsketch/src/chrome/selectionMenuPlacement.ts` with 13 unit tests), and the **canvas screen-space layer**. Everything else is configuration.

**2. Copy VS Code's `IMenuItem` shape, not kbar's `Action`.** kbar (MIT, npm-installable) is the closest packaged config registry, but its `Action` has **no `when` predicate and puts `priority` on the action rather than the placement** — so one verb cannot be item 2 in the context menu and item 7 in the toolbar. That is exactly bbox-ui's case. Write `bbox/command-registry` instead: `CommandDef { id, title, shortTitle?, icon?, keybinding?, precondition? }` + `MenuItemDef { command | submenu, when?, group?, order? }` + `resolveMenu(menuId, ctx)` sorting group-lexicographic then order, with `navigation` special-cased first. Keep VS Code's `enablement` (command-wide, applies to keybindings too) vs `when` (this surface only) distinction — and **ship the unit check for the unquoted-literal when-clause bug** the vault already paid for (`when: "kind == call"` compares against an unset key and is silently always false).

**3. Split the two animals — this is the finding.** SystemSketch's `contextualControlRegistry.ts` (491 lines) has VS Code's *vocabulary* (`CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY`, `ContextualControlRecipe`, `composeContextualControls`) but Tweakpane's *semantics*: its `ContextualControl` carries `value: SharedStyle<string> | null`, `onSelect(value)`, `options[]`, `customSize.applyPx()` and `rungPx()` — that is `addBinding(object, key, params)`, not `appendMenuItem`. So the port should produce **two registries over one renderer family**:
  - `bbox/command-registry` — VS Code shape — for the burger file menu, the right-click context menu, the toolbar's tool buttons, the frames/problems panel row actions, the draft-selector and breadcrumb menus, undo/redo. Items have no value.
  - `bbox/control-registry` — Tweakpane/Blender shape — for the floating appearance toolbar and the inspector. Port `ContextualControlDefinition` more or less verbatim (`kind`, `label`, `options`, `layout`, `trigger`, `glyph`, `columns`), because its `ContextualGlyphFamily` lookup table is already the right instinct — but **replace the hand-maintained family union with Tweakpane's `accept(value, params) => Acceptance | null` chain**, so a host adding a control kind registers a plugin instead of editing `AppearanceGlyph.tsx`. Keep Blender's rule at the call site: the widget comes from what is bound, and `layout`/`trigger` are the un-choose overrides (Blender's `expand`/`slider`/`toggle`/`icon_only` play the same role).
  Conflating these is what produced an interface carrying both `onSelect` and `trigger` and `modePlacement`, and why `composeContextualControls` silently drops a candidate the recipe omits (the `lineShape` bug the file's own comment records).

**4. The registry→JSX seam is Base UI's `render` prop.** `BaseUIComponentProps.render?: ReactElement | ComponentRenderFn<Props, State>` (internals/types.d.ts:33) plus the public `useRender()` hook means the registry stays pure data with an optional `render` escape hatch, and the renderer is ~40 lines mapping resolved items onto `DropdownMenuGroup` / `DropdownMenuItem` / `DropdownMenuShortcut` / `Toolbar.Button`. Both layers ship; the JSX layer is the primitive with no opinions, the registry is the only place a product verb may be declared.

**5. Registry-packaging constraints, because they will bite.** `@base-ui/react`, `lucide-react`, `class-variance-authority`, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge` are all public npm and can go in a registry item's `dependencies` array — a consumer can install them. **`@bbox-ui/glyph-content` cannot** (`workspace:*`, `private: true`), and it is already why `glyph.tsx` is not a registry item. So `CommandDef.icon` and `MenuItemDef` must type as `React.ReactNode` and the menu items must never import the glyph package — otherwise the menu items inherit the exact unpublishable blocker that already stops `glyph`, `block-node-reactflow` and `block-shape-tldraw`. Also: use **Base UI, not Radix**. Radix's `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu@2.1.20` is equivalent in every way that matters, but adopting it would leave the kit shipping two primitive families with two different composition escape hatches (`asChild` vs `render`) — the same class of split as the existing `port` / `port-v2` problem.

**6. Do not add tweakpane, leva, or kbar as dependencies.** All three are MIT and all three are the wrong shape: Tweakpane is imperative and non-React, leva is stitches-styled (not Tailwind) and has no `when`/groups/command ids, kbar is a palette. Take their *patterns* — `accept`-chain widget dispatch, data-nesting via `folder(schema, settings)`, and the store/panel split (`useCreateStore` + `LevaStoreProvider` + `LevaPanel`) which is the best verified argument that the schema can live host-agnostic while the surface drawing it is chosen per host. That last one is precisely bbox-ui's "use it in any host" requirement.

**Vault verdict:** this is not an open design question. `C - Semantic Type Registry` already states the rule ("resolve semantics once, then project them many times… give plugins a constrained contribution point rather than an unbounded new visual language"), and `Commands vs UI Triggers (2026-07-25)` already ruled "clone VS Code's model wholesale; sequence it Zed's way", measured six parallel verb lists and ten resulting defects, named the four-layer split (gesture / trigger / command / document), and shipped the widened `Command<A>` interface with `when`, `scopeLabel` and `defaultArgs`. It also establishes that Obsidian is the *wrong* reference here (no `MenuItem.setCommand()`, so an Obsidian context menu cannot reference a command at all) — which matters because Obsidian is usually the reference app. The port should carry that ruling forward rather than re-deriving it.

design.verdict: Ship both layers, asymmetrically, with the boundary between two different animals SystemSketch conflates: command-shaped surfaces (file menu, context menu, tool dock, panels, draft bar, status strip) are compound components — JSX all the way down, because in a copy-paste registry the consumer owns the placement file and editing it IS the extension mechanism — while value-bound controls (the appearance pill, title formatting) keep SystemSketch's registry + recipe + resolver + one-renderer architecture, ported nearly verbatim as pure data with two changes: the registry becomes a factory (palettes/vocabularies injected, never imported) and the glyph table becomes a host-extendable Record. The control renderer is itself built from the compound parts (popover.tsx, toolbar.tsx), so one popup engine (Base UI, already a dependency) sits under both layers; a VS Code-style command registry is deliberately deferred as a reversible ~150-line later add. A host touches JSX for menus and data for controls.

components.propsSketch: menuLabModel.ts ports verbatim as the story's model (388 pure lines; only import is the registry). LabState.popoverMode collapses into the popover autoFocus/container props. The ?menu-lab route and Settings embedding do not travel.

hostContract: container?: HTMLElement | null — portal target inside the host's token scope, on every popup-bearing component. Replaces both document.querySelector('.systemsketch-theme-root') sites; the kit must never query the DOM.
popupClassName? / host CSS on [data-slot=…] — stacking and z-order. The kit ships zero z-index; layering is host policy (the drafts-bar --systemsketch-layer-modal lesson is the documented example).
autoFocus?: boolean on popovers — host passes false while a live text editor must keep focus (the pill's editing mode); replaces the tldraw-vs-Radix popoverMode switch.
onPanelPointerDownCapture?: React.PointerEventHandler — the 'this pointer event is mine' seam (tldraw markEventAsHandled or nothing); the kit only forwards it.

Floating toolbar placement loop (host-owned end to end): measure the rendered bar via the exposed ref (ResizeObserver/getBoundingClientRect), read selection+viewport rects in screen space from the engine, call placeFloatingToolbar({selection, menu, viewport, bottomObstacleTop?, overlayInset}) — overlayInset is now REQUIRED (its 5px default was measured against tldraw's handles) — gate on its own isManipulating, guard async placement with a monotonic pass counter (donor placementPass WHY documented), re-run on camera/size/scale change, and pass maxWidth = floatingToolbarMaxWidth(viewport, scale) while mirroring the same scale in its CSS (the two-place invariant).

Wheel pass-through: host attaches its own hook to the FloatingToolbar/ChromeBar ref; the kit wraps and never scrolls horizontally so redispatch hooks stay safe (the four nested flex-wrap levels survive; usePassThroughWheelEvents does not).

Control bindings: host writes the binder — bindControl(kind, {id, value: ControlValue<string>|null, onSelect(value?,{continuous?}), automaticOption?, customSize?: {sharedPx, onPresetRungs, applyPx, minPx, maxPx} as plain VALUES recomputed per render (no signals/thunks), rungPxByValue?, modeControl?/modePlacement?}); hostTag branching (HOW to write a value) lives entirely in the binder, as does any restructure-candidates precondition, which must be stated beside the recipe that requires it (the lost-lineShape lesson).

resolveSwatchHex(name) => string | undefined — or a palette whose entries carry hexes — injected into swatchGlyph; the registry factory takes palette names + column count as construction input (CONTEXTUAL_CONTROL_REGISTRY stops being a module const).

Tool dock: activeToolId + activeVariant? from the engine; families/simpleTools as data with icon: ReactNode (no string icon registry); preferences + onPreferencesChange controlled (storage — localStorage, file, nothing — is a host adapter carrying 'Preferences are helpful feedback, never a reason to block drawing'); real keybindings host-wired (hints are display-only; the split is documented so they cannot silently drift — derived arrow hints stay derived); the press-tile-then-draw click-capture CSS written by the host against the exposed data-bbox-family-open hook; family footer content + its selection predicate.

Chrome bar: crumbs/depth/canGoBack/canGoForward as plain data (no TLShapeId, no signals); onBack/onForward/onReturnToRoot/onJumpToLevel callbacks (all void); global gestures — F2, mouse buttons 3/4, BrowserBack/Forward — wired host-side onto the same callbacks (with the donor's measured note that only mouseup reliably cancels button navigation in Chrome); identity {title, statusTone, statusLabel, path?} plus onCommitRename/onSaveAs/onCopyPath/onReveal/onTrash; confirm dialogs, toasts, and clipboard are host's.

BranchChip: {isDraftMode, draftCount, activeDraftName, drafts: DraftSummary[], activeDraftId} + onSwitchTo/onCreate/onRename/onDiscard; secondaryLabel computed host-side (the baseLabel-fabrication guard is drafts semantics); renderTrigger kept as the proven re-skin seam.

Panels: models as props (items+previews for Frames; groups+counts+severities for Problems); every mutation a callback returning {ok, reason} so validation feedback travels as data; locks as separate props (readOnly / reorderLocked / landmarksLocked — the three notices say different useful things); drag gesture bolted onto dragHandleProps/dragging/dropTarget; open/close state and Escape policy host-owned (the chromeState LRU reducer is a documented 60-line recipe, not a kit export).

Compare: comparison computed host-side (ported pure compareBoards over structural RecordLike, or any other diff — recordsOfSnapshot stays in the tldraw adapter); version discovery/snapshots host-side (versions: HistoryRecord[], problem?: string); both pane renderers as render props; camera framing via onFrameChange(change|null) — ONE rule — and camera linking host-owned (canOverlay gates the blend slider); the modal wrapper, Escape-unwinds-one-layer policy, and fullscreen promotion (kit emits data-fullscreen + onStageShapeChange; no timers in the kit).

Draft bar: all props in DraftBarProps supplied by the host; the entire Compare/Merge/Rebase orchestration (~130 donor lines building CompareExplicitSource + CompareAction) is host code; status-line expiry is host's; changeCount and canMerge stay two separate props.

Status strip: item list with active flags + onSelect + badge/indicator values (e.g. diagnostics count, preview dot); the zoom readout as children (there is no portable zoom implementation — DefaultZoomMenu is tldraw's); panel-open bookkeeping (aria-expanded derives from the active prop).

Theme: kit styles against trunk Tailwind tokens; the 13 --systemsketch-pill-* names survive as optional --bbox-pill-* overrides scoped at the HOST ROOT (popovers portal out of the pill's subtree — app-root scoping documented); accent-on-soft copy is ink, never accent text (measured 2.6-4.3:1).
testIdPrefix?: string everywhere (default 'bbox') — no test id derived from display text, so renaming visible copy cannot break a consumer's tests.

buildOrder.lane: N — registry publish (BARRIER: orchestrator-owned, last, alone)
buildOrder.rationale: registry.json is a shared resource with one owner. Sibling rule applied (components/bbox/*, lib/utils.ts -> components/lib/utils.ts); then throwaway-install + tsc — the check that caught TS2307 when the build exited 0.

omitted: VS Code-style command registry (CommandDef/MenuItemDef, when/group@order, resolveMenu) — in a copy-paste kit the consumer owns the JSX file, so contribute-without-editing has no customer yet; reversible ~150-line add on the same compound parts (plus the unquoted-when-literal unit check) when a plugin-shaped host appears.

Measured overflow toolbar (tldraw OverflowingToolbar: children rendered twice, ResizeObserver + MutationObserver that broke twice upstream) — self-measurement is banned anyway; ship wrapping bars, revisit when a real surface overflows.

CustomColorPicker — a separate port project (history stopping points, undo keybindings, retire-as-you-drag registration); controlPanel exposes customColorSlot so it lands later without touching the panel.

Rich-text toolbar component — none exists in SystemSketch (55 lines of CSS over tldraw's own toolbar, deliberately); building one is a product decision, noted not built; ControlStrip could be re-aimed at rich-text commands later.
Menubar wrapper — no screenshot surface is a horizontal menubar (the burger is a DropdownMenu); shadcn's menubar-from-copied-dropdown recipe makes it a cheap later add.

FigJam palette, FigJam traced icons, and vendored Excalidraw icons as kit data — palettes/vocabularies are injected by design; the traced assets carry unresolved provenance and are SystemSketch product taste; stories use a small demo palette.

draftModel.ts state reducers — pure and tested but they are SystemSketch's localStorage branching bookkeeping; the kit ships only the DraftSummary prop shape (a git-backed host would never use the model).

All persistence (toolbar preferences, density, pill presentation) — controlled props only; storage is a documented host-adapter recipe carrying 'Preferences are helpful feedback, never a reason to block drawing'.
Modal/dialog wrapper for Compare and every position:fixed / z-index — host-owned by the trunk's law; compareReview is headless.
Virtualization in Problems/Frames lists — 175 plain rows today; add a windowing slot only when a real board hurts.
chromeState reducer as a kit export — offered as a documented 60-line host recipe instead (LRU Escape order and the inspector exemption are host chrome policy).
cmdk command palette — future surface; composes inside a kit Popover when wanted.
compareSource.ts — superseded in the donor; confirmed not ported.
PillPresentationChip / PrototypeSwitch as components — lab affordances; only the 13 pill token NAMES survive as the --bbox-pill-* theming contract.

openDecisions.question: Open vs closed control-kind union — SystemSketch's closed 16-member union makes Record exhaustive and the resolver total, but the 16 names are its shape-drawing concepts.
openDecisions.recommendation: Generic createControlRegistry<K extends string>: the app closes the union, the kit stays open; exhaustiveness survives where the app wants it.
openDecisions.reversibleDefault: Ship the generic factory — an app can pin K later at zero cost.

openDecisions.question: Does the object-diff engine (compareModel.ts) ship in the kit, or only the compare VIEW typed on BoardCompare?
openDecisions.recommendation: Ship it — it is pure over structural RecordLike, its fixture tests are the spec, and a host with a different graph model simply doesn't import it; recordsOfSnapshot stays in the tldraw adapter.
openDecisions.reversibleDefault: Ship; deleting an unused pure module later is trivial.

openDecisions.question: Does 'mixed' (three-state ControlValue) belong in a general editor kit, or is it a canvas-multi-selection concept?
openDecisions.recommendation: Keep it — mixed-state folding is the essence of multi-selection property editing and the whole pill assumes it; single-subject hosts just never pass mixed.

openDecisions.question: Which pill recipes travel (V1 compact, V3 segmented, default)?
openDecisions.recommendation: None as kit exports — recipes are app data; stories carry demo recipes with V3-segmented as the default story (it is the shipped default) and V1-compact as a lab variant, restructure precondition stated beside it.

openDecisions.question: Problems 'info' severity — promote to a full citizen (chip + filter) or keep SystemSketch's counted-but-unsurfaced asymmetry?
openDecisions.recommendation: Severities become config rows; the demo config mirrors SystemSketch exactly so the port changes nothing visibly, and promotion becomes a host config edit.

openDecisions.question: Problems group header — render the group's own label, or keep the hardcoded 'Board'?
openDecisions.recommendation: Render from data (also fixes the raw 'EXPANDED-BLOCK' caption via the Frames kinds map); SystemSketch's adapter can pass 'Board' for parity.

openDecisions.question: composeControls silent drop — it enables optional slots but caused the lost-lineShape bug twice.
openDecisions.recommendation: Keep the drop (load-bearing) and add onDangling firing a dev-mode console.warn — the lab's labDangling proved it is computable.
openDecisions.reversibleDefault: Warn in dev, silent in prod.

openDecisions.question: Frames thumbnail aspect depends on the current window size (donor getFramesPanelPreviews quirk) — intended or latent bug?
openDecisions.recommendation: The kit takes preview as data so the question stays host-side; flag for Zach in the SystemSketch adapter notes rather than freezing either answer into the core.
openDecisions.reversibleDefault: Preserve current behaviour in the SystemSketch adapter.
